News.title: Biker, 28, dies in crash with tractor as family pay tribute to ‘gentle loving son’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

'DEEPLY LOVED' Biker, 28, dies in crash with tractor as family pay tribute to ‘gentle loving son’







Next

A BIKER has died in a horror crash with a tractor, as family pay a touching tribute to their “gentle, loving son”.

Kieran James Lerwill, from Bishops Nympton, died following a two-vehicle collision on the B3227 at Nadder Lane, near South Molton, North Devon.

Cops were called at around 4.55pm on October 4 to the collision involving Kieran’s blue BMW S1000 motorbike and a green John Deere tractor.



Kieran’s family have now paid a touching tribute to him.



They said: “Kieran was a gentle loving son, grandson, brother, uncle, partner and friend.

“He is deeply loved and his loss has left a hole in our hearts that can never be filled.

“Words cannot express the sadness and despair we are feeling.



“We ask that our family’s privacy and space to grieve be respected at this incredibly difficult time.”

Specialist and local officers attended the scene and conducted an initial investigation and the road was closed for several hours.

Anyone who witnessed the incident or has any information or dashcam footage is asked to contact the Devon & Cornwall Police via their website here or by calling 101 quoting 517 of 4/10/26.

News.title: Ann Widdecombe would still be alive today if police properly probed firebomb attack on my home, blasts Nigel Farage
News.content:
Next

NIGEL Farage has said Ann Widdecombe “would still be alive” today if police had properly investigated an attack on his home the year before her murder.

The Reform UK boss also claimed Government ministers would “rather I be dead” than give him the security he needs.



Former Tory minister turned Strictly star Ms Widdecombe, 78, was found bludgeoned to death at her home in Devon in July.

Joshua Kerry, 28, has been charged with her murder.



Since being in custody Kerry has also been charged with trying to firebomb Mr Farage’s home in April 2025 — more than a year before Ms Widdecombe was killed.

Mr Farage told The Sun on Sunday: “I’m sorry to say, had the police done their job with me I think Ann would still be alive.



“Why do you think counter- terrorism police have referred themselves to the IOPC (Independent Office for Police Conduct) for the first time in history?

“The bloke given the CCTV didn’t look at it. Why not? Because it’s me. Who gives a f**k about me?”

Mr Farage slammed ministers for failing to give him security despite his pleas for protection.

He said: “I’ve had this now for years. These threats have been constant since 2013. I’m the most physically attacked and verbally attacked person of modern times.



“But these have always been belittled. It’s appalling.

“I’ve had to live surrounded by security now for well over a decade. There’s no way around it.

“The Government has consistently refused to provide me with security.”



Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood is expected to address Parliament tomorrow about the security of politicians in the wake of Kerry’s most recent charge.

But asked if he thought the Government would change its mind and give him security now, Mr Farage replied: “I think they would rather I be dead.”

Mr Farage, 62, who has three children and four grandchildren, said he worried more for his family than for himself.

He is currently under investigation by Parliament’s standards watchdog over a £5million donation he received from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne.

Mr Farage has said the money is for his personal security and did not need to be declared as it was donated before he became an MP.



Defending his acceptance of the cash, the party boss said he expects to have threats made against him for the rest of his life.

“You are never safe — even when you’re retired,” he said, grimly.

And he added that he would tell anyone with children today not to bother going into politics because of the risks.

His astonishingly frank words are the first time he has spoken since Ms Widdecombe’s murder and the attack on his home 14 months before were linked.



Mr Farage spoke out as The Sun on Sunday joined him on the campaign trail in Accrington, Lancs, on Thursday.

He is convinced that PM Andy Burnham will call an early election next May and has put Reform on an “emergency” footing to prepare.

“We are working round the clock”, Mr Farage tells me, flashing his signature massive grin.

He argues that Mr Burnham is now trapped between left-wing Labour MPs who will not let him make spending cuts on the one hand and a “worsening economic climate” on the other.



Mr Farage predicts: “He’ll look at it and say: ‘This is going to get worse.’ And he will call a vote.”

As we talk, Mr Farage, is clutching a bag containing the applications of 200 would-be Reform candidates.

He has already kicked off a national tour of Reform target areas.

Last week was Doncaster. Today it is Accrington.

Walking down the high street, locals dash over to take photos with Mr Farage and shake his hand. Others stand outside shops filming.



One woman who stops for a selfie tells Mr Farage she fears for Britain’s future and this is “our last chance” to change.

A man in his 80s has a go at the revolving door of Tory and Labour governments who don’t seem to bother about areas like his.

He tells Mr Farage: “We have been sold down the river. It’s as simple as that.”

A few others are not so welcoming. One man loudly accuses Mr Farage of doing “the devil’s work”.

But on the whole these voters love him. We are in the heart of the Red Wall, and these are his people.



“The Tories have given up on the Red Wall”, Mr Farage says gleefully.

“They lost a lot of seats last time. Now they are not even in the game.”

The day before we meet, Tory leader Kemi Badenoch used her conference speech to launch a blistering attack on Reform — and rule out an electoral deal with the party.

She slammed Reform MP Suella Braverman for questioning whether non-white people can be English.

In what was her most savage attack on Reform, Mrs Badenoch said she does not want to live in a country led by people “who debate whether my mixed-race children are English”.



But Mr Farage hit back at the Tory leader — accusing her of trying to paint Reform as racist because they are an electoral threat.

“It’s the oldest trick in the book, isn’t it?”, he said. “They are very scared of us.”

Asked if he agrees with Ms Braverman’s comments, he said she was speaking “personally” and it is not for him to tell her if she should feel English or not.



He branded Mrs Badenoch and her team a “Thatcher tribute act” who are stuck in the 1980s — just as Andy Burnham is stuck in the 1970s.

So what does Mr Farage think of his main rival — Mr Burnham?

He concedes that the new PM is more charismatic than Sir Keir Starmer, but claims he is hamstrung by his own nostalgia for a bygone era that never really existed.

Bestowing a new nickname on the PM, Mr Farage declared: “He is out-of-date Andy”.

Asked what will happen if Mr Burnham tries to overturn the EU referendum result, Mr Farage said: “I’ll win the election.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The next election is shaping up to be a battle royale — with Reform and the Tories scrapping it out to be Labour’s main opponent.

With chatter of an early election growing ever louder, we may not have to wait long to find out.

News.title: Trump calls for Zelensky to be replaced as he ‘wants to make problems for the world’ amid row over Putin diesel deal
News.content:
Next

DONALD Trump has said “it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president” as he slammed Volodymyr Zelensky for strikes on Russian oil refineries.

The US president claimed Zelensky wants “to make problems for the world” by blasting Vladimir Putin‘s petrol producers and said the Ukrainian president should be replaced.



It comes after Trump struck a huge diesel deal with Mad Vlad on Friday to allow Russian oil to be sold to the US and the world.

The US president claimed on Saturday that Zelensky “better damn well stop” his blitzes on Russian refineries.



The attacks have caused petrol shortages in Russia and brought the cost of war home to Putin’s population.

Sale of sanctioned oil is a significant source of funding for the Russian tyrant’s bloodthirsty war on Ukraine.

But Trump said on Saturday that Ukraine should “get a new leader who can make a deal” and told Zelensky to stop striking Russian oil.

The US president added: “We said, ‘you can do whatever you want to Russia, don’t hit the refineries’, because that’s a world problem that’s caused.”

“He could have made many deals and for some reason, he never does.”

It comes after a Russian glide bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia killed 20 people, including three children, in the early hours of Saturday.



And terrifying footage emerged showing a man miraculously escaping death by seconds as a Russian drone strike decimated a playground.

Zelensky wrote on X: “Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia.”

Trump announced his deal with Putin on Friday to try and bring down petrol prices after the cost of fuel spiked during his war on Iran.



The Ukrainian president was left fuming by the talks, saying the bombshell agreement “looks like a happy birthday present for Putin”.

Speaking to Axios, he added that Trump was “not fair and not honest”, believing the decision will bring further “terror” to his country.

In a post to his Truth Social on Friday evening, Trump announced that 3 million tonnes of diesel would be delivered to the US and world in a “short period of time”.

He said Russia would immediately supply 300,000 tonnes with another 500,000 tonnes during November.

Zelensky fumed: “Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilised world.



“Russia will ‘repay’ the diesel with further terror and perfidy.”

He went on to say the Kremlin earning money from selling the diesel would only prolong the war against his country.

Putin said in a statement that he was ready to supply oil to the US and global markets, believing it will help the global economy.

The ageing tyrant also said the two leaders discussed stopping the wars in Ukraine and Iran.

Trump announced the agreement following a phone call with the dictator and touted it as bringing lower prices for Americans.



He said: “Between our TOTAL CONTROL of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority.”

The UK, however, will “maintain pressure on Russia” through tough sanctions, Downing Street has said.

News.title: Andy Carroll’s sex abuser branded a ‘monster’ by his own daughter as she reveals he never even told her he’d been jailed
News.content:
Next

ANDY Carroll’s abuser has been branded a “monster” by his own daughter, who says he never even told her he’d been jailed.

Celebrity dance teacher Kevin Adams, 59, got 20 months’ prison for sexually assaulting the former England striker in 2021.



But his two daughters and their mum were in the dark about his 2023 conviction until weeks ago.

His youngest daughter Avia, 21, has branded her father a “sick individual” and praised Carroll, 37, for talking about the attack.



She said “I feel really bad for him. I just think my dad is a monster.”

Asked if Carroll had been brave to talk, she said: “100 per cent.”



Avia added: “As far as naming him — he’s done something terrible to you so name him. If I was in that position I’d do the same.”

Avia also said she’d say “sorry” to Carroll if they met. Wiping away tears, she added: “Obviously, I know it’s not my fault but it’s just like, that’s my dad. It’s just disgusting. And I’m sorry that that’s happened to him.”



Avia says Adams carried on enjoying his celebrity lifestyle while keeping his crime secret.

She said his mother, sister and cousins knew about the case.

But Avia and her sister had little contact with him after his marriage to their mother broke down in 2011.

Avia, who works in beauty and hospitality, also revealed Adams kept his real age secret from his family for years. She thought he was in his 40s and said: “I only found out two weeks ago.”

She has not heard from him since the revelations — and plans to change her surname to cut ties.



Avia grew up in Essex surrounded by the trappings of her dad’s success.

Adams was a talented dancer and choreographer who worked with the likes of Sir Elton John, Mariah Carey and the Spice Girls.

He appeared on BBC show Fame Academy from 2002-3, and worked on productions linked to Comic Relief and Disney High School Musical.

He also ran his own performing arts academy.

Avia still remembers enjoying some of the perks of having a famous father: “I got to do things which my friends thought were cool, like go to premieres and shows.”



Adams married Avia’s mother in September 2005, six months after Avia was born.

Their eldest daughter had arrived in 2003.

Her parents were friends with reality TV stars Jade Goody and Jeff Brazier, and the families shared a house when Avia was a toddler.



She fondly remembers holidays with Jeff and his sons Bobby and Freddie Brazier.

Avia’s parents split when she was about six.

Adams lived in Loughton and became a familiar face at celebrity haunt Sheesh in Chigwell where he taught dance and mixed with footballers and stars.

Teenaged Avia and her sister spent weekends at their dad’s, where a male showbiz pal had become a regular visitor.

In one upsetting incident, she claims the two men performed cartwheels in the garden while wearing nothing under their dressing gowns.



She recalled: “I just remember them laughing.”

Adams also taught fitness classes at a hot yoga studio owned by former Towie star Billi Mucklow, who later married Carroll.

Avia recalled spending time at the studio with Billi, although she never met the footballer.

Avia says she remembers her last phone conversation with her dad weeks before his trial. They discussed relationships but Adams gave no hint of his court case.

He was convicted at Chelmsford crown court in September 2023 and jailed for 20 months in November.



Avia lost contact and noticed that his social media accounts had fallen silent.

But she assumed he had decided to retreat from the limelight.

It was only last month that she learned the truth.

Carroll revealed in his autobiography, Owning It, how he had been sexually assaulted by a male celebrity, without naming Adams.

The striker, now at Dagenham & Redbridge, had woken to being assaulted under his dvuet.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Last week The Sun on Sunday named Adams after the footballer confirmed his identity when made aware it was in publicly available court documents.

Avia added: “Me and my sister said to each other, we knew something like this was going to come out. And then I was sad. then angry, then yeah, a mix between every emotion possible.”

News.title: Boy, 5, rushed to hospital with serious injuries after being hit by car
News.content:
ROAD HORROR Boy, 5, rushed to hospital with serious injuries after being hit by car







Next

A FIVE-year-old boy has been rushed to hospital after he was hit by a car and suffered serious injuries.

The accident happened at around 5.42pm on October 8 on Red Holt Drive in Keighley, West Yorkshire.

A black Mercedes Vito was involved.



The child was taken to hospital, where he was found to have suffered serious injuries.



Cops spoke to the driver of the vehicle.

An investigation has been launched by West Yorkshire Police’s Roads Policing Unit who have appealed for witnesses to come forward.

A spokesperson for West Yorkshire Police said: “Our Roads Policing Unit is investigating this incident and is appealing to anyone who witnessed the collision to contact them, either by calling 101 or using our LiveChat facility on the website.



“Anyone with footage that may assist this investigation is also asked to make contact, quoting log 1181 of 8 October.”

News.title: Prisoners given classes in yoga and cell mindfulness paid for by taxpayers
News.content:
LONG STRETCH Prisoners given classes in yoga and cell mindfulness paid for by taxpayers

Credit: Getty







Next

PRISONERS have been given classes in colouring, yoga and in “cell mindfulness” worth over £300,000, The Sun on Sunday can reveal.

Critics said it was outrageous that taxpayers cash is being lavished on the lessons while prisons are infested with drugs and rats.



At HMP Rochester in Kent, inmates were given “calming and mindful” lessons in creative writing, scrapbooking, and scrabble.

The contract, worth over £35,000 and awarded in June 2025, was intended to build “confidence, resilience, teamwork, patience, and communication”.



Rochester was placed under an urgent notification in September 2024 after inspectors found that 42 per cent of prisoners tested positive in random drug tests.

They also discovered that assaults had risen by 67 per cent in a year, rats and mice were ‘plaguing older buildings’ and inmates were stuffing cardboard under their cell doors to keep the vermin out.

Tory shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy said: “When HMP Rochester has rats in its cells, drugs circulating freely and uncontrolled violence, it’s shocking that Labour are wasting money on ‘mindfulness’ exercises and yoga for prisoners.

“Labour are spending taxpayers’ money on wasteful, questionable contracts for colouring in classes and songwriting courses when they should be cracking down on drugs and crime in our prisons. This is absurd.”

He said the Tories would build 50,000 new prison places.

The Ministry of Justice has gone on a spending spree of other woke classes at prisons. It includes £10,680 on yoga and in cell mindfulness at HMP Maidstone.



HMP Belmarsh has a £46,350 contract for music and fashion classes, £12,370 on painting and drawing classes.

Across seven prisons £312,793.05 was spent on the classes.

A Prison Service spokesman said: “We inherited a prison system on the brink of collapse.

“We are pulling every lever to restore order by building 14,000 extra spaces and investing £75 million to clamp down on violence, criminality and drugs.”

A Labour source said: “The Tories talk a big game on prisons to distract from their woeful record.



“Their 14 years in office saw just 500 places added to the estate and 23 prisons closed, while drugs ran rife.”

News.title: Three injured after ‘student goes on stabbing spree’ in THIRD knife attack at a school in less than a week in Poland
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SCHOOL 'STABBING' Three injured after ‘student goes on stabbing spree’ in THIRD knife attack at a school in less than a week in Poland







Next

THREE people have been injured after a horror stabbing spree at a further education college in Warsaw on Saturday, police said.

It’s the third knife attack at a school in Poland this week alone, sparking fears of copycat violence.



It comes after a 37-year-old woman died after a teenage boy allegedly stormed a primary school and stabbed three members of staff in in Leszczydół-Nowiny on Thursday.

Just hours earlier, ten people were wounded in a separate stabbing at a school in Ostrołęka on Wednesday.



On Friday thousands of police visited schools nationwide to try to reassure pupils after the spate of stabbings.

But cops confirmed the third knife attack on Saturday afternoon.



Police said the suspected attacker was a 21-year-old female student at the school.

She used a “dangerous object” to launch the attack at around midday on Saturday, cops said.

Her victims were reportedly two teenage girls, both 17, and a 24-year-old woman who were there to hand in documents to enrol at the college.

One person was rushed to hospital after the stabbing spree.



The other two victims were treated at the scene.

They did not know their attacker, Poland’s state news agency reported, as fears grew of seemingly random violence in the Eastern European country.

She was arrested at the scene.



Police spokesperson Jakub Filipiak said: “At 12:30 today, we received a report of an incident involving the use of a dangerous weapon.”

“One person was injured and transported to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

“Two other bystanders also sustained injuries but did not require hospitalisation.”

Fears of growing youth violence grew to fever pitch this week, with 59 schools cancelling classes on Friday.

There were even warnings that the end of this week could see a “bloody Friday” with rumours of coordinated attacks.



Schools which stayed open have ramped up security.

In Thursday’s attack, a 15-year-old armed with three knives allegedly attacked a 37-year-old caretaker, the headteacher and a teacher.

Despite desperate resuscitation attempts by paramedics, the caretaker died at the scene, authorities confirmed.

The attacker, reportedly a student at the school, was arrested at the scene.

After Wednesday’s attack, two of ten people who were wounded were left in serious condition.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Police arrested a 19-year-old former student near the city beach.

And in a separate incident on Wednesday police detained a 17-year-old who was plotting “something dangerous” on school grounds, Interior minister Marcin Kierwinski said.

News.title: ‘Dozens wounded’ in huge blast at major airport just days after Iran’s Houthi rebels blitz on passenger plane kills 3
News.content:
AIRPORT BLAST ‘Dozens wounded’ in huge blast at major airport just days after Iran’s Houthi rebels blitz on passenger plane kills 3







Next

DOZENS of people have been wounded in a huge blast at the airport in Saudi Arabia’s capital just days after it was blasted by Iran-backed Houthi rebels.

Officials said King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh was attacked again by the terror group again on Saturday, triggering an urgent evacuation at the international travel hub.



Donald Trump told reporters on Saturday he is considering if should join Saudi strikes on the Houthis, warning: “We move very quickly.”

Asked if he would attack the Iranian proxy, the US president said: “We may. We’re going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack. So we’ll make a decision.”





Today’s attack saw a missile smash into terminals three and four at King Khalid International Airport, which are used for domestic flights.

And health officials activated a rare mass call-up of doctors to deal with the “serious emergency”, according to a medical source.

The source said many of the injured were in critical condition, adding: “We were told we are dealing with a ‘serious emergency situation’.

“Injured are being moved to hospitals across Riyadh.”



Anonymous officials revealed the attack as ambulances were seen rushing to the airport.

A source at a local hospital said dozens had been injured and five people were in intensive care.

The blitz was then confirmed by Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation, GACA, who said the travel hub was “targeted by an attack, amid continued attacks targeting civil aviation facilities in the Kingdom”.

GACA confirmed all operations were suspended at King Khalid International Airport, after sending out an alert telling passengers to check their flight status before travelling to the area.

Riyadh residents reported hearing two huge explosions that rocked the capital during today’s attack.



Earlier, one official said all air traffic to the King Khalid International Airport had stopped.

And flight tracking services showed planes diverting to other airports in the region.

The British embassy in Riyadh warned UK nationals to avoid King Khalid International Airport, reporting a “serious incident” there.

Canada’s embassy warned of “ongoing military activity” at the airport.

It’s not yet known if anyone was killed by today’s blitz.



At least 225 flights at the airport were cancelled in the past 24 hours, according to flight-tracking site FlightAware.

The Houthis have not yet given a statement about the attack.

It comes just two days after three Saudi citizens including a pilot were killed when Riyadh’s international airport was blitzed by Houthi rebels.

The Iran-backed terror group launched a deadly missile barrage on Riyadh’s main airport on Thursday, in its latest escalation of attacks against Saudi Arabia.

Terrifying footage showed a Saudi passenger jet ablaze as firefighters battled a huge blaze.



Three Saudi citizens were killed on Thursday, including a pilot with the national airline, and several others were wounded in the blitz, Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation said.

An initial swarm of missiles targeted airport facilities before a second struck the aircraft, authorities added.

It did not identify those responsible, but the Houthis claimed the attack, saying their soldiers targeted the airport with a ballistic missile.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Brig Gen Yahya Saree, a Yemeni military spokesman aligned with the Houthis, said forces also struck Najran airport and the Khamis Mushait air base.

But Saudi Arabia said air defences intercepted and destroyed two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh and one heading for Khamis Mushait.

News.title: Man dies after tiger attack at wildlife park
News.content:
A man has died after being attacked by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, police have confirmed.

South Yorkshire Police said it had been called at 13:35 BST to reports of a man entering the tiger enclosure at the attraction near Doncaster. The tiger then attacked the man and he died at the scene, the force said.

His family had been informed and were being supported by officers, it added.

A park spokesperson said: "We are deeply saddened by today's tragic incident. Our thoughts and heartfelt sympathies are with the family and loved ones of the person who has lost their life."

They added: "We are working closely with the police and relevant authorities and would ask that the privacy of those affected is respected at this extremely difficult time. The park will remain closed tomorrow."

Police said the tiger was uninjured, remained in the enclosure following the incident and there had been no wider risk to the public.

The park was evacuated and officers remain at the scene.

The force added: "We are aware of videos circulating online and we would encourage people not to share this footage."

Earlier, in a statement posted on its website, the park said its emergency response procedures had been "immediately activated" and it was "working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened".

News.title: Sara Sharif's grandfather granted guardianship of her siblings in Pakistan
News.content:
Sara Sharif's paternal grandfather has been granted guardianship of her siblings by a court in Pakistan.

The decision comes after years of legal limbo following the murder of 10-year-old Sara by her father and stepmother in 2023.

All five children, who are now aged between 16 and four, have been living in Pakistan since 2023. They were asked to speak to the judge in court, where the eldest said they were comfortable and the siblings were settled.

Sara's grandfather, Muhammed Sharif, told the BBC he was relieved to be granted guardianship after three years of legal battles, saying his hope is that the children "stay healthy" and receive "a good education".

"It is my responsibility to ensure they get the best possible education and care," he said.

When told by the judge that the grandfather would become their guardian, the eldest child responded saying "that's all good".

The five children have been in Pakistan since August 2023, when they were brought to the country by Sara's father, stepmother and uncle after Sara was killed.

The family was in hiding for weeks before the children were discovered by police at the grandfather's house. They were initially put into state childcare.

The adults flew back to the UK and were arrested at the airport. Sara's father Urfan Sharif and stepmother Beinash Batool were found guilty of Sara's murder. Sharif was sentenced to a minimum of 40 years in prison and Batool received a minimum of 33 years.

Her uncle, Faisal Malik, was found guilty of causing or allowing her death and given a 16-year sentence.

Sara had been hooded, burned and beaten during a "campaign of torture" that lasted two years before her body was found at the family home in Woking, Surrey.

News.title: King warns malicious online actors are evolving tactics
News.content:
King Charles III has warned of the challenges disinformation and other "hostile online activity" pose to trust and security in the digital age.

The comments, made in a letter to the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) to mark its 10th anniversary, spoke of "malicious actors" continuing to "evolve their tactics by using automated technologies".

"From threats to our international order, to the need to balance the risks and opportunities of powerful new technologies, strong cyber security is fundamental to making the online environment safer and more resilient," he wrote.

Last month, the King warned AI executives of the "existential dangers" posed by the technology falling into the wrong hands.

In the letter published on Saturday by NCSC, the King praised the government agency. He said its achievements over the past decade have included defending the country against cyber attacks, safeguarding democratic institutions and protecting "the critical infrastructure upon which daily life depends".

"You have built resilience across our public services, businesses and communities, equipping us all to prosper in our ever-evolving digital world," the monarch added.

The King said he was "acutely aware" that much of the work done by the NCSC cannot be praised publicly and that he was filled with "profound gratitude".

The NCSC was established in 2016 as part of the Government Communications Headquarters to protect the UK against cyber threats.

Earlier this week, the NCSC offered assistance to online shopping store Asos after customers received a notification from its app sent by hackers, the BBC understands.

The high profile hack made global headlines on Tuesday when cyber criminals used Asos's own app system to send a pop up notification to potentially millions of people.

Asos said it was investigating "unauthorised activity" involving third-party platforms. The company told its customers that hackers are in possession of detailed profiles of potentially millions of the company's users - including names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, customer numbers and dates of birth.

It issued the update after BBC News told the retailer it had been contacted by cyber criminals who said this week's breach went beyond the "basic contact details" Asos previously said might have been accessed.

The letter from the King to NCSC came after he spoke to AI executives at Dumfries House in Ayrshire last month on how the tech can be used to benefit security.

News.title: Ashe was too scared to cancel her wedding, then her story became a hit song
News.content:
No songwriter is ever off duty. And for the US pop singer Ashe, that included her wedding day.

Last October, she was getting ready to tie the knot at a gorgeous hilltop ceremony in Nashville when inspiration struck.

As she watched her family gather, the musician flashed back to her first wedding, almost a decade earlier. The contrast was stark.

She's called that first marriage "horrifying". Her ex, who she met in college, was, she says, emotionally manipulative and psychologically abusive.

He had insisted on a beachfront wedding, which sounds romantic until you learn that Ashe has a fear of the ocean.

In the run-up, she had been tempted to call it off, but felt powerless to stand up for herself.

On her second wedding day, she realised the opposite was true.

"I'm in a happy, healthy relationship and I have total autonomy over my own life," says the singer, now in her early 30s.

"I thought, if this didn't feel right, I could totally put a halt to the whole thing. I definitely didn't have that first time around."

As she adjusted her veil and prepared to walk down the aisle, she filed that feeling away.

Two months later, and back at work, the idea resurfaced and a song spilled out.

Its name? Stop the Wedding.

It unfolds like a movie scene. Ashe pleads with her younger self to trust her instincts.

"You know how you really feel / You don't have to waste your life," she sings, as the wedding band stutters to an uncertain halt.

"Do I wish I'd had that advice at the time? 1,000 per cent," Ashe says.

"If someone had given me the insight that I was not stuck, and that I could run, I could have changed things sooner. Maybe not at the altar. Maybe weeks before â but it was something I really could have used."

What about the line where she pledges to "burn the wedding dress and run away"?

"I didn't burn my dress," she laughs, "but I did get into a bathtub with it for a photoshoot right after I left my ex-husband, which really ruined it!"

News.title: I couldn't access my family's medical history - not knowing was terrifying
News.content:
When Aaliyah found a lump in her breast, she was anxious to find out if she had inherited an increased risk of cancer.

But because she had been removed from her biological parents at the age of seven months and later adopted, she had no way of accessing her family medical history.

"Not knowing anything about yourself genetically is terrifying," says the 26-year-old, "you can't even begin to imagine it."

The lump turned out to be non-cancerous, but it was one of many occasions when she found herself unable to answer questions about her biological family's health.

Aaliyah, now a trainee solicitor, spent years trying to source information from local authorities and eventually made an official data access request to Bradford Council, which removed her from her biological family as a baby.

She says the whole process took its toll.

"I would say bureaucratic hellscape is an understatement," she admits.

News.title: Public executions in the US stopped nearly a century ago, why are they resuming now?
News.content:
They came in their thousands from near and far. Men, women and children lined up on a Kentucky riverfront for the public hanging of a black man convicted of raping and killing an elderly white widow.

It was 14 August 1936 in Owensboro, Kentucky, a sweltering Friday in the middle of a legendary heatwave. Some slept overnight near the gallows to preserve their spots. Others held "necktie" parties the previous evening, arriving hungover as teenagers sold popcorn and soda to spectators.

By the execution time of 05:00, the crowd had swelled to an estimated 20,000.

That's when Rainey Bethea, an orphan in his 20s, stepped up to the gallows - sentenced to death after allegedly confessing to robbing, raping and killing Lischia Edwards, 70.

The previous afternoon, he'd eaten a last meal of fried chicken, pork chops, mashed potatoes, pickled cucumbers, cornbread, lemon pie and ice cream.

Many of those gathered - including press from as far away as Chicago and New York - came to see the rumoured "Lady Executioner". The local sheriff had died four months earlier and his widow had become his unlikely replacement.

She declined to pull the trip lever herself, however, and it was a hired hangmen who instead sent Bethea to his death.

That moment marked the last high-profile public hanging in the US. The circus surrounding Bethea's death embarrassed many in Kentucky and the governor outlawed public executions 18 months later.

By then, most states had abolished capital punishment in view of the masses as societal attitudes sought more humane and private methods. Another hanging was attended by a few hundred in Missouri in 1937, but that was lesser known and marked America's final public execution - until now.

News.title: Afrobeats singer Ayra Starr on making history at her NFL half-time show in London
News.content:
Afrobeats singer Ayra Starr has already broken numerous records, and her NFL half-time performance this weekend is set to level up her list again.

The Nigerian star will become the first African artist to headline one of the American football league's international games when the Philadelphia Eagles take on the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday.

Ahead of the performance at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Starr told BBC Newsbeat her history-making performance "itself is a message".

Earlier this year, Puerto Rican superstar Bad Bunny used his Super Bowl half-time show to celebrate Latin American culture.

The 32-year-old also made history by becoming the first musician to perform entirely in Spanish at the sporting event, normally the most-watched each year on US TV.

Starr said it's "very important" for singers to seize opportunities like this.

"At the end of the day, as artists, we speak for the culture and we speak for the people that listen to us," she added.

"And we have to represent any way that seems fit, that they need."

She didn't want to give away too much about her performance, but confirmed it would feature tracks from her new studio album, Starrgirl, which was released in August.

"Sunday is gonna be amazing," she said.

"I'm still in rehearsals. It's a lot of work we're putting in so I'm really excited."

News.title: Boots has a new owner: Three ways it could affect you
News.content:
Upgrading its portfolio of 1,800 stores is high on the list of Boots' new owners, Wittington Investments. This is the holding company of the Westons - a wealthy and retail-steeped Canadian family who used to own Selfridges and currently own several large retailers across the Atlantic.

The UK branch of the family also controls the owner of Primark, Associated British Foods (ABF).

What Boots stores might look like in the future has not been disclosed.

Business has been good for Boots in recent years, and new-look beauty areas in some of its bigger shops have given shoppers more of a department store experience, according to Sofie Willmott, an associate director and analyst at GlobalData Retail.

Since the opening of its first beauty-only store in 2023 in the Battersea Power Station development, it says it has redesigned over 180 beauty halls, while also opening its first fragrance concept store and an Opticians dedicated to luxury eyewear.

"They should invest in the rest of the chain because they've got such a big store portfolio that I think some of the smaller stores have really lacked investment over time, and I think that is something that they need to kind of catch up with," Willmott says.

A more "consistent" look would also be an improvement, Willmott adds. "At the moment there is a bit of a disconnect."

Jackie Naghten, a retail industry veteran who has worked for the likes of Top Shop, Marks & Spencer and Debenhams, thinks Boots' stores need to be made "more functional" by not having their health hubs "squeezed in the corner".

But Yasmin Trimble, 22, who buys beauty products from Boots, likes how easy the stores are to navigate.

"You can get everything you need...it is not confusing. It has got a cleaner aesthetic to it as well."

News.title: Head of Met's volunteer force fired after AI tool found deleted intimate images on work phone
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police has fired the head of its Special Constabulary after Palantir's AI monitoring uncovered that he had used his work phone to copy intimate images of a woman.

Special chief officer James Deller, who led the force's volunteer officers, was dismissed following a misconduct hearing on Friday.

The Met said investigators used lawful business monitoring and Palantir's Foundry system, which uses artificial intelligence (AI), to find the misconduct by Deller.

Cdr Pete Stevens said: "SCO Deller failed to meet that bar. His actions were an abuse of the trust put in him and it is right that he is no longer able to serve in policing."

Investigators found that in July and August 2025, Deller used his police-issued phone to take photos of two intimate images that had been sent to his personal phone.

The pictures had been sent using WhatsApp's "view once" feature, which makes them disappear after they are opened.

He then sent the copied images back to his personal device before deleting them from his work phone.

The misconduct was discovered during a week-long operation called Project Galatasaray, which used the AI technology in a bid to identify corruption and professional misconduct within the Met.

Deller will be added to the College of Policing's barred list, meaning he will not be able to serve in policing again.

Stevens added: "The vast majority of Met officers and staff serve London with dedication and integrity, and they rightly expect robust action against the small minority who abuse their position and undermine public trust.

"That is particularly true of those who serve in the Special Constabulary. They are volunteers who selflessly give up their time to keep London safe.

"They deserve to be led by people who demonstrate the highest standards in all parts of their lives."

News.title: Green Party MP wants to make sure it is 'not vulnerable to extremists'
News.content:
A Green Party MP has said her party needs to make sure it is not "vulnerable to capture by extremists and racists" after members voted for a motion that claimed Zionism was racism.

The motion put forward by activists, which became formal policy after it was approved at the Green's conference earlier this month, has divided senior party figures and been criticised by Jewish groups.

Westminster leader Ellie Chowns told the BBC it was a "significant and damaging policy" and she would work to reform the Green Party.

It comes after ex-leader Caroline Lucas said it was not being protected from entryism - where people sign up to a party to try to change it.

Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today Programme on Saturday, Chowns said: "I don't know if there are extremists and racists in my party. But I want to make sure that my party isn't vulnerable to capture by extremists and racists."

The MP described Zionism as a "contested concept" and said the motion did not represent the views of the large majority of Green Party members, "nor of people in the country".

Chowns said the motion would be a "distraction from the very important work" the party has been doing campaigning for Palestinian rights.

She added: "I think it is clear that if we have policy, such significant and damaging policy, made by a vote of just 0.4% of our members, that something isn't working in our structures and our policy-making process."

Members of the Green Party of England and Wales endorsed the policy motion by 1,022 votes to 813.

There are 230,000 members of the Green party overall and not everyone attended the conference.

The policy also backs a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine", which includes modern-day Israel.

It defines Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state".

The Board of Deputies of British Jews and the Jewish Leadership Council, which criticised the motion, said: "Zionism is anti-racism, creating a refuge for Jews in their ancient homeland after millennia of persecution outside it."

News.title: Drumcree parade ban was in 'best interests of peace', says Bryant
News.content:
The Northern Ireland secretary of state has said his decision to ban the contentious Orange Order Drumcree parade "was in the best interests of peace".

The decision on Friday came after agreement couldn't be reached between the Portadown District Lodge and the Garvaghy Road residents over whether the march would be allowed down the predominantly nationalist road.

Sir Chris Bryant said he received advice from the PSNI chief constable that allowing the procession to go ahead could lead to serious injury, disorder and wider unrest.

On Saturday, a legal challenge by Orangemen against the decision to ban the parade was adjourned until Monday after the judge said it was not an "emergency" case.

The stalemate has reopened what was once the most bitter parading dispute in Northern Ireland, with stand-offs in the mid-to-late 1990s accompanied by riots, roadblocks and killings.

The Parades Commission was established in 1998 to regulate contentious processions.

Its decisions restricting the Drumcree march have been challenged by the Orange Order for decades.

Earlier this year, a court overturned the commission's original decision to stop the parade, ruling it could go ahead, with restrictions on 27 September.

But Garvaghy Road residents blocked the road that morning, preventing the Orangemen from marching, and a stand-off has continued for almost two weeks.

The Court of Appeal has reserved judgment on a legal challenge brought by Garvaghy Road residents against the decision to allow the march.

Sir Chris said he had spent almost two weeks trying to broker a deal and believed the two sides had come close to an agreement.

He said two outcomes were discussed. One would have allowed the Orangemen to complete one final march along the Garvaghy Road, on the condition it would not apply to march the route again.

The other would have seen the group accept that it had won the right to march, but agree not to exercise that right, but neither proposal secured agreement from both sides.

News.title: Eight men arrested by Greater Manchester Police days after early release from jail
News.content:
Eight men have been arrested by Greater Manchester Police days after leaving prison under the government's early release scheme.

About 700 prisoners from across the country were released early on 1 October in a bid to tackle overcrowding, with about 50 of them being from Greater Manchester.

GMP confirmed that five men had been arrested for breaches of criminal orders, including a domestic abuse prevention order, and others were held on suspicion of robbery, drug offences and domestic violence.

In response, the Ministry of justice (MOJ) said: "We inherited a prison system on the brink of collapse. If we had failed to act, the police would have been forced to halt arrests."

News.title: Rail disruption after overhead line fault
News.content:
Rail passengers are being urged to check before they travel due to overhead line problems on the West Coast Main Line in Staffordshire.

Work was ongoing to fix a fault with the 25,000-volt wires which power trains near Penkridge, causing disruption between Stafford and Wolverhampton.

At 12:00 BST, National Rail confirmed that lines have reopened between Stafford and Birmingham New Street, but residual disruption can still be expected until 16:00 BST on Saturday.

Adam Checkley from Network Rail, said: "Our teams have now cleared the issue allowing the route to reopen, but with trains and their crew out of position, delays and cancellations will continue throughout the day."

Rail replacement buses are in place at Birmingham, Stafford and Wolverhampton.

Checkley added: "We're sorry to passengers impacted by the overhead line problems at Four Ashes near Penkridge.

"With disruption to train services likely throughout the day, I'd urge people to check National Rail Enquiries before they set off on their journey."

Ticket acceptance is in place on alternative routes including the East Coast Main Line, and Midland Main Line via Sheffield.

News.title: Queen reflects on reading 'forbidden' Lady Chatterley's Lover under the pillow
News.content:
Queen Camilla has recalled secretly reading Lady Chatterley's Lover, the passionate and controversial novel by DH Lawrence, as a teenager in the 1960s.

"As teenagers you read a lot of romances. It was the moment of Lady Chatterley, under our pillows, reading that by torchlight. You know the minute something is forbidden, you want to get hold of it," she said about the novel that had been at the centre of an obscenity trial.

The Queen spoke about memorable moments in her own reading for BBC documentary The Book That Changed My Life, and about the life-changing power of literacy and books.

She gave a glimpse of how regular reading is part of her royal marriage: "It's like the best tonic in the world. My husband and I actually read before dinner, just sitting quietly and reading.

"He loves biographies, and PG Wodehouse. I occasionally, when I'm deep in a book, hear him roaring with laughter about something," said the Queen about the King's affection for the author of the Jeeves and Wooster comic novels.

"It's very off-putting, I can't get back into my book, or I'll suddenly start weeping. But it's a lovely, quiet time. I think it would be a complete and utter tragedy if books went forever," she said.

The Queen also revealed more of her own youthful reading, saying she was "mesmerised" by Charles Dickens's Tale of Two Cities and its depiction of those watching the guillotine during the French Revolution.

"Those ghastly women sitting there knitting while everybody had their heads chopped off," she said.

The Queen, who is 79 years old, said she was part of a generation of women who missed out on higher education, which made reading and books even more important.

"I left school quite young. In my day, women didn't go to university, so I think reading has been most of my education," she said.

News.title: Four murder arrests after teenagers attacked
News.content:
Police are continuing to investigate following the arrests of four people after a man died and another suffered life-threatening injuries in Stoke-on-Trent.

A cordon remains in place on Brookhouse Road, Meir, after police were called to reports of violence at 23:45 BST on Friday.

A man in his late teens was confirmed dead at the scene, Staffordshire Police said, and another man, also in his late teens, was taken to hospital, where he remains in a critical but stable condition.

Two 18-year-old men, a 20-year-old man and a 17-year-old boy, all from Stoke-on-Trent, were arrested on suspicion of murder, while the boy was also arrested on suspicion of attempted murder. All remain in police custody.

News.title: Man arrested after boy, 11, injured in 'dog attack'
News.content:
A man has been arrested after an 11-year-old boy was injured in an alleged dog attack.

Three dogs were reported to be "out of control" in the Scotland Hall Road area of Newton Heath in north Manchester at about 16:00 BST on Thursday, Greater Manchester Police said.

The force said one dog was seized and the other two were placed in kennels. The boy suffered minor injuries.

A 31-year-old man has been held on suspicion of possessing an aggressive animal.

The force has not confirmed the breed of dog.

News.title: Fort Hood survivor wants to see mass shooter die — but not Hegseth’s way: ‘Look at my eyes’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A survivor of the Fort Hood mass shooting says he looks forward to attending the execution of the gunman whom he watched gun down his colleagues nearly 17 years ago, but feels uneasy about the Pentagon’s plan to livestream it for the public.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Thursday that the execution of Nidal Hasan would be broadcast online. Hasan, who described the shooting as an act of jihad, is scheduled to be executed by firing squad on Dec. 3 at Fort Hood, the Texas Army base where he killed 13 people and wounded 32 others in the November 2009 rampage.

Alonzo Lunsford, who served in the Army from 1990 until his retirement in 2013, was a sergeant stationed at Fort Hood when Hasan opened fire. Hasan shot Lunsford seven times, including in the head and stomach, and Lunsford witnessed the gunman kill several colleagues who had become close friends.

Lunsford plans to attend Hasan’s execution — the first military execution by firing squad since World War II — telling ABC News he wants to face the convicted gunman one last time.

"I want him to be able to look at my eyes and to let him understand I won't be defeated, can't be defeated. I am no longer a victim, his victim. I am a survivor," Lunsford said.

open image in gallery Nidal Hasan, a former U.S. Army Major and psychiatrist, is set to have the first military execution in more than 65 years in December, which some survivors feel uneasy about ( Reuters )

Lunsford welcomed President Donald Trump’s approval to proceed with Hasan’s execution, saying he believes it could finally bring a sense of closure to him and other survivors of the attack. He also supports the administration’s decision to use a firing squad.

“It's how he shot us,” Lunsford said.

However, Lunsford is uncomfortable with the Pentagon’s plan to make the execution available for anyone to watch online. He believes the broadcast should be restricted to survivors of the shooting and the families of those killed.

"I don't want this to be viewed upon as a spectacle, like a pay-per-view event, or like going to a basketball tournament," he said.

Lunsford also questioned the message a public livestream would send to the rest of the world, arguing that the U.S. should set a moral example rather than turn an execution into a public event.

"We're not trying to meet a standard – we're trying to set a standard for the free world," he said.

open image in gallery Hasan killed 13 people and wounded 32 others in November 2009, after embracing a self-radicalized jihadist ideology and opposing U.S. military deployments in Muslim-majority countries ( 2009 )

Dayna Ferguson, another survivor of the Fort Hood shooting, said she was surprised by the announcement that Hasan's execution would be livestreamed. However, she believes the decision reflects a longstanding history of documenting death and warfare.

"It's not completely shocking, given that death and war have historically always been documented through photographs and video. But it's just not something I expected to hear," she told ABC News.

Ferguson was 21 and serving as an Army specialist when Hasan opened fire. She was shot three times in her arm, shoulder and thigh. She credits a birth defect with helping her survive, as one of the bullets ricocheted off her stomach and into her thigh rather than causing a potentially fatal injury.

"I hadn't really thought about if I agree with the decisions being made – but it doesn't make a difference in what happens to him," Ferguson added.

Ferguson left the Army after completing her four-year enlistment and is still working out arrangements to attend the execution. Despite the injuries and trauma she experienced during the shooting, she said she remains grateful to have survived.

"I've been hurt worse in life than by Nidal. Sometimes you're just the collateral damage in someone else's warfare in their own mind," she said.

open image in gallery In this photo from November 10, 2009, a fallen soldiers memorial is seen in front of the podium where the memorial service that then-President Barack Obama and First Lady Michelle Obama attended to honor the 13 victims ( AFP/Getty )

The criticism extends beyond survivors of the shooting, with Republican and Democratic lawmakers questioning whether livestreaming an execution is appropriate.

Rep. Austin Scott, a Georgia Republican and senior member of the House Armed Services Committee, said he supports Hasan's death sentence but opposes broadcasting the execution publicly.

"I absolutely support the sentence of death, but live-streaming executions is what jihadists do," Scott wrote on X. "America is better than that."

Rep. Adam Smith, the highest-ranking Democrat on the House Armed Services Committee, also criticized the plan, arguing that a public broadcast would undermine the seriousness of the legal system.

"We are a democratic country and should take the rule of law seriously, not turn it into a spectacle," Smith wrote in a statement.

Another Saturday means another brand new episode of Strictly Come Dancing, with more show-stopping routines, more sequins and more fake tans – we wouldn’t have it any other way.

Last week’s episode saw the celebrities and the professional dance partners take to the stage to perform to tracks from Hollywood movies, marking the earliest point that Movie Week has ever occurred in the show’s schedule.

Hairdresser Chris Appleton and his professional partner Amy Dowden were the first couple to leave the show, after the judges chose to back Jaime Winston and Carlos Gu in the dance off.

This time around, there’s no set theme, meaning that we’re being treated to everything from a Charleston to Gina G (yes, really) to a quickstep to “I’m a Believer”.

And with the season now in its third week, there are still criticisms from fans over the new presenting trio.

Last week’s results show saw proceedings get a bit of a shake-up, with Emma Willis joining Johannes Radebe to debrief with the judges. Fans seemed to react positively to this Emma-Jojo combo – could the show bosses be gearing up to test out yet more iterations to see what works best?

Follow all the latest updates below...

News.title: The consistent and concerning trend that should worry Manchester United
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

To paraphrase Sir Alex Ferguson, lads, it’s Manchester United. A game that Tottenham Hotspur ought to have won instead saw then entering injury time staring at defeat. An eventual draw may have showed some of the shortcomings of two early-season underachievers but reflected far worse on United.

Their poorest start to a league season for 40 years has constituted of a series of missed opportunities. Given the lead by Bryan Mbeumo, given a one-man advantage by the stupidity of Rodrigo Bentancur, given the opportunity to turn their dismal first-half display into a second domestic victory of the campaign, they contrived to concede to winless opponents. As against Everton and Brighton, a lead was lost, along with any thought there was a springboard to their season.

Boos rang around Old Trafford at the end. The supporters who had begun by decrying Manchester City’s “cheating bastards” soon realised they had more immediate issues. But their Tottenham counterparts were buoyant. They have spent a record amount to fail to win but, in the performance in the first hour and the spirit at the end, there were reasons for optimism, grounds to feel Roberto De Zerbi’s side is taking shape.

open image in gallery Bryan Mbeumo scored the opening goal for Manchester United ( PA )

That may prove a generous interpretation. Even factoring in Dominic Solanke’s injury-time equaliser, Tottenham still lack ruthlessness. A team with three league goals all season could have been three ahead before they conceded – inevitably, given their recent history – to Mbeumo. Since they tried to sign him last year, he has three goals in as many games against them.

Part of the script seemed copied and pasted in from Spurs’ previous games. Tottenham were terrific for half an hour and failed to turn that dominance into a lead. Then, as they often do, they conceded in the final quarter. It may be slightly harsh to fault Jan Paul van Hecke for Mbeumo’s well-taken goal but the summer signing, culpable against Aston Villa three weeks ago, did not get tight enough to the Cameroonian.

Yet there was a twist at the end when the stand-in skipper Solanke stooped to glance in a header from Sandro Tonali’s cross; it was a first assist for the Italian since his £100m move from Newcastle but Lisandro Martinez was too busy tugging Solanke to actually try and defend the ball in.

open image in gallery Rodrigo Bentancur and Luke Shaw got into a tussle on the side of the pitch ( Getty )

open image in gallery Rodrigo Bentancur was dismissed for a headbutt on Luke Shaw ( Getty )

So United remain the only club without a clean sheet in the Premier League this season. They ought to have conceded far sooner; indeed, Senne Lammens had to make a fine second-minute save from Solanke, remedying the error of his own poor pass.

United were slow and sluggish at the start, hassled and harried. The two managers made six changes apiece but there was some method to De Zerbi’s apparent madness, a seemingly strange selection explained by the omission of several who had played all four internationals for their countries and the inclusion of those he had worked with for the previous three weeks. They had a plan and a blueprint; United seemed to have neither. They looked faster, fresher and fitter. They pressed ferociously.

They were summed up by Conor Gallagher, that least creative and most energetic of No 10s, who almost scored by bundling the ball in; it was all graft and no craft. Savio was electric but lacked an end product, a comment that could be made all too often in his career; the wisdom of spending £75m on him remains questionable. Luke Shaw nudged Savio’s low cross-shot off the line. Solanke spooned a shot from six yards over. Tottenham’s spending spree came to over £300m – almost £400m when Omar Marmoush’s loan becomes permanent – but has not brought them a finisher.

open image in gallery Dominic Solanke headed in a late equaliser for Spurs ( Getty )

United’s first-half yielded one shot, from a fit-again Amad Diallo, and an xG of 0.05. They scored after Michael Carrick made a triple change and relocated Mbeumo to the right. Granted a licence to roam infield, he took Matheus Cunha’s low pass, turned and angled a shot past Antonin Kinsky. Ultimately, though, United could rue the chance Mbeumo had to make it two.

But United struggle to beat teams reduced to 10 men and Tottenham had lost Bentancur, sent off for reacting to a push by Luke Shaw by headbutting the United left-back. Only on for 12 minutes, the Uruguayan will now be banned for three matches. Meanwhile, United’s next three are away at Atletico Madrid, Leeds and Como. They have faced two of the promoted three, two of the current bottom three. They have only won once. It is one more than Tottenham but that will be scant consolation.

News.title: Hurricane Isaias tracker latest: Two dead and scores without power as storm makes landfall
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Hurricane Isaias peeled off hotel and condominium rooftops and facades along the Florida Panhandle before charging north Saturday, dishing out torrential rains and the threat of flash floods and tornadoes across the Southeast.

Two people were killed when trees fell onto homes in Florida and Alabama, and nearly 700,000 customers were without power by midday in four states. Forecasters warned that flooding could stretch into the southern Appalachians.

More than 726,000 people in Alabama and the Florida Panhandle have been left without power on Saturday after Hurricane Isaias crashed into the US Gulf Coast.

The storm made landfall Friday as a Category 2 hurricane, then quickly moved north through Alabama as its wind speeds dropped sharply, weakening to a post-tropical cyclone, the US National Hurricane Center said in its latest advisory.

But residents are bracing for flooding and gusty winds in Isaias’ aftermath as authorities warned of the potential for tornadoes.

open image in gallery Maps show strong winds moving across Alabama ( Windy.com )

The storm is expected to continue weakening but produce gusty winds well inland as the possibility of life-threatening storm surges still looms for parts of the Florida Panhandle.

It will travel northwards across Alabama and over the Tennessee Valley later on Saturday, according to the National Weather Service.

Forecasters also warned that conditions could stir up tornadoes across parts of the Florida Panhandle and into Georgia and the Carolinas.

Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, as the first hurricane of the Atlantic season. Hurricane-force winds lashed the Gulf shoreline in the low-lying coastal area known for powdery white-sand beaches dotted with vacation homes, waterfront bars, and seafood shacks.

“The storm is here. Buckle down at this point. Don’t be getting out on the roads,” Florida governor Ron DeSantis said Friday.

Roads in Destin were flooded, while in nearby Pensacola, police warned residents to stay off the streets because of debris across roadways. While the extent of the damage was not immediately known, many area residents posted pictures online of downed trees and power lines, and one social media video showed a roof being ripped off an inn in Pensacola.

open image in gallery The storm is expected to travel northwards across the Tennessee Valley ( Windy.com )

Some Panhandle counties temporarily suspended emergency response Friday night because of dangerous conditions.

Parts of southern Alabama also were flooded, with officials in Mobile reporting downed trees and power lines. Roads in Houston County, which is in the southeastern corner of the state, were closed because of similar conditions.

open image in gallery Kevin Hudgins helps guest Laura Gower after a power outage at the Residence Inn ( Getty )

More than 726,000 customers in Florida and Alabama were without power early Saturday, according to poweroutage.com.

Despite weakening, heavy rain is forecast as Isaias moves inland, with 4 to 8 inches (10 to 20 centimeters) or even more expected through the weekend from southern Alabama, the Florida Panhandle and Big Bend, and southwest Georgia.

Isaias, the first hurricane to hit the eastern US since Milton tore up the Gulf Coast of Florida in 2024, is also expected to bring heavy rain and potential flooding to much of the Southeast over the weekend, then to parts of the Midwest and Northeast into Monday.

The storm also grounded most Friday flights at several panhandle airports, including all flights into and out of Destin-Fort Walton Beach Airport. President Donald Trump, meanwhile, scrapped his plans to attend Saturday’s football game between the University of Georgia and the University of Alabama in Tuscaloosa. He said he didn’t want to disrupt emergency response efforts.

Meanwhile, in the Pacific, Simon strengthened into a Category 4 hurricane as it approached Mexico’s coast.

Tropical Storm Rachel was also expected to bring heavy winds and rain to northern Mexico and Southern California over the weekend.

— with Associated Press

News.title: Trump tears into Zelensky: ‘Time for Ukraine to get a new president’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump said Saturday that “it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president,” railing at Volodymyr Zelensky, and claiming he has not done enough to end his country’s war that has raged since Russia invaded four years ago.

Speaking to reporters at the White House on his way to a rally in Tennessee, Trump said, “I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal,″ adding that ”for some reason (Zelensky) never does."

“Zelensky could have settled this war many times, many many times, and he chooses not to,” Trump railed, after being asked about his deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to supply diesel to the U.S. in a bid to lower fuel costs ahead of the midterm elections.

It comes as Americans have seen their fuel costs rocket following Trump’s war in Iran. The deal raises questions about Trump’s sweeping sanctions on Russia, signed into law just last month, that aimed to punish and pressure Moscow for its war against Ukraine.

“Very difficult. It's a war that should have never been started. If I were president, if the election weren't rigged, I would have been president, and that war would have never started,” Trump said Saturday, repeating a debunked but oft-repeated claim about the US election in 2020.

’Zelensky could have settled this war many times, many many times, and he chooses not to,’ President Donald Trump railed at Ukraine’s leader Saturday ( Getty )

Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than 4 1/2 years since Moscow’s full-scale invasion. Ukraine is struggling to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed more than 60 people over the past four days.

“But he could have settled it many times, and he chose not to,” Trump went on about the Ukraine leader. “We said you can do whatever you want to Russia. Don't hit the refineries because that's a world problem that's caused. And he wants to make problems for the world.”

Trump then appeared to extrapolate his rage at Zelensky to some of the domestic matters that have seen his approval rating plummet to epic depths, a plunge that has Republicans facing loss of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in November’s elections.

“He wants to make problems for our farmers, our ranchers with diesel fuel because Russia supplies a large portion of the diesel fuel throughout the world, and we told them, do whatever you want, but don't hit the diesel fuel because there's a big problem, a big shortage. And what does he do? He goes and hits the diesel fuel,” Trump railed.

Trump punctuated his rant by concluding of Zelensky: “He better damn well stop!”

Zelensky has “lost 30% of your country and you’ve had over a million people go between the two of them, over 2 million people killed. That’s a war that should have never started. And I think it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president,” Trump said.

Zelensky on Friday night lashed out at Trump over the deal, perhaps sparking Trump’s strong rebuke.

“I believe our team is simply being used as a smoke screen, and that is certainly not fair,” Zelensky said.

“It is certainly not how partners should treat each other,” he added, calling Trump’s announcement of the diesel deal with Putin a “weak decision.”

In a post on social media, Zelensky blasted: “Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilised world.’

News.title: Eight people killed in ‘devastating’ shooting in Pennsylvania
News.content:

Eight people were killed Friday in a shooting in Erie, Pennsylvania, police said.

The shooter was also dead, and there was no threat to the public, the city said. Authorities didn't provide more details.

“I have not seen anything like this in my 28-plus years,” Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah told a local news station. “I’m not sure that the city of Erie has ever seen the loss of life and the devastation that we just witnessed.”

Erie is about 117 miles (188 kilometers) north of Pittsburgh.

News.title: Scotland’s Grant Forrest and England’s Joe Dean tie for lead in Spanish Open
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Grant Forrest and Joe Dean share a one-shot lead going into the final round of the Open de Espana in Madrid.

Forrest began the day with a one-shot advantage at the Real Club de Campo Villa de Madrid but slipped down the leaderboard after bogeying the fifth hole.

However, birdies at the 11th, 14th and 16th gave the Scot a four-under-par round of 67 and a total of 13 under.

Forrest, who is searching for his third DP World Tour title, said on europeantour.com: “I’m happy with how I handled today.

“I didn’t have my best stuff but I’m really proud of how I dug in and made some nice putts, a couple of good recovery shots, and all in all a decent score again.

“This is one of my favourite tournaments, it’s been good to me in the past, and I’d love nothing more than to go home with a trophy tomorrow.”

His round was enough to leave him tied for the lead alongside Sheffield’s Dean, who will feel he should have produced an even better outcome than the 65 he signed for.

Dean followed five birdies on the front nine with three more at the 12th, 14th and 15th to open up a three-shot lead.

But the 32-year-old then double-bogeyed the 16th and dropped another shot at 17 before finishing on a high with a 31-foot putt for birdie on the last.

“It gave a little bit of hope after those previous two holes,” said Dean. “We’ll go again and see what happens.”

France’s Victor Perez and Dane Jacob Skov Olesen both also posted rounds of 65 to move to 12 under, one shot off the lead, alongside Joel Girrbach of Switzerland, who was round in 67.

Angel Ayora is the leading Spanish hope and he sits three shots off the lead after a 66 on a day of low scoring.

News.title: Park service could remove more than 500 trees at historic golf course Trump wants to redesign
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The National Park Service has begun a new round of tree-cutting at a historic golf course near the National Mall as the Trump administration proceeds with a plan to renovate the East Potomac Golf Links into a championship-level course.

More than 500 trees “that do not contribute to the historic landscape will be removed” as part of the rehabilitation project, the National Park Service said in a court filing Friday. “No healthy trees that are contributing features of the historical golf course” — including historic cherry trees — will be removed as part of the project, the park service said.

A total of 169 trees will be removed starting Saturday, with another 90 trees slated for removal later, the agency said.

The tree removals come as President Donald Trump has moved to turn the course into a world-class golf venue — part of his grand vision for Washington, D.C., where he has torn down storied structures, remade or renamed others and deployed the National Guard for more than a year.

Some residents fear the planned changes to the golf course — where Trump has visited with a cabinet member, a well-known golf course architect and blueprints — risk altering the character of a place that has served Washingtonians of all income levels for more than a century. Turning the park into an upscale golf course will mean costlier fees and a likely loss of public space.

"The National Park Service is finally implementing a 7-year-old plan to address tree overgrowth at East Potomac Golf Course,'' the Interior Department said in a statement Saturday. The department oversees the park service and other agencies that manage federal lands.

The renovation work will include selective tree and vegetation work to restore the course, the Interior Department said, adding that the work is intended to “help restore the course’s historic character and reopen views toward landmarks, including the Washington Monument, National War College, Potomac River and Washington Channel."

The park service “recognizes the importance of trees to the park and its visitors. This carefully planned work is part of our required stewardship of the park,” the statement said.

The golf course will remain open to the public throughout the renovation effort, although individual holes may temporarily close while work is underway, the agency said.

The 106-year-old public course has been embroiled in a lawsuit since February. Plaintiffs including the DC Preservation League say the Trump administration’s reconstruction would violate the congressional act that created the park in 1897. The group sought an emergency stop-work order this spring because of concerns that work was expected to begin immediately on the course.

Trump, an avid golfer, has posted about the course on social media, “When completed, this Course will have the ability to host Major Golf Tournaments, including The U.S. Open, The Ryder Cup, The PGA Championship, and other top PGA Tour events,” he wrote in late June.

It’s unclear when the course could host any major tournaments, as locations are chosen several years ahead of the events.

The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

News.content:
Before the game we talked about two things, the challenge ahead against a team that had not lost in the Premier League. They full deserved to be where they are and it was going to be really tough. The second was to restore our identity and be ourselves again.

We weren’t pleased with our performance against Brighton and we wanted to put it right. But the context is that this was a difficult one [opponent]. But we reacted in a way that was unique and made it so special.

[Leeds] are very well organised, very physical and very committed in everything that they do. They are a threat. They are incredible the way they attack the ball and set-pieces, with belief. They came close to punishing us. They have individual quality and they are in a good moment.
