News.title: Resurgent Verstappen on fire in the Singapore smog
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the sprint race for the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix from the Marina Bay Circuit. Given the way the championship standings are, it looks like Kimi Antonelli has one hand on the drivers’ title. That means that the most significant thing is the battle for individual race victories. That includes grands prix, but also sprint races, like we have today.

Formula One is very keen on sprint races, increasing their number significantly next year, but we have never had one in Singapore before. We will find out today whether there was good reason for it. I suppose the logic is that even a processional sprint race is better than a free practice session and that having two qualifying sessions on a street circuit such as this is exciting, too.

Still, although he might be strolling towards the championship, he and Mercedes are not the dominant force they were at the start of the season when he won five in a row having finished second in the opening race. In fact, in the last 10 grands prix, Antonelli has won three and Russell two. With Max Verstappen’s win in Malaysia last weekend it meant each of Red Bull, McLaren, Ferrari and Mercedes have won races this season.

It is Verstappen who is in strong form in an upgraded Red Bull, as he snuck pole position from George Russell by just over a tenth of a second. He was followed by Charles Leclerc in the Ferrari and then Oscar Piastri in the McLaren. Antonelli, in the upgraded Mercedes, found things more difficult, finishing down in seventh nearly 0.7sec off the pace.

Anyway, the sprint gets under way in about 30 minutes and we will be here for all the updates from that, as well as qualifying later today.

News.title: Majestic All Blacks copy Springbok playbook to dismantle Australia
News.content:
Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Bledisloe Cup Test as New Zealand host Australia at Eden Park in Auckland.

The All Blacks are enduring one of the toughest periods in their history, having suffered three successive Test defeats against South Africa in August and September, which saw the Springboks claim the inaugural Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series tour. Dave Rennie’s men are under immense pressure to avoid a fourth consecutive Test defeat for the first time since 1998.

You could argue there’s never been a better opportunity for Australia to beat New Zealand at Eden Park. The Wallabies are enjoying a six-Test unbeaten run – their longest such streak since 2017, with five games in this rejuvenated period coming under new head coach Les Kiss. In their most recent outing, Australia secured an extraordinary 42-38 victory over a much-changed South Africa side in Perth, despite being reduced to 11 players at one point.

Australia will feel further encouraged due to several key absences for New Zealand, as Ardie Savea, Ruben Love, Richie Mo’unga, Caleb Clarke, Fehi Fineanganofo, Billy Proctor and Anton Lienert-Brown are all out injured. In a reshuffle for the All Blacks, Damian McKenzie will begin at fly-half for the first time in 2026. Other notable inclusions for the home side see all three Barrett brothers, Codie Taylor, Tupou Vaa’i, Cam Roigard and Will Jordan starting.

Meanwhile, the visitors are without the suspended Hunter Paisami, with Isaac Henry taking his place at centre. The likes of Ryan Lonergan, Len Ikitau, Harry Wilson, Ben Donaldson and Max Jorgensen, who were all key to the triumph against the Springboks, retain their starting spots.

All the statistics overwhelmingly favour New Zealand. The All Blacks have not lost any edition of the Bledisloe Cup since 2002, winning 51 series to Australia’s 12, and are unbeaten at Eden Park since 1994, when they lost to France. Australia are winless at Eden Park since 1986, tasting defeat there 30 times in 34 games, and have lost their last 11 Tests against New Zealand.

However, given the landscape heading into this historic rivalry between these two heavyweights, it genuinely feels like anything could happen.

Kick-off is at 7:10am.

News.title: Black British Business Awards 2026 winners revealed
News.content:
The chief executive of Dr. Martens has been named the Black British Business Person of the Year at the 2026 Black British Business Awards (BBBAwards).

Ije Nwokorie, who became chief of Dr. Martens in January last year and is the only black chief executive in the FTSE 250, was awarded in recognition of his role shaping Dr. Martens’ growth strategy.

He is recognised inside Dr. Martens for his strong communication with staff, according to the judges.

Before joining Dr. Martens, Mr Nwokorie spent more than 11 years at Wolff Olins, the marketing giant, before working as a senior director at Apple.

Born in the US but brought up from age six against the backdrop of post-civil-war Nigeria, Mr Nwokorie has described how he and his family went from the lifestyle trappings of 1960s America to a small Nigerian village and a home with no running water.

On winning the award, Mr Nwokorie said: “This recognition means a lot to me. While this award bears my name, it reflects the talent, dedication and generosity of the incredible teammates, mentors and leaders who have shaped me as a person and a professional.

“It is a powerful reminder that there is nothing more important in our leadership journeys than the time we invest to help others thrive.”

Alongside his executive career, he has served as a trustee at Charity: water for nearly a decade and held board roles at cultural and humanitarian organisations including the Institute of International Visual Arts and Malaria No More UK.

He also served as chairman of trustees for the Chineke! Orchestra, a British orchestra championing change and the first in Europe to feature a majority of black and ethnically diverse musicians.

The Black British Business Awards started in 2014 to celebrate the achievements of black people in British business. The Telegraph is the national media partner for the awards.

Mr Nwokorie was presented with the award at an exclusive ceremony sponsored by JPMorgan Chase at London’s Hilton Park Lane hotel.

Speaking at the ceremony, Sophie Chandauka, the executive founder of the awards, said: “You lend the BBBAwards credibility not simply to celebrate excellence, but to ensure the best and brightest from all communities get a fair shot. That commitment has made the BBBAwards the UK’s premium awards programme for black business achievement.”

A spokesman for JPMorgan Chase said: “We couldn’t be prouder to support and celebrate such an outstanding breadth of black British talent.

“Their accomplishments continue to inspire future generations and demonstrate the exceptional value they bring to businesses, communities and the wider UK economy.”

This year’s winners are as follows:

Black British Business Person of the Year: Ije Nwokorie, chief executive of Dr Martens

News.title: Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it
News.content:
England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

News.title: What is the XFG Covid strain? Symptoms and what to know as the variant hits the UK
News.content:
Cases of Covid-19 have risen sharply across the UK this month, driven largely by a variant of the virus known as ‘XFG’.

Sometimes referred to as ‘Stratus’ and the ‘American strain’, owing to the fact that it is now the most common strain in North America, it was first identified in January 2025 and has since spread worldwide.

Between August and September, Covid cases in Britain jumped 230 per cent, from 1,374 to 4,589 new infections, half of which were caused by the XFG strain.

Hospitalisation rates have also increased by 15 per cent in the same period, according to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

The true number of cases is likely to be much higher, as most people who contract Covid-19 experience a milder illness and will not visit hospital or receive an official diagnosis via their GP.

What are the symptoms, and how is it different from other variants?

Symptoms of XFG are similar to other variants of Covid-19 like Delta and Omicron, and typically begin with a sore throat, before developing into a cough and fever.

However, experts have noted that patients diagnosed with XFG tend to present with a characteristic hoarse, croaky voice, which is distinctive from older strains.

More than 30 other symptoms have been known to be associated with XFG and other Covid strains, including diarrhoea, vomiting, loss of taste and smell, shortness of breath, headache, and muscle aches.

Why are cases rising?

Current data does not suggest that XFG leads to more severe illness than any other variant in circulation, according to the UKHSA.

As the UK moves into winter, colder and wetter weather naturally influences the rise in respiratory illnesses like Covid-19 and the flu, given people spend more time indoors and in closer proximity to each other, where viruses can more easily transmit between them.

It has also been roughly a year since the last significant wave of Covid-19 cases, meaning that the population-wide immunity has somewhat waned, making people more susceptible to the disease, the UKHSA said.

Can you be vaccinated against XFG?

The current Covid-19 vaccine is designed to protect against XFG and related strains specifically, after modelling suggested it would become the dominant variant this season.

Those eligible for a Covid-19 autumn booster include adults over the age of 75, residents in care homes, and anyone over six months old with a weakened immune system, due to a health condition or treatment.

Covid vaccines are also available to buy privately for those who are not eligible for a free jab, and typically cost around £98 per dose.

What should you do if you suspect you have XFG?

The NHS no longer advises that people with symptoms of Covid-19 take a test, unless they want to do so.

If you feel unwell or have a high temperature, health authorities advise you to try and stay home and avoid contact with people until you feel better.

They also recommend avoiding contact with vulnerable people, like those undergoing chemotherapy or the elderly, for at least 10 days.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Harry’s Invictus Games challenge in Kenya is helping veterans battle physical and mental scars
News.content:
Wounded veterans from 10 countries have gathered in Kenya’s Great Rift Valley for a week of endurance challenges, organised by the charity behind Prince Harry’s Invictus Games.

Twenty-five serving and former personnel, among them a Ukrainian who survived a direct bomb hit in Donetsk and a Danish combat engineer who cleared roadside bombs in Afghanistan, will run, hike or cycle up to 120km across the area on Saturday October 10, World Mental Health Day.

The Invictus Games Foundation, the charity the Duke of Sussex founded in 2014 for wounded, injured and sick service personnel, has organised the event.

For Vasyl, a Ukrainian soldier, it will be his first time in Africa and his first long-distance challenge.

After three weeks of military training in the UK, the 34-year-old joined a brigade in Donetsk as a reconnaissance squad commander, spending more than 19 months on the front line. He was wounded when a drone dropped a grenade three metres from him, and the shrapnel still causes frequent pain in his leg which can sometimes make walking difficult.

But he said the physical injury was easier to bear than the loss of the friends he made in the trenches.

“There is a level of kindness between comrades in a trench that you will never find in civilian life,” he said. “If someone made a mistake or said something wrong, we immediately forgave them and thought nothing more of it.

“For me, the pain of loss is the hardest thing the war has left behind.”

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Settlement talks with Premier League before punishments agreed
Sports.content:
Man City are in the centre of a major Premier League charges storm

Manchester City are back in Premier League action for the first time since the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules

Hello and welcome to The Mirror's live blog on Saturday, October 10, as Premier League action returns following the extended international break.

Manchester City are set to return to the pitch for the first time since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. The club have already launched an appeal after an Independent Commission found them guilty of 114 out of 115 charges relating to the period between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

The allegations include claims that more than £830million in owner funding was used to inflate the club’s revenues through so-called 'sham' agreements. Speculation continues to mount over the potential sanctions City could face, with possible punishments ranging from a substantial fine and points deduction to the prospect of expulsion from the Premier League.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick has nowhere to hide as Man Utd fans turn in draw with 10-man Tottenham
Sports.content:
Tottenham secured a much deserved point as Dominic Solanke scored in stoppage time to deny a Manchester United team who had been outclassed in front of a frustrated Old Trafford.

It was a shock when Bryan Mbeumo scored on 70 minutes to put the hosts ahead after the home fans had jeered throughout such was the level of Tottenham dominance.

They looked poised for three points, even more so when Rodrigo Bentancur was sent-off, but Solanke was on hand to head home with 92 minutes on the clock, leaving the north Londoners with something to show for their efforts, although their performance deserved all three points.

In the opening exchanges Tottenham looked like the team that they dreamed they would be under Roberto De Zerbi, dominanting the ball and the territory, albeit aided in part by United themselves.

‌



The hosts seemed to be on a mission of self harm such was their desire to play out in and around their own box, which saw Solanke gifted with a one-on-one chance, only to fluff his lines. Senne Lammens needed quick feet shortly after as he was again under pressure.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The Old Trafford crowd, clearly not prepared to be subjected to another abject display, begun jeering as Tottenham came forward in waves. Those boos peaked when Lammens booted a clearance straight out of play.

United did steady the ship as the game went on, but it was a shock that it was a goalless contest come half-time. The home supporters still ensured the Red Devils stars walked off to a chorus of boos.

‌



Tottenham's onslaught continued with Savio racing to the byline, only for his cutback to somehow get cleared. Solanke missed his second chance minutes later, firing over to leave De Zerbi feeling like he should almost laugh otherwise he'd cry.

That feeling was only emphasised when Mbeumo converted in front of the Stretford End. The Tottenham boss saw his team finish with ten men as his midfielder was dismissed for a clash with Luke Shaw, but they would get the last laugh as Solanke headed home in stoppage time.

OLD TRAFFORD TURNS AS CRACKS EXPOSED

They're renowned for the patience. If this were any other club the amount of toxic games over the past decade would be through the roof, but every fanbase has their breaking point.

View 3 Images Tottenham rescued a much deserved point

‌



It takes a lot to boo one of their own, you can see that by how long they stood by Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. But Carrick tasted the Old Trafford jeers after they squandered a 2-0 lead to lose against Brighton in the Carabao Cup only weeks ago.

During their shocking first-half showing against Tottenham the boos came as Tottenham continued to dominate, and they reached boiling point midway through the opening 45. United did rally and improve as the half went on, but this simply isn't good enough and the supporters are now willing to let the players and the boss know.

Against any other team this game would've been done on the hour. That is something United and Carrick cannot escape as their direction of travel seems to be, front their perspective, heading in the wrong direction, and for good measure the home side were booed at full-time.

WHERE'S THE MONEY GONE?

For so long former players and pundits would cast their eye over United's squad and wonder just where the tens of millions actually went. Its no secret how much money they've spent in the years since Sir Alex Ferguson, desperately trying to find that level once again.

‌



But their investment has often not been reflected in the squad, owing to overpaying for players or struggling with a direction with their recruitment. Last summer the money spent on the attack seemed to look smart business, which was a rarity for United.

And yet 12 months on and that feeling is back again. Over £150million was spent on their midfield options - Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba all arriving.

There's been some injury issues, but Tielemans isn't looking like he has in recent years and Santos is struggling for minutes. Their engine room was constantly over run, and after a matter of games we're already questioning those transfer decisions.

View 3 Images Bryan Mbeumo's strike wasn't enough for the win after Tottenham's late leveller

‌



PRETTY FOOTBALL DOESN'T WIN GAMES

Probably something of a backhanded compliment but watching Tottenham in that opening 20 minutes was similar to watching Manchester City during Pep Guardiola's first season when they were purring.

Throughout that season City quickly adopted the principles that had made Guardiola such a success elsewhere in Europe. They were in charge of the ball, they won it back quickly, their attacks seemed to be relentless, they seemed like it was a case of when, not if, they would score.

But Guardiola himself would bemoan their inability to turn their dominance into goals. It was scoring the goals that turned them into a machine. Tottenham did everything but score. That perhaps sums it up. You can coach a team up until the final bit of the game, but converting chances requires a killer instinct Tottenham are struggling with, although this was a display they can be proud of.

‌

Sports.title: Bayern Munich break Bundesliga record by conceding goal after EIGHT seconds after Neuer disaster
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich break Bundesliga record by conceding goal after EIGHT seconds after Neuer disaster

Bayern Munich kicked off against Augsburg but found themselves a goal down just eight seconds later in incredible scenes in the Bundesliga

View 2 Images Manuel Neuer's error cost his team (Image: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images)

Bayern Munich conceded a goal after just eight seconds despite being the team to kick off as a Manuel Neuer clanger cost them against Augsburg. Neuer played a weak chip as he was closed down but could not avoid forward Robin Fellhauer, who caught him in possession after just two seconds

‌



‌



Luis Diaz had played the ball straight back to the legendary goalkeeper, who played himself into trouble. Fellhauer claimed the ball with Neuer well outside of his box, and drove forward with composure to slot the ball into the net with a handful of seconds on the clock.

‌



Fellhauer's effort set a new Bundesliga record as he found the net fast enough to usurp a mark that had stood for 12 years. Karim Bellarabi scored for Bayer Leverkusen against Borussia Dortmund in 2014 after nine seconds, and that was matched in 2015 when Kevin Volland also scored against Bayern Munich, for Hoffenheim.

‌

Bayern Munich found their way back into the game when Ismael Saibari found the net after 55 minutes, but their hosts were able to take the lead again. Neur won't look upon Augsburg's second strike with fond memories after he parried Calvin Brackelmann's effort into the path of Rodrigo Riberio, who made no mistake to tap in the rebound.

Nathaniel Brown secured a point for the Bundesliga giants with an 80th-minute equaliser as Bayern slipped up for the second time this season and allowed Borussia Dortmund to take top spot.

‌



But it was record-breaker Fellhauer who would take the headlines from the game. "It's indescribable because you're part of something really big. Someone has to make up for those eight seconds now," he said.

View 2 Images Robin Fellhauer of Augsburg celebrates scoring his team’s first goal (Image: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Neuer's performance could yet put his position under scrutiny with less than a year remaining on his contract. The World Cup winner signed a contract extension in the summer and now shares minutes with Jonas Urbig in Bayern's net.

The 23-year-old has played just one Bundesliga match this season but he made his Germany debut during the international break, keeping a clean sheet against Germany. Lothar Matthaus has high expectations for the youngster.

"I see Jonas Urbig as a serious challenger,” Matthäus wrote. “His build-up play, his movements, his saves, and how he intercepts crosses – I thought I saw the young Manuel Neuer there.”

Article continues below

Neuer, 40, has already hinted that he could retire at the end of the season. Speaking during pre-season he admitted it looked to be the direction he was heading towards.

"I don't play the matches just to say, 'This is my last game,'" Neuer said. "It doesn't matter whether this might have been my last time at one stadium or another – we'll see. It certainly looks very much as though I'm going to retire."

Sports.title: Arsenal star admits he wants to cause problem for Mikel Arteta after Leeds United decision
Sports.content:
Arsenal star admits he wants to cause problem for Mikel Arteta after Leeds United decision

Arsenal struck twice in eight second-half minutes to secure a comeback 2-1 win against Leeds United at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday afternoon

View 3 Images Gabriel and Bruno Guimaraes following Arsenal's win over Leeds United (Image: (Alex Burstow/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

Bruno Guimaraes admitted he wants to give Mikel Arteta a selection headache after coming off the bench to put Arsenal’s title defence back on track. Guimaraes was on target as Mikel Arteta’s side scored two goals in eight second-half minutes to come from behind against Leeds United.

‌



‌



James Justin fired Daniel Farke’s side ahead before Riccardo Calafiori drew the reigning Premier League champions level just after the hour mark. Guimaraes completed the comeback with an assured finish from the edge of the penalty area less than 10 minutes after coming off the bench.

‌



The victory ensured the Gunners returned to winning ways after a 3-0 defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion before the international break. And the Brazil international, who moved to the Emirates Stadium from Newcastle United during the summer, admitted he is keen to give his manager a decision to make when it comes to team selection.

‌



“I feel unbelievable,” he told TNT Sports. “I feel in the last game against Brighton we were not the level that... and today the mentality was bouncing back.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“To be honest, to be fair, this is my first official game at home, it's been unbelievable: score an important goal, three important points and yeah, great finish, I'm very happy.”

“For me it's important when I'm on the pitch to give my best - give a little bit of a headache for the manager.

“I'm just very glad to score my first goal here at the Emirates, an important goal. We want to be champions again so three points is always welcome.”

‌



Before he added: “Well, I think I've been proving [myself] in the Premier League for the last five years. So but of course it's a new challenge for me, it's always important to play.

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes celebrates after putting Arsenal in front against Leeds

“And like I said, for me, the most important thing for Bruno is going onto the pitch and playing my best football, and I'm very happy about today.

‌



“The Premier League is very tight. I think Leeds have a great team. It was a tough game, we're glad we got the three points but like I said, very tight - so very welcome when we get the three points.”

Speaking after the game, Gunners boss Arteta said: “This is the level for Arsenal, every week, every game, every minute, every action that you have to be at.

“Against Brighton he wasn’t at that level, and today he was much better, and he can still be much better, and that’s what we have to demand.

‌



View 3 Images Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta during the win over Leeds United

“I demand it from myself, and I’m going to demand the same with my players because if we do that we will raise the standards and we’ll be a better team.

“He’s still not in the best condition because he did not have a pre-season. But he’s done it twice, (scoring from the bench) against Sunderland and now against Leeds, and that’s the quality needed at this level to continue to win.”

Sports.title: Gary Neville lip reads Senne Lammens' X-rated message to Man Utd teammates
Sports.content:
Gary Neville lip reads Senne Lammens' X-rated message to Man Utd teammates

Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens endured a difficult first-half against Tottenham Hotspur

View 2 Images Gary Neville has claimed Senne Lammens told his teammates he didn't 'want the ball' after some hairy moments vs Spurs.

Gary Neville highlighted Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lamme struggles during a difficult first-half against Tottenham Hotspur. The former Red Devils right-back suggested that the Belgian told his teammates that he didn't want the ball.

‌



‌



The United number one struggled during the first-half with his distribution and was at fault in almost gifting Spurs the opener before clearing out of play.

‌



Lammens' pass to Kobbie Mainoo was cut out inside 10 minutes but the shot-stopper stepped up to deny Dominic Solanke a certain effort from close-range.

‌



It was a dour first-half back after the international break from United and they were booed off at half-time by the Old Trafford faithful. Spurs' profilgacy spared the Red Devils from going in at the break behind with the North London club cutting through Michael Carrick's side on multiple occasions.

Cristiano Ronaldo suspension confirmed as Portugal FA issue new statement READ MORE :

Out-of-character struggles for Lammens didn't help matters and Neville picked up on the 24-year-old's struggles, boldly claiming that he urged his teammates not to pass the ball back to him.

He said: "Senne Lammens, that ball is getting back to him too much by the way, number one.

‌



"But number two, when it comes back to him, he's looking like it's a struggle in his mind. 'I don't want it' he's just said, I'm not a lip reader but there was a little f (swear word) in there as well."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Prior to the international break, Carrick faced pressure over his position in the Old Trafford hotseat after two defeats and a draw in their previous three.

‌



United haven't been able to continue the impressive work from last season under the Premier League-winning midfielder. The new signing haven't managed to impact the play and marquee signing Carlos Baleba has had to wait for his first start for the club but was on the bench for the visit of Roberto De Zerbi's side.

Sky Sports pundit Jamie Redknapp felt that United were the cause of their own problems in the opening 45.

View 2 Images Senne Lammens endured a tough evening with Man United. (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Article continues below

He said: "Michael Carrick will be thinking, 'how do we get a foothold in this game?' They've got no idea how to play out, no real structure, spread out and I think Tottenham have been excellent in the first-half.

"Man United have caused their own problems, that pass isn't on (from Lammens). Playing it into a midfield player there, Bergvall pounces on it."

Spurs went into Saturday's game in as much difficulty after starting the day at the foot of the table. The Italian's side have yet to win in the Premier League this season with two draws and three defeats to start the season.

Sports.title: Arsenal star 'carried off the pitch' after suffering worrying injury during warm down
Sports.content:
Arsenal star 'carried off the pitch' after suffering worrying injury during warm down

Arsenal came from behind to secure victory against Leeds United but Mikel Arteta received some bad news following the match as the Gunners suffered an injury

View 2 Images Piero Hincapie suffered an injury after the match (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal defender Piero Hincapie had to be carried off the field during the Gunners' warm-down after their victory over Leeds. The defender featured in the game as a substitute but went down clutching his right ankle, completing some further work following the full-time whistle.

‌



‌



Mikel Arteta's side came from behind to earn three points at the Emirates. James Justin opened the scoring for Daniel Farke's team as the north London side struggled to find their rhythm. Riccardo Calafiori got the Gunners back on level terms following a smart move before Bruno Guimaraes scored an impressive winner in the 70th minute.

‌



But Arteta's mood may have soured when he discovered one of his players suffered a late injury outside of match action. Back-up goalkeeper, Illan Meslier, carried Hincapie from the pitch as he was spotted holding his right ankle.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Last month, Hincapie suffered from muscular problems that saw him miss the Carabao Cup against Ipswich Town. The Ecuador international was not called up to the South American side for the three-week break from domestic action before his nine-minute outing against Leeds.

Hincapie was being managed following his early-season issues and had made just four appearances for Arsenal heading into the match against Leeds. The 24-year-old had featured for 152 minutes before Saturday and only started against Napoli, having missed 16 matches for club and country since the start of last season.

‌



He will now have to wait to discover if he faces a more significant spell on the sidelines.

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta looks to have another injury to deal with (Image: Mikel Arteta looks to have another injury to deal with)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Speaking after the match, Arteta was pleased with his side's reaction after losing to Brighton ahead of the international break.

"It's every time we put that shirt on," he said. "The last time that we put our shirt on, something was missing, and we need to be very conscious of that.

"From being exceptional and being the champions to being extremely average, like in that game, it’s a really thin line. So if you don't want it more than the opponent, you are not able to cope emotionally with certain situations, you're going to suffer.

Article continues below

"We all suffered and we didn't enjoy one bit that game. But then you have to learn the lesson, and we certainly did that. We spoke about it and you could sense that it was something in their tummies."

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo suspension confirmed as Portugal FA issue new statement
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo suspension confirmed as Portugal FA issue new statement

Cristiano Ronaldo is edging close to being suspended by Portugal after their federation confirmed proceedings had begun after he stormed out of camp

View 2 Images Portugal have provisionally suspended Cristiano Ronaldo (Image: Getty Images)

Portugal have confirmed that Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended with "disciplinary proceedings" against him beginning as the nation's authorities digest the events of the recent international break.

‌



‌



He walked out of camp following a row with Jorge Jesus, which stemmed from conversations they had over playing time. Ronaldo was angered by his omission, despite Portugal winning all four of their games under their new manager, who took charge after the World Cup.

‌



Ronaldo would later put out a statement, where he underlined the reasons for his actions, criticising the "the absolute breach of trust in the coach’s word". However he admitted he was deserving of a punishment from the Portuguese authorities.

‌



There is huge scope for the suspension that could be handed down to the five-time Ballon d'Or winner. Anything that extends beyond a month would see Ronaldo ruled out of his nation’s Nations League fixtures against Denmark and Wales next month.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

A statement from the Portuguese federation read: “The initiation of disciplinary proceedings against Cristiano Ronaldo, by deliberation of the Non-Professional Section, of October 9, 2026, with the purpose of the investigation of any disciplinary relevance of the facts participated on October 7”.

‌



“Without prejudice to the automatic preventive suspension to which he was subject until the date of establishment, the non-automatic preventive suspension of the player was determined and the urgent nature was attributed to the process”.

Ronaldo has chosen to play on in the aftermath of his sixth World Cup, despite there being an expectation he would retire, but his actions are now set to see him sidelined for a period.

View 2 Images The veteran's actions whilst on international duty look set to land him in hot water (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

The 41-year-old claimed: "The consequence of this act of mine must be assessed and punished by the Portuguese Football Federation. I understand that the punishment should have no mitigating factors. I am not just any player; I am team captain, and that constitutes an aggravating factor."

When quizzed on Ronaldo's outburst Jesus told reporters: "I read the statement and now, like I do every day, I'm going to the Federation headquarters to work, to think about the Portuguese national team. I have nothing more to say."

Sports.title: Man Utd transfer blunder exposed as Real Madrid enquiry revealed for £25m star
Sports.content:
Man Utd transfer blunder exposed as Real Madrid enquiry revealed for £25m star

Scott McTominay has been a key player for Napoli since leaving Manchester United in 2024, but the midfielder could be on the move again

View 2 Images Scott McTominay is yet to agree new terms with Napoli

Manchester United's decision to sell Scott McTominay is back under the microscope as speculation surrounds future at Napoli. The midfielder has been linked with a return to the Premier League - with Real Madrid now said to be enquiring about his availability.

‌



‌



McTominay departed United in the summer of 2024 to join Napoli in a permanent transfer worth £25.9million (€30.5million). The Scotland international has since become a crucial figure in midfield for the Italian outfit.

‌



He played a key role as Napoli secured the Serie A title in his first season in Naples, with the club finishing runners-up to Inter Milan last term. Despite appearing content and continuing to be a vital player for Napoli, rumours surrounding McTominay's future have sparked suggestions of a possible exit in the coming months.

‌



Sky Sports announce big change to Man Utd vs Tottenham coverage READ MORE :

Man Utd star may need surgery after latest injury setback causes Michael Carrick headache READ MORE :

McTominay is understood to be embroiled in a contract stand-off with Napoli, raising the prospect of a January departure if the two sides fail to reach an agreement.

Italian publication Tutto Mercato suggests there is 'danger' that an exit 'could become more and more concrete.' Real Madrid are reported to have made enquiries to assess the situation, while additional interest could emerge from the Premier League.

Napoli are believed to be eager to postpone any potential sale until the summer, but it remains unclear whether they can retain McTominay when the transfer window reopens in January.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Reports have suggested that McTominay is 'open' to the prospect of making a return to the Premier League.

The midfielder spent 22 years at Old Trafford having come through Manchester United's youth system.

‌



Meanwhile, Sky Sports previously reported that United had 'enquired' about the possibility of bringing McTominay back to the club, with Aston Villa also understood to be keen.

The report added that the midfielder's representatives remain in dialogue with 'several' Premier League sides, though it is not clear whether United are amongst them.

Should McTominay depart Napoli for another club in the coming months , United stand to gain financially, as long as the switch is not a return to Old Trafford.

‌



View 2 Images McTominay in action for Napoli

The club secured a sell-on clause as part of the midfielder's move to Italy in 2024.

Under the terms of that deal, United are due 10% of any future transfer fee. That could result in a substantial windfall, with the 29-year-old having boosted his standing through his displays for club and country in recent seasons.

Sports.title: Ten-man Spurs claim dramatic draw at Man Utd as Solanke rescues point
Sports.content:
Tottenham rescued an unlikely point at Manchester United after fighting back to draw 1-1 with 10 men - but their search for a Premier League win extends into another week.

The point at least lifts Spurs off the foot of the table but Roberto De Zerbi's side remain marooned in the relegation zone, without a league victory since May.

Their predicament can be summed up by three cases of extreme wastefulness and one of ill-discipline, with Dominic Solanke particularly guilty of spurning the chances that might have seen his side take a comfortable first-half lead.

Instead, it was Bryan Mbeumo who broke the deadlock in the 73rd minute, combining with Matheus Cunha in the box and turning smartly to guide a clinical finish across Antonin Kinsky.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mbeumo fired Manchester United ahead

Spurs spent most of the game in the ascendancy but were hurtling towards their fourth loss of an already chaotic campaign, made worse by a moment of madness from Rodrigo Bentancur, who saw red for a headbutt motion towards Luke Shaw five minutes after the goal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rodrigo Bentancur saw red for a headbutt on Luke Shaw

De Zerbi's mission looked hopeless. But Spurs did not give up, and were rewarded with a leveller in stoppage time when Solanke glanced a header past a static Senne Lammens.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Solanke snatched a late equaliser

Neither manager will be happy with the outcome. Man Utd are stuck in the midst of their worst start to a season for 40 years, while Spurs' plight is more damning still. After the points were shared, it's perhaps a result that leaves more questions than answers for both.

Sports.title: Hits & Misses: Blues ready to attack key run of games as Madueke shines in new role
Sports.content:
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Chelsea and Bournemouth.

Chelsea's season is set to be shaped by the run of games they have before the November international break. After a mixed start to Xabi Alonso's reign, he is in need of a strong run in the Premier League to boost the bid to return to Champions League football, while a Carabao Cup tie at Liverpool could be a launchpad for early silverware.

His Chelsea side showed how they're going to go about it on Saturday, blowing away Bournemouth with their attacking power.

Joao Pedro is fit again and still firing. Cole Palmer was classy and looks recovered from the issue which forced him out of England duty and buoyed by a new Chelsea contract. Morgan Rogers is in form and connecting with both in style. And a certain Jordan Henderson has developed an ability to crack in stunning goals.

Chelsea's next fixtures (PL unless stated) Everton (a), Spurs (h), Liverpool in Carabao Cup (a), Man Utd (h), Sunderland (a).

Moises Caicedo's first start brought extra punch in midfield. There was, though, some nervousness when Bournemouth bundled one back, such has been Chelsea's poor defensive record this season. But while Alonso was preparing a double change to intervene, Chelsea scored two more. That looks like it will be their way for now, as they aim to blast their way into a position to push for success this season.

Peter Smith

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Arsenal and Leeds United.

Noni Madueke can be a frustrating player to watch at times. Arsenal and Chelsea fans have seen it. England fans witnessed it at the World Cup. Even Mikel Arteta feels it.

"When I haven't liked so much what he was doing or it wasn't impacting the game, I made certain decisions, he has accepted them," the Arsenal manager said. But this was a display where Madueke shone - and led the way - in a slightly different role.

Madueke lined up on the left wing for Arsenal against Leeds. He has only started two games for the Gunners in that position - the first came 14 months ago in the 5-0 win over Leeds. That was his full Arsenal debut.

But with Christos Tzolis injured, Arsenal have been a bit short at left wing. Many expected Eberechi Eze to fill in - but Madueke got the nod and as Arteta said: "He took his chance."

Image: Noni Madueke impressed at left wing

Madueke was Arsenal's best forward player on the day, creating three chances - that Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard should put away.

He then played a big role in the equaliser, with his right-footed cross finding Ben White at the back post, who then set up Riccardo Calafiori.

Madueke was the only Arsenal player to complete a cross against Leeds - and he completed five crosses from six attempts. He was making things happen - he has been doing it for a while in front of Arteta.

"What he's done is raise the level. And in training he's been the best player in the last 10 days. You could see that every time he was in and around the ball he looked a threat."

Like other signings last season, including Viktor Gyokeres and Martin Zubimendi, Madueke's Arsenal career was at risk of stalling. Has he now found a second wind in a new position?

Sam Blitz

It is a mark of the progress Leeds United have made that Daniel Farke was heartbroken to leave the home of the Premier League champions empty-handed.

Last season, they lost four and five-nil to Arsenal. At the Emirates on Saturday, Leeds were comfortably the better side for nearly an hour, limiting Arsenal to just five shots before James Justin fired Farke's side ahead after 55 minutes.

In the immediate aftermath of their opener, Leeds kept pushing and Dominic Calvert-Lewin was a whisker away from doubling the advantage from Jayden Bogle's cross. If that goes in, we might be talking about a completely different outcome.

Farke set Leeds up to go for it at Arsenal, spurred on by Brighton's blueprint before the international break, and he was nearly rewarded for his ambition. The unbeaten run might be over, but Leeds can keep looking up. They should be considered European contenders.

Zinny Boswell

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Ipswich Town and Fulham.

Alvaro Arbeloa is going to have to learn quickly if he is to survive the Premier League.

Ipswich's 2-1 victory over Fulham was a painful reminder that managing at the highest level is about more than having a tactical plan. It is about understanding the physical demands of this league, recognising the momentum shifts and knowing when to make the right substitutions.

Fulham's decision to retreat in the closing stages was almost Thomas Tuchel-esque in England's approach against Argentina. The invitation was there for Ipswich to pile on the pressure, and they duly obliged, scoring twice late on to turn the game around. Just like Argentina did.

Bringing on the lightweight Manuel Ángel for a Premier League debut felt like a gamble at precisely the wrong moment. With Ipswich turning the contest into a physical battle, Fulham needed players capable of matching that intensity, winning second balls and relieving the pressure.

Instead, Ipswich's power and directness came to the fore when it mattered most.

Lewis Jones

"At Villa Park, we have played three matches and we did not win until now," said Unai Emery after seeing his side held by Kristoffer Ajer's goal that earned Brentford their 2-2 draw. This place was once a fortress but it is proving trickier for a much-changed squad.

There will be patience with the players, particularly given that Nicolas Jackson, scorer of Aston Villa's opening goal, has made a promising start and there is such excitement about the potential of talented new signings like Johan Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye.

But could the empty North Stand be another factor in their home form too? Villa Park feels unusually open with no supporters there and the Brentford supporters were likening the atmosphere to that of a library right from the early stages of the contest.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Aston Villa’s match against Brentford in the Premier League

"It just feels wrong, doesn't it? I don't know what it is," said Bees boss Keith Andrews. "I have got a little bit of OCD, so maybe it's that, if there's a whole stand missing it doesn't quite sit well with me. Naturally, it's not going to generate the type of atmosphere.

"I have to say, I love coming here. When I was growing up as a kid, some Irish legends played here, Ray Houghton, Paul McGrath, Andy Townsend, so it's always been a special place for me and you can feel the history of it. With a stand missing, it is a bit different."

Emery has been sanguine about the situation publicly, accepting that it is one step back to take two forwards by increasing the capacity. But Villa Park is less claustrophobic for its visitors right now and that is far from ideal for a club so reliant on its home form.

Adam Bate

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Sunderland’s match against Brighton in the Premier League.

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris will be praying Brian Brobbey's hamstring injury is not too serious after his side drew a blank against the 10 men of Brighton at the Stadium of Light.

The striker, who scored a brilliant hat-trick in the Black Cats' previous outing at Manchester City, picked up the knock while recently on international duty with the Netherlands, meaning a first Premier League start of the season for Wilson Isidor.

The Haiti international nearly gave the hosts an early lead when his sliding opportunity was deflected, while after the break he was involved in Pascal Struijk's dismissal, having been brought down by the Brighton defender while through on goal.

However, Isidor was unable to find the net, meaning Sunderland have now lost back-to-back league games on Wearside without scoring for the first time since April/May 2017 as they slipped to 16th in the table.

Rich Morgan

Sports.title: Man Utd fans take aim at Man City with return of famous ticker banner
Sports.content:
Man Utd fans' famous banner mocking the years since Man City won a trophy returned to Old Trafford on Saturday; United were playing first game since City were found guilty of all serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission

Man City charges: Manchester United fans take aim at rivals with return of famous ticker banner

The banner displays 50 years - ticking over to 51 years - since Man City won the 1976 League Cup

Manchester United's famous ticker banner returned to Old Trafford on Saturday, displaying 50 years since Manchester City won a trophy.

The banner was first displayed in 2000, at which point it was 24 years since City last won a trophy - the 1976 League Cup.

The year listed on the banner ticked over every year until 2011, when City ended their trophy drought by beating Stoke in the FA Cup final - their first silverware since Sheikh Mansour's takeover.

Image: The banner was on display before supporters filled Old Trafford ahead of the game against Tottenham

But after City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission, United fans took aim at their rivals by displaying a new version of the banner for the visit of Tottenham.

It marks 50 years since City won the 1976 League Cup, therefore discounting the eight Premier Leagues, four FA Cups, seven League Cups, four Community Shields, one Champions League, one Super Cup and one Club World Cup they have won since the takeover.

City deny wrongdoing and lodged an appeal against the commission's findings. The commission's findings specifically related to the period between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons.

United fans also displayed a banner of Rui Pinto with the caption 'computer genius'. Pinto is a convicted hacker who obtained emails that formed the basis of articles published by Der Spiegel in 2018 that first alleged financial breaches by City.

United's game against Tottenham was their first since the news of the independent commission's judgement was revealed.

City play for the first time since the news broke on Sunday, away to Liverpool, live on Sky Sports.

On Friday, City boss Enzo Maresca insisted his club are "going to win" their appeal.

Sports.title: Former delivery driver Dean tied with Forrest for lead at Open de Espana
Sports.content:
England's Joe Dean and Scotland's Grant Forrest share a one-shot lead going into the final round of the Open de Espana in Madrid.

Forrest began the day with a one-shot advantage at the Real Club de Campo Villa de Madrid but slipped down the leaderboard after bogeying the fifth hole.

However, birdies at the 11th, 14th and 16th gave the Scot a four-under-par round of 67 and a total of 13 under.

Forrest, who is searching for his third DP World Tour title, said on europeantour.com: "I'm happy with how I handled today.

"I didn't have my best stuff but I'm really proud of how I dug in and made some nice putts, a couple of good recovery shots, and all in all a decent score again.

"This is one of my favourite tournaments, it's been good to me in the past, and I'd love nothing more than to go home with a trophy tomorrow."

His round was enough to leave him tied for the lead alongside Sheffield's Dean, who will feel he should have produced an even better outcome than the 65 he signed for.

Dean, a former delivery driver, who secured his maiden victory on the European-based circuit at the British Masters, followed five birdies on the front nine with three more at the 12th, 14th and 15th to open up a three-shot lead.

But the 32-year-old then double-bogeyed the 16th and dropped another shot at 17 before finishing on a high with a 31-foot putt for birdie on the last.

"It gave a little bit of hope after those previous two holes," said Dean. "We'll go again and see what happens."

France's Victor Perez and Dane Jacob Skov Olesen both also posted rounds of 65 to move to 12 under, one shot off the lead, alongside Joel Girrbach of Switzerland, who was round in 67.

Angel Ayora is the leading Spanish hope and he sits three shots off the lead after a 66 on a day of low scoring.

Shane Lowry produced his best round of the week with a four-under 67 boosting him into a tie for 17th but still trails by eight shots.

Sports.title: Northampton beat Bath in chaotic 18-try, 119-point classic
Sports.content:
Northampton Saints ran riot to defeat Bath 71-48 in the second highest-scoring Gallagher Prem game in history.

Eighteen tries were scored in total, with Saints bouncing back from defeat at Bristol Bears last week in spectacular style.

Ollie Sleightholme scored a hat-trick in an astonishing afternoon at Franklin's Gardens in which 119 points were scored.

"We put our game on the pitch," Sleightholme said on TNT Sports. "We don't want to concede that many points, so we've got stuff to work on.

"It's wicked [to play in this team]. We know we're going to create opportunities. We capitalised on the ones that we got.

"It was very loud. I haven't heard it like this for a while. It's great to be back."

Saints are also at the centre of the highest-scoring game in Prem history when they scored 14 tries to humiliate Bristol Bears 94-33 at Franklin's Gardens in May.

The total of 127 points meant it was the highest-scoring game in the history of English top-flight rugby union, beating the previous record of 118 in Richmond's 106-12 win over Bedford in 1999.

Northampton struck first after seven minutes when Fin Smith glided through a gap for the opener, which he could not convert.

Bath's response was excellent and swift as Finn Russell's off-load sent Arthur Green into space, with his pass inside giving Tom Carr-Smith an easy finish and Russell a simple conversion.

The visitors were over again three minutes later following a tapped penalty as Carr-Smith whipped a pass left for Charlie Griffin to finish in the corner, with Russell converting brilliantly.

The Saints were quickly back in business, though, as some wonderful quick hands led to Tommy Freeman off-loading to James Pater, whose long pass put Sleightholme in the clear, Smith's conversion making it a two-point game.

After Bath had Josh Bayliss sin-binned for killing the ball close to his own line, Northampton took the lead when Smith's pass put Freeman under the posts.

Despite being down to 14 men, Bath hit back hard again as they levelled at 19-19 when tighthead Archie Griffin barged his way over from close range down the right.

And they led when Kepu Tuipulotu broke through some flimsy tackling before putting Green in the clear, although Saints soon squared proceedings once more when their captain, Fraser Dingwall, glided through.

Russell's penalty with the final kick of a breathless first half had Bath 29-26 ahead at the break, and they extended their lead within two minutes of the restart when Carr-Smith set up Green's second of the afternoon.

Saints were momentarily back within three points when Pater ran in after Santi Carreras fumbled Russell's pass, but the Argentinian soon made amends when Russell's looping ball gave him a walk-in.

Back came Northampton again when Josh Kemeny scored in the corner from Alex Coles' pass to make it a dozen tries shared between the two teams in 51 minutes.

And Saints led again when Alex Mitchell scored a lovely individual try by collecting his own kick ahead before Sleightholme's second score brought up 50 points for the hosts.

There was just no let-up as Sleightholme ran in under the posts to complete his hat-trick, with Bayliss pulling a score back for Bath before Smith's strong carry allowed Coles to get in on the act.

There was time for one more try as more quick hands from Rory Hutchinson and Anthony Belleau put Freeman in for his second, and Northampton's 11th, of an extraordinary afternoon.

Dowson: High-scoring clash due to 'different mindset'

Image: Phil Dowson says high-scoring matches are due to teams shifting in mindset

Saints director of rugby Phil Dowson thinks high-scoring matches is due to teams shifting in mindset in recent years.

Dowson said: "There have been some rule changes from a kicking point of view that's opened the game up and the best ball to play off is broken field, counter-attack turnover ball. You get a lot more of that.

"I think the ability of teams now - all teams - have an appetite to move the ball on the counter attack first before kicking first, so I think there's a different mindset.

"I think risk is being rewarded more often and there's the actual skill level of the playing group.

"You can talk about the underfoot conditions, the way it's being refereed, all that sort of stuff, you're still seeing tons of turnover at the breakdown.

"We don't want it to be 99-88 - not basketball, and I hear that in the media from some coaches - but we also don't want 9-3, so we've got to find a balance in how we run the game.

"But at the moment there are lots of Saints fans happy."

Sports.title: Five-star Hearts thrash St Mirren for biggest home win since 2023
Sports.content:
Hearts eased to their biggest home win in the Scottish Premiership for three-and-a-half years as they dismantled meek St Mirren 5-0 to remain on the coat-tails of Rangers and Celtic.

The third-placed Jambos dominated from the start and rarely looked in any danger from the moment Laurent Mendy fired them ahead in the 20th minute.

Calvin Miller then notched two penalties, either side of half-time, before further goals from Claudio Braga and Josh McPake ensured a smooth afternoon for Wouter Vrancken's side ahead of their Conference League opener at home to Nordsjaelland on Thursday.

It was Hearts' biggest league win at Tynecastle since they defeated Ross County 6-1 under Steven Naismith in April 2023, and they are now comfortably the top scorers in the league. Saints, by contrast, left Edinburgh licking their wounds after a fourth defeat in succession.

Hearts started brightly, with Harry Milne, Miller and McPake - buoyed by making his Scotland debut against Slovenia on Tuesday - all threatening early on.

Saints were offering little, although Killian Phillips tried to catch Beau Reus out with a lob from the centre circle after a misplaced pass from James Wilson.

A minute later Milne went clean through but saw his shot pushed over by Buddies keeper Jacob Chapman.

Hearts made a deserved breakthrough in the 19th minute. Miller floated a free-kick into the box and Mendy got his header all wrong, sending it back the way, but Saints' Chris Mochrie inadvertently knocked it back to the former Forest Green midfielder, who pounced to lash a powerful finish, on the bounce, high past Chapman from 12 yards out.

The visitors were bedraggled, unable to generate any rhythm, and they fell further behind in the 32nd minute. McPake was tripped by Alex Gogic as he burst into the box, and Miller duly sent Chapman the wrong way from the spot.

Having seen his team outplayed in the first half, McLeish made a triple change for the start of the second half. But the first notable involvement of one of those substitutes, Liam Donnelly, was to give away a penalty for tripping Wilson in the box, and Miller stepped up to convert his second spot-kick in the 50th minute.

Image: Hearts' Calvin Miller (L) scored twice from the penalty spot

Miller turned provider four minutes later as his nicely weighted pass released Braga, who rounded Chapman before slotting home despite the efforts of two Saints defenders to get back and clear.

After Reus made a brilliant save to deny Calvin Ramsay, the outstanding McPake got himself clear in the box to fire past the exposed Chapman from eight yards in the 80th minute.

What the managers said...

Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken:

"From the first session (in the summer), the players liked what we were doing and they tried to make those steps and you see it today that they are trying to do it and succeeding.

"We try to play a kind of football that is positive and constructive and proactive, and not a reaction.

"I think people come to the stadium to see nice football, to see goals from your side.

"Also for the players, we try to play a style of football that, when you were a little boy, when you started playing football on the street, you played football to score goals, not to stay in front of your goal and prevent the goals.

"You want to score goals because this is the nicest feeling you have in football.

"We are trying to play a type of football where we can come in the positions as much as possible to get this feeling. Some days it will work better than other days, but it's nice to see that it worked well today.

"It's good for the guys that they have such a game where they felt comfortable on the ball. Also out of possession we were good. Hopefully it gives us more confidence for this run of games."

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish:

"It's not good enough from our point of view. We shot ourselves in the foot and gave away two penalties which are avoidable.

"There were individual errors for the other three and that's not to take anything away from Hearts, who were excellent.

"You can't come to places like this and expect to play football from the first minute, you have to earn that right. You have to fight and out-run teams and we didn't do that at points.

"It's not an excuse but we lost Niko Agrafiotis in the warm-up and he's a big part of what we're trying to do. We had to shuffle things around and it didn't quite happen for us.

"We all have to take responsibility. I have to rectify it."

Sports.title: Can Ferraris work together to beat Verstappen at Singapore GP?
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari will do "whatever it takes" as a team to beat Max Verstappen in Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix.

Verstappen will start on pole for the second weekend in a row with Charles Leclerc on the front row and Hamilton in behind in third, with all three drivers desperate to win their second races of 2026.

The tight confines of the Marina Bay Street Circuit means overtaking is difficult so the start will be crucial when the lights go out at 1pm (build-up from 11.30am), live on Sky Sports F1.

"As a team we need to do whatever it takes to win," Hamilton told Sky Sports F1.

"The start in the Sprint was in the wet so it was different. But I believe from third we can have a good start. I will try to capitalise there and after that I think we have a car we can fight with.

"I will give it absolutely everything to try and undo our qualifying. It would be great for us to get another win."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix Sprint

Having topped Q1 and Q2 in Qualifying, Hamilton headed into Q3 as favourite but could not put a completely clean lap together so was beaten by Verstappen and Leclerc by just one tenth.

"The car felt amazing in Q1 and Q2, and when I finished the laps, I was like, 'she's got more in her'. And the only way in order to try and extract that is to try and add wing," he explained.

"In doing so, I think it just tipped it over the edge. It was only like one hole or something like that, but it was just on the knife point, and after that then the car was just snappy, and none of the laps in Q3 are any good. So I'm grateful to be third, to be honest, given that those laps weren't very good."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton remained optimistic about the Singapore GP despite missing out on pole to Red Bull's Max Verstappen

How vulnerable is Verstappen at the start?

Verstappen is concerned about the start after a "horrendous" launch in Saturday's Singapore Sprint which saw him lose out to George Russell before the Mercedes driver crashed at the end of the lap.

It was reminiscent of last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, but both starts were in the wet and Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix is expected to be dry.

However, even Verstappen's most recent starts have not been good in comparison to his rivals. Although he did not lose positions by the end of the first lap in the last three dry starts in Baku, Madrid and Monza, his initial getaway off the line was, at best, average in all three Grands Prix and he was forced to fight hard into Turn 1 itself to retain his starting position.

Given the first corner in Singapore does not require the drivers to brake hard, Verstappen will not be able to recover from a poor getaway on Sunday, particularly if the Ferraris start quickly.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell holds onto the lead on the opening lap of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix

"That's definitely something that we need to improve on because if you have something like that tomorrow, that's your race over if nothing crazy happens," said Verstappen, who will make his 250th F1 start.

"We have a few limitations that we have to work on. Also from our side, I think we have to do a better job, because Racing Bulls sometimes do start better than us. So we just need to be better."

Leclerc and Hamilton themselves will be itching to get away cleanly and will be aware of the importance to be the leading Ferrari after the first lap.

It might mean the two Ferraris get very close on the short run down to Turn 1 and both drivers are likely to be unwilling to back out...

Singapore GP Starting Grid: Top 10 1) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



2) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



3) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



4) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



5) Lando Norris, McLaren



6) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



7) Pierre Gasly, Alpine



8) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



9) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls



10) Nico Hulkenberg, Audi

What can happen after the start in Singapore?

The high Singapore track temperatures coupled with several traction zones mean tyre degradation can be an issue during the long race, which often can get close to the two-hour limit due to the relatively low average speed.

However, the drivers have learned, if they manage their pace, you can stretch the first stint length to make a one-stop race work.

"In terms of strategy we will have to look, but it's also true whoever is behind after the first lap, if that happens, the second car can lose a lot - whether that's Lewis or me," Leclerc told Sky Sports F1.

"That's a team choice and something we will discuss. If a win is on the table we will have to take a decision. But we will talk about it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen claims pole with Charles Leclerc in P2 and team-mate Lewis Hamilton in P3 ahead of the Singapore Grand Prix

Leclerc is suggesting the second Ferrari will need to try something different, or perhaps even sacrifice themselves by helping the other car.

The two options the second Ferrari would have is to pit relatively early to try and undercut Verstappen, if needed, allowing the leading car to have free air. Or to run long and hope for a timely Safety Car or Virtual Safety Car to make a 'cheaper' pit stop where you lose less time in the pits compared to pitting under green flag conditions.

"It will be very hard for us to beat Max tomorrow, but there's two Ferraris there and I think we can hopefully, there might be opportunities for us to work together to try and apply the pressure," said Hamilton.

"They [Red Bull] are very quick but I think we have the car in a good place that hopefully we can at least hold on."
