Sports.title: Manchester United 1-1 Tottenham: Premier League – live reaction
Sports.content:
3m ago 14.47 EDT Spurs starting captain – and injury-time goalscoring hero – Dominic Solanke speaks to Sky Sports. “We dominated … was on top throughout the first half … we wasn’t clinical enough … the story of the season so far … to get a point in the end, we’ll take it … the character shown from the team today was magnificent … a few times last season when we went a goal down, we didn’t react in the right way … but today we showed so much fire and grit … the mentality we want to show in every game … I probably should have had a hat-trick today … I really wanted to get a goal … I showed great fight [for the equaliser] … a deft touch into the far corner … so happy … I wanted to make up for the missed chances I had and I’m grateful I did that … [starting the game as captain] is something I’ll remember for the rest of my career … [the result] is something to build on … we’re so close … we just need a little spark and everything will click … hopefully this is the start of something good.” Share

9m ago 14.41 EDT Post-match postbag (red-card brouhaha edition). “If there was a case for an infra-red card, then Bentancur would have one - completely out of control on Fernandes, followed by the violent conduct on Shaw. However, Shaw should probably have gone too - deservedly booked for the push, but that fall when Betancur lightly touched his forehead was worthy of Olivier” – Andy (not that one) Flintoff “I get the red card for Spurs. But Shaw kicked it off by shoving him of the pitch” – Mary Waltz “Shaw deserved two yellows: 1. Push. 2. Simulation. It’s not not simulation because the opponent leaned forward first. Shaw responded in kind by leaning forward himself to draw contact — without which there’s no foul” – Mike Chiropolos “It’s come to something when Lisandro Martinez is the calming influence” – Adam Roberts Share

13m ago 14.37 EDT Post-match postbag (red-card brouhaha aside). “There was an awful lot of talk about Baleba needing to take control of United’s failing midfield. I know it’s early days yet but he certainly did that since he came on. He lifted everyone around him, and the crowd too. Quite the debut!” – Justin Kavanagh “Perhaps United fans will explain but I’m quite baffled by the fuss around Mainoo. Clearly, Tielemans was struggling today but that moment when him and Mainoo appeared to be struggling to run back seemed amazing for such a young player. Or could he just not be bothered?” – Stephen McCrossan “Have any of the people on the pitch ever actually played, or even seen, a game of football before? I ask because the overwhelming evidence, after some 68 minutes of gametime, is that they haven’t” – Jim Morrish “I’m not watching the game, but the phrase ‘two bald men fighting over a comb’ springs to mind” – Simon McMahon “Disappointing result for the neutrals. United in a relegation battle still retains comedy value, but with Spurs it just feels routine these days” – Tim Woods “Both teams deserved to lose. What Man City did to football in reality, Utd and Spurs have done aesthetically” – David Scahill Share

18m ago 14.32 EDT A point is the least Tottenham deserved. They were much the better side for the most part, carving out a series of big chances that they butchered in an impressively wide range of styles. So from their point of view, they’ll wonder how on earth they didn’t come away with all three points. But two things can be true at once, and Manchester United will be asking themselves exactly the same question. Having clung on, then made the breakthrough, their reward for an improved second-half showing, how did they fail to get over the line against ten men? The final xG of 0.77 to 1.56 suggests Spurs will be the more frustrated, but in truth it’s one of those games where neither team will be pleased, but both will be relieved, for differing reasons, not to have lost. Manchester United remain in 12th spot, while Tottenham Hotspur peel themselves off the bottom. Share Updated at 14.38 EDT

24m ago 14.27 EDT FULL TIME: Manchester United 1-1 Tottenham Hotspur The whistle goes. Another smattering of boos for the home side, but not half as loud as the ones that met them at the break. Share

25m ago 14.26 EDT 90 min +9: Baleba lashes another long-range shot over the bar. That should be about that. Share

25m ago 14.25 EDT 90 min +8: Gray rugby-tackles Heaven, and the referee’s card pops up, toaster-style, once again. Share

26m ago 14.24 EDT 90 min +7: Fernandes takes the Tottenham free kick, but it’s no good. Share

27m ago 14.23 EDT 90 min +6: Tonali prepares to bust into space down the inside-left channel, only to be clipped late by Dalot, who goes into the book. A free kick. All of Tottenham’s big men go up for the set piece. Share

28m ago 14.22 EDT 90 min +5: A double change for United, who send on Heaven and Rashford for Cunha and Shaw. Share

29m ago 14.21 EDT 90 min +4: United had looked suddenly shaky since the announcement of eight additional minutes, and paid the price. Maguire tries to reply with a fierce drive that warms Kinsky’s palms. Neither team looks in the mood to declare. Share

31m ago 14.20 EDT GOAL! Manchester United 1-1 Tottenham Hotspur (Solanke 90+2) A slow-motion equaliser! Tonali clips a cross in from the left-hand edge of the United box. Solanke wrestles with Martinez, eight yards out, and wins the tussle, flicking a header across Lammens and into the bottom right! View image in fullscreen Dominic Solanke heads the ball into the net to put Spurs level. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA View image in fullscreen Solanke celebrates scoring Tottenham Hotspur’s equaliser with teammates Savio and Archie Gray. Photograph: Jan Kruger/Getty Images Share Updated at 14.27 EDT

33m ago 14.18 EDT 90 min: Dalot is sent into space on the overlap down the right. He cuts back for Cunha, who shoots towards the bottom right. Van Hecke slides in to block, and Kinsky claims. Cunha claims a handball, but that’s never going to be given. There will be eight additional minutes, Share

35m ago 14.16 EDT 89 min: Senesi comes on for Fernandes. One of United’s failed summer transfer targets is booed in the pantomime style upon his arrival. Share

36m ago 14.14 EDT 87 min: Maddison prepares to advance down the left when Martinez slides in late. Another yellow card. Suffice to say this game continues to putter away on the stove, ready to spill over at any moment. Share

38m ago 14.13 EDT 85 min: Baleba sends a clever long pass down the United right. Mbeumo beats Senesi in a foot race, and shoots from the edge of the box. Kinsky parries around the right-hand post. Share

39m ago 14.11 EDT 83 min: Fernandes lands on Van Hecke’s achilles. It’s not a great challenge, and he’s booked. The Spurs players want more, but they’re not getting their wish. Share

40m ago 14.10 EDT 82 min: Shaw’s reaction amid all of that wasn’t great … but then he’s been on the end of a dreadful tackle before, and at great and lengthy cost, so you can perhaps understand how his buttons were pressed. Share

42m ago 14.08 EDT 80 min: In the dugout, De Zerbi sits quietly seething. How have his team got themselves into this mess? Share

43m ago 14.07 EDT RED CARD: Bentancur (Tottenham Hotspur) 78 min: It’s red for Bentancur. Yellows for Van Hecke and Shaw. That escalated in super-fast time. Old Trafford really bubbling now! View image in fullscreen What’s that for ref? Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP Share Updated at 14.21 EDT

46m ago 14.05 EDT 77 min: It all kicks off! Van Hecke crashes into Fernandes. Bentancur then scissor-tackles Shaw, missing his man by inches. He’s about to get booked when Shaw comes back at his man and shoves him hard in the chest, and off the pitch. Bentancur springs up and reacts with a butt. Cue an old-school bench-emptying melee on the touchline! View image in fullscreen Rodrigo Bentancur of Tottenham Hotspur scissor-tackles Luke Shaw of Manchester United. Photograph: James Gill/Danehouse/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Bentancur (left) butts Luke Shaw. Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP View image in fullscreen Stop, melee time. Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at 14.22 EDT

47m ago 14.03 EDT 76 min: Spurs are up against it now all right, because they haven’t won in the Premier League after conceding first for 48 games. Everton and Leeds are next with nine! Share

48m ago 14.02 EDT 74 min: Spurs respond by sending on Maddison and Van de Ven. Udogie and Gallagher make way. Share

50m ago 14.01 EDT GOAL! Manchester United 1-0 Tottenham Hotspur (Mbeumo 73) United have been second best for the majority of this match, but now look! Cunha probes down the left and cuts back for Mbeumo, who isn’t closed down by Van Hecke. He’s got just enough time and space to turn and thread a shot across Kinsky and into the bottom right! Lads, it’s the same old story. View image in fullscreen Bryan Mbeumo shoots … Photograph: Alex Livesey/Getty Images View image in fullscreen And watches as his shot heads towards the Tottenham net. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters View image in fullscreen Mbeumo (left) celebrates with Matheus Cunha. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters Share Updated at 14.31 EDT

51m ago 13.59 EDT 72 min: Maguire takes a whack from 25 yards. Blocked. A bit early to get this desperate, surely, though it worked against Ipswich I guess. Share

52m ago 13.58 EDT 71 min: Gallagher busies himself down the right, released into a little space by Savio’s cute pass. But the eventual cross is no good. Share

53m ago 13.57 EDT 69 min: United do their best to tee up Spurs a couple of times, Fernandes, Shaw and Maguire failing to clear the ball under pressure in a slapstick sequence. Eventually Savio shoots from the right-hand edge of the box; Mainoo extends to deflect over the bar. Nothing comes of the resulting corner. How is this game still goalless? Answer: Ineptitude of attackers > ineptitude of defenders. Share

1h ago 13.54 EDT 67 min: Spurs respond to the United triple change with a double of their own. Bergvall and Kudus make way for Bentancur and Marmoush. Share

1h ago 13.54 EDT 65 min: Spurs waste another chance. Senesi slides a pass down the left. Tonali flicks it on, and Udogie is clear in the box! Udogie tries a fancy outside-of-foot shot across Lammens, aiming for the bottom right … and sends the ball bouncing apologetically wide. The offside flag goes up to give him a little succour. View image in fullscreen Tottenham's Destiny Udogie fires a shot past Manchester United's goalkeeper Senne Lammens but wide of the goal. Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP Share Updated at 14.02 EDT

1h ago 13.50 EDT 63 min: Dalot crosses from the right. Fernandes stoops to head, but can’t connect. Goal kick. Then seconds later, Fernandes slices a shot from the right-hand corner of the Spurs box well wide. But Old Trafford is suddenly energised. Share

1h ago 13.49 EDT 62 min: Fernandes gracefully wedges the free kick over the wall, the ball dropping to Zirkzee who wins a corner, from which Baleba skies his first shot in a Manchester United shirt. Goal kick. View image in fullscreen Tottenham Hotspur's Dominic Solanke (left), Marcos Senesi (centre) and Jan Paul van Hecke fail to block Bruno Fernandes’ free kick. Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at 13.55 EDT

1h ago 13.48 EDT 61 min: The triple-sub energises the crowd, and United surge forward. Cunha advances down the inside-left channel and feels Kudus’s hand on his shoulder. He needs no second invitation to go down and buy a cheap free kick, just to the left of the D. Bruno Country. Share

1h ago 13.47 EDT 59 min: United deal with the second corner easily enough, and here come the replacements. Zirkzee, Dalot and the debutant Baleba replacing Yoro, Tielemans and Diallo. Share

1h ago 13.45 EDT 58 min: The corner’s hit long from the left. Van Hecke wins a header past the far stick, sending the ball back across the face of goal. Maguire is forced to eyebrow over his own bar for another corner. Share

1h ago 13.45 EDT 57 min: Savio runs at the United defence but can’t make a decision. United take over, and Fernandes nearly releases Mbeumo down the right. Goal kick. Spurs then counter the counter, and Savio’s low drive from the left is deflected wide left. Michael Carrick prepares a triple sub, but before that, here comes the corner. Share

1h ago 13.43 EDT 55 min: Gray shepherds the ball out of play down the left, under pressure from Cunha. But then Cunha slide-hooks the ball back into the path of Tielemans, who calmly passes into the bottom-right corner of the net! But then the flag goes up, the ball having been clearly out of play before Cunha’s intervention. Share

Sports.title: Henderson and João Pedro lead Chelsea charge against Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Watch and learn, kids. The day began with one for the youth audience, Cole Palmer appearing on a live stream to explain the thinking behind his latest contract extension. It finished with the oldest player to join Chelsea during the BlueCo era stealing the show with an all-action midfield display.

Even Palmer was happy to step aside as Jordan Henderson used his right foot to curl home a free-kick that drew comparisons with one of David Beckham’s specials. It was Henderson’s second spectacular strike – he marked his home debut by opening the scoring with a bending effort from 20 yards and also laid on an assist for Morgan Rogers to make it 2-0 – although it is fair to assume that Xabi Alonso did not bring the veteran to Stamford Bridge for his goalscoring prowess.

The idea was more to lift standards in the dressing room. Chelsea needed experience and are surely better off now a 36-year-old starting for them in midfield is no longer a laughable notion.

“We signed him for everything,” Alonso said of Henderson. “If he’s able to score two beauties as today, we are more than happy for him. But apart from the goals he’s done many good things. He’s always involved in the action, always giving solutions to teammates.”

Henderson set the tone for Chelsea, driving into tackles and raising the tempo with the urgency of his passing. He joined from Brentford in the summer and is keen to do more than make up the numbers. Chelsea, up to fifth after their first win in four league games, were more stable with Henderson alongside Moisés Caicedo, who lasted 72 minutes on his long-awaited return from a calf injury.

Alonso, who was without Reece James after the captain picked up a knee injury in training on Friday, was still disappointed his side have now gone 22 league games without a clean sheet. They were 3-0 up when Evanilson pulled a goal back for Bournemouth, who are finding the transition from Andoni Iraola to Marco Rose trickier than anticipated and must manage games better.

View image in fullscreen Moisés Caicedo (left) returned to the Chelsea team after a spell on the sidelines due to injury. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Even so, Alonso was pleased with Chelsea’s level. They have scored in the first 10 minutes in five of their six league games this season and are a match for anyone when the front three of Palmer, Rogers and João Pedro take full flight.

Palmer had a point to prove after having his desire to play for England questioned by Thomas Tuchel last month. His impact was immediate, although it owed much to Bournemouth’s naivety. The visitors lined up in a flat 4-4-2 formation and gave Palmer far too much space when he sauntered down the right in the first minute.

It was encouraging to see Palmer moving freely, especially after Alonso’s admission that the playmaker’s decision to sit out the international break was related to last season’s groin pain, but Bournemouth were a soft touch. There was no challenge on the 24-year-old, who has displayed his commitment to Chelsea by signing on until 2034.

Palmer floated into the area, turned and rolled the ball to Henderson, who hit it first time with the inside of his right foot and saw his bending effort go in off the inside of the right post.

View image in fullscreen Jordan Henderson scores Chelsea’s fifth goal from a free-kick. Photograph: Ryan Pierse/Getty Images

There were 68 seconds on the clock when Henderson became Chelsea’s oldest scorer in the Premier League since John Terry in May 2017. “We knew Chelsea are a team that starts well,” Rose said. “It was our responsibility that we didn’t react the right way with this information.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Bournemouth were overwhelmed. Chelsea pushed again in the third minute, Palmer’s flick freeing Pedro Neto to test Djordje Petrovic. The ball broke loose and Henderson swept a pass to Rogers, who cut in from the left and his shot flew in via a deflection off Antonio Silva.

The focus switched to Bournemouth’s long list of absentees. Justin Kluivert and Eli Junior Kroupi are big losses in attack. Alex Scott, the subject of multiple bids from Chelsea in the summer, exacerbated a thigh problem during a scintillating display for England against Croatia last Saturday.

These are worrying times for Bournemouth, who are winless after six league games. Goal difference is keeping them out of the bottom three and they struggled without Scott’s energy and quality in midfield. Ryan Christie and Tyler Adams were overrun and Silva had a nightmare at the back, his error at the start of the second half allowing Neto to nip in and set up João Pedro to make it 3-0 with an emphatic shot.

Bournemouth had chances during the first half, Christie, Rayan and Silva drawing saves from Emiliano Martínez, but it suited Chelsea for a basketball game to develop.

There were echoes of past battles between Alonso and Rose in the Bundesliga. Rose, who ended Alonso’s 35-game unbeaten run with Bayer Leverkusen when he was RB Leipzig’s manager, was a distinct second-best this time. Evanilson bundled in from a corner, but Chelsea were rampant.

The fourth goal arrived when Rogers found the overlapping Pep Chavarria, whose low cross was gobbled up by João Pedro. Alonso, who had become increasingly frantic on the touchline, relaxed. He was a great midfielder in his day and will have appreciated the technique when Henderson’s free-kick flew beyond the reach of Petrovic.

Sports.title: Ten-man Brighton continue fine form with battling win at Sunderland
Sports.content:
When Jaouen Hadjam lashed Brighton’s second goal low beyond Robin Roefs, it sparked a mass exodus. With a smattering of boos, the Stadium of Light emptied at a speed of knots and frown lines creased the forehead of Sunderland’s manager, Régis Le Bris.

Undaunted by Pascal Struijk’s second-half red card, Brighton had not merely cemented their hold on third place but boosted an already healthy points tally to 13.

This was not quite as fluent as Brighton’s 3-0 deconstruction of Arsenal before the international break, but no one can possibly underestimate their supreme defensive organisation now.

“It wasn’t easy but we always had this belief we could get something here,” said the Brighton manager, Fabian Hürzeler. “We keep clean sheets and we always have chances to score. We’ve always played good football, but I don’t want us just to be known as a nice team anymore.”

Sunderland are stuck on four points with a solitary Premier League victory to their name this season. They head to central Portugal for Thursday’s Europa League meeting with Torreense in introspective mode.

View image in fullscreen Jaouen Hadjam sealed the win for Brighton at the Stadium of Light. Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty Images

As a cagey first half unfolded, Kyril Louis-Dreyfus looked on anxiously from the directors’ box. Sunderland’s owner and chair has added the title chief executive to his club portfolio after Tom Burwell’s abrupt departure just five months into the role of interim CEO.

Among the 29-year-old’s more pressing tasks in this hands-on role is to secure a front-of-shirt sponsor after the collapse of a deal with Visit Ghana.

At the interval, Louis-Dreyfus was probably relieved the scoreboard read 0-0. Deep in stoppage time at the end of the first period, Struijk had headed against an upright with Roefs beaten.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Le Fee shows his disappointment after Sunderland’s defeat to Brighton. Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty Images

It was the best chance of a half low on clearcut chances and only really enlivened by some beautiful calibrated deliveries from Enzo Le Fée. Sunderland’s attacking playmaker created decent early openings for Wilson Isidor – deputising for the hamstrung Brian Brobbey – and Thomas Meunier. Significantly, though, Le Fée faded badly in the second half.

In the 53rd minute, a home defence missing the hamstrung Dan Ballard paid the price for a failure to clear a long throw when Pascal Gross’ clever through ball cued up Maxim De Cuyper to slide the crispest of low first-time shots between Roefs and a post. It was the 35-year-old Gross’s seventh direct goal involvement in a Brighton goal in his last six Premier League appearances, but his team were soon reduced to 10 men.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

When a poorly positioned Struijk felled Isidor as he accelerated towards the area the £20m summer signing from Leeds denied a clear goalcoring opportunity, but initially the referee, Tom Bramall, did not see it that way. The video assistant referee urged Bramall to visit the pitchside monitor, which prompted a change of heart and a red card for Struijk.

View image in fullscreen Brighton defender Pascal Struijk was shown a red card after a VAR review. Photograph: Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty Images

Despite their numerical disadvantage, Brighton continued to look comfortable. It did not help Sunderland’s cause that, unusually, Granit Xhaka proved untypically slapdash in possession. Perhaps the strain of admitting to obtaining a fake Covid vaccination certificate during the pandemic – the authorities in Lucerne issued Switzerland’s captain with a suspended £136,000 fine last week – took its toll.

Recent social media footage shows Xhaka demonstrating commendable restraint in the face of jibes from Newcastle fans while out shopping with his wife near their home in Gosforth, but he could have perhaps done with a little more trademark aggression here. In its absence, the visiting substitutes Georginio Rutter and Hadjam combined for the Algeria left-back to strip the shine expertly from Sunderland’s Portuguese trip.

“It was a tight, intense game,” said Le Bris. “But we weren’t at our best. It’s a question of composure. We have to change the momentum.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa’s wait for home win goes on after Ajer hits back for Brentford
Sports.content:
Kristoffer Ajer spent a chunk of the extended international window fielding questions about the state of mind of his Norway teammate Erling Haaland and perhaps in recent weeks he also picked up some finishing tips. Two minutes after John McGinn’s shot cannoned in via Ajer’s calf, the centre-back strode into the Villa box and kept three defenders at arm’s length before equalising, his side-foot shot also catching a nick off a defender, on this occasion Victor Lindelöf.

For the second time in the game, one team cancelled out the other within two minutes; just 88 seconds separated Yehor Yarmolyuk’s opener, born from Jaidon Anthony pressing Tyrone Mings, from Nicolas Jackson’s simple equaliser. It was a strange, seesawing and tempestuous game and a busy one for Ajer, who was also booked late on for questioning a decision by Craig Pawson, who managed the impressive feat of drawing ire from both sets of supporters.

Unai Emery had dipped into expletive to make it clear he was not enamoured of Villa’s previous home performance, describing their display in defeat by Nottingham Forest as “very shit”, and his side’s failure to hold on to the lead against Brentford extended their winless record since the Villa Park revamp left the ground with just three stands in play.

“We are not happy, we are sad, but I am optimistic because we improved things we needed after the match against Nottingham,” said Emery, conceding his team are struggling to control games in the manner they have so often across his near four-year tenure. “To draw at home is not a good result.”

This feisty draw also maintained Keith Andrews’s fine, unbeaten record against Emery across four meetings, though the visitors also had chances to snatch victory with the left-back El Hadji Malick Diouf’s delivery into the box keeping Villa’s defenders on their toes and the Brazil striker Igor Thiago a constant threat.

Ajer’s equaliser – his first goal in club football for two and a half years – served as confirmation that Villa had threats coming at them from all angles. “When he goes on one of those mazy runs, I encourage him to stay involved in the attack,” Andrews said. “It can be quite off-putting for the opposition defence when they see someone of his size and technical ability around the 18-yard box.”

Brentford, who remain one of four unbeaten sides in the league this season, seized the lead when Anthony forced Mings into a loose pass and Kevin Schade located Thiago, whose cross was cleared by Lindelöf to the edge of the box. Yarmolyuk hammered the ball in but Villa quickly replied. Emi Buendía’s shot deflected off Jannik Schuster and Jackson nipped around the back of Ajer to finish unmarked from the six-yard box.

View image in fullscreen John McGinn pulls his shorts up in response to chants from the Brentford fans about his weight. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

Buendía missed a chance to gain the lead in the first half, crashing to his knees theatrically, just after Michael Kayode, fresh from scoring on his Italy debut during the break, had superbly blocked Johan Manzambi’s low strike.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Caoimhín Kelleher made a brilliant, instinctive double save on the verge of half-time to deny Jackson and then McGinn. After the interval his opposite number was called into a fine save, Zion Suzuki pushing wide a Schade volley. Emery clenched both fists and momentarily basked in the joy of Villa taking the lead on 77 minutes. Manzambi had the coolness of mind to locate McGinn, who celebrated by dragging his shorts high above his waist in a retort to the chants about his weight. But a roaming, towering Ajer had the final say at the end.

“I sensed Villa were starting to click before the international break, embedding new and talented players and trusted lieutenants that Unai has had for numerous years,” Andrews said. “We could’ve won it, could’ve lost it and I’m a tad disappointed that we couldn’t take advantage of situations in the last 10-15 minutes where I felt we were coming on strong and had the opportunity to win the game.

“But to come away [disappointed] at a club that is playing in the Champions League, won the Europa League, with a manager who has just been nominated for the Ballon d’Or [coach of the year], it probably says where we’re at the moment.”

Sports.title: Bruno Guimarães completes Arsenal comeback to end Leeds’ unbeaten run
Sports.content:
Arsenal built the foundations of their new success on a desire for competition, an appetite for battle. But what happens when that spirit is insufficient, when your opponents play just as hard as you do? Well, then you bring on Bruno Guimarães and you play even harder.

Arsenal had just snatched an equaliser against a dominant Leeds side when Mikel Arteta introduced his key summer signing. The former Newcastle captain has been having to bide his time but when he entered the field just after the hour, he turned the game on its head.

Arsenal had been ponderous until this point, even uncertain at times. The passing had been intricate, not incisive, and echoes of familiar weaknesses had put the crowd on edge. Guimarães put paid to all that. Not only snapping into tackles, not only moving the ball at pace, he was desperate for everything to go faster, more aggressively, with sharper intention. Nine minutes after coming on, he scored the winner.

It was a goal that deserved to decide the contest and reflected the best of what the home side had been trying to achieve. Play developed down the left where Noni Madueke had shone, but here it was Bukayo Saka playing a one-two with Martin Ødegaard. The captain then poked a short pass to Declan Rice who – with Guimarães now covering him – had burst into the opposition area. Rice back-heeled the ball to the edge of the area and there was the Brazilian waiting, poised, to steer the ball unerringly into the corner of James Trafford’s goal.

In the time between Leeds’ opener and the winner, Arsenal had five efforts on goal, the same as in the preceding 55 minutes. Once the lead was established, they should have had at least two more goals, with Ødegaard somehow missing from two yards out and Trafford denying Saka in a one-on-one in the final move of the match. Leeds did not feature as an attacking threat in the final half hour, so decisive was the switch in momentum.

View image in fullscreen Riccardo Calafiori equalises for Arsenal against Leeds. Photograph: Hannah McKay/Reuters

Arteta said his team had to “pinch our desire to win” to overcome a visiting side who appear no longer to be punching above their weight, but rather have moved up a class.

“We had to face the challenge because [Leeds] are a team that hadn’t lost in the Premier League,” he said. “They’re in a great position because they fully deserve it. They are incredibly dangerous and we got into a situation, [a goal down] after that defeat against Brighton, 12:30 kick-off.

“It is a bad mixture and we got out of it through … pinching our desire to win, by showing the personality and courage that we have in this team.”

Arteta will be able to take satisfaction from the way his team managed the result, the effectiveness of his substitutes and other smaller details such as the continuing creative contributions of Rice – now with three assists to his name – and a second goal for Riccardo Calafiori, whose buccaneering inside runs have been a feature of the season.

On the other hand, his midfield was outmuscled and outplayed in the first hour, with the opening 10 minutes of the second half a period of dominance for the visitors that deservedly delivered a goal when James Justin finished Gabriel Gudmundsson’s cross after the Swede had run off the back of Ben White.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen James Justin (centre) fires Leeds ahead. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

Arsenal’s centre-halves, are looking like less of the sum of their parts, with Ezri Konsa and Gabriel uncertain when faced with the accuracy and variation of Leeds’ deliveries.

“It’s a credit to the mentality that Mikel Arteta has created, that even on a tough day they found a way to win”, said Daniel Farke. The German bemoaned the Arsenal equaliser, bundled home by Calafiori after White had knocked down a Madueke cross, believing that if Trafford had got a hand to it, “we would have gone on to take three points.”

With the proviso that there can be no back-slapping in defeat, however, Farke said the match showed his team’s improvement since returning to the Premier League. “We have developed in all aspects,” he said. “You can speak about game management, you can speak about pressing, about compactness against the ball, or quality in possession, or in counterattacks. We were able to compete much better with set pieces.

“Today we came very close to winning an away game against one of the best sides in the world and we played exactly on their level, more or less.”

Sports.title: European football: Bayern fight back after conceding fastest goal in Bundesliga history
Sports.content:
Augsburg’s Robin Fellhauer scored after eight ⁠seconds against Bayern Munich on Saturday to record the fastest ⁠goal in Bundesliga ⁠history, ​but the visiting German champions twice came from a goal down to snatch a 2-2 ⁠draw.

Fellhauer benefited from a blunder by Bayern’s Manuel Neuer as the keeper tried to clear, ⁠but sent the ball to Fellhauer who ​beat the record held ‌jointly by Kevin ‌Volland and Karim Bellarabi by one second.

Bayern, whose only league defeat in their past 48 matches was by Augsburg in January, upped their game after the break, and Ismael Saibari scored the equaliser.

Another Neuer error put Augsburg ahead again in the 64th ​minute, the 40-year-old punching Calvin Brackelmann’s shot into the path of Rodrigo Ribeiro, who only had to push the ball over the line.

Bayern battled back once more ⁠when Harry Kane, who hit the woodwork in ​the first ​half, cut the ball ​back for Nathaniel Brown to tap in ​the equaliser 10 ‌minutes from ​time.

There was also drama elsewhere, as Bayer Leverkusen grabbed a rollercoaster 4-3 win in Mainz while Hamburg snatched a late 3-2 win at Hoffenheim.

Robert Andrich gave Leverkusen the lead with a superb volley after just five minutes, before Patrik Schick doubled the lead with a smart finish four minutes later. Anthony Caci dragged Mainz back into the game, scoring twice to make it level before half-time.

View image in fullscreen Jarell Quansah heads Bayer Leverkusen 3-2 ahead at Mainz. Photograph: Christian Kaspar-Bartke/Getty Images

Second-half goals from Jarell Quansah and Moussa Diaby put Leverkusen back in control, before Benedict Hollerbach grabbed a late third for Mainz.

Yussuf Poulsen bundled in an early opener for Hamburg, before Fisnik Asllani jabbed home an equally scrappy equaliser for Hoffenheim. Bambase Conte put Hoffenheim in the lead with a brilliant shot from outside the area early in the second half, but a red card for his teammate Bernardo swung the game back in Hamburg’s favour.

The visitors had one late equaliser ruled out by the video assistant referee before Terem Moffi equalised with an 83rd minute header and Miro Muheim grabbed a stoppage-time winner.

In Saturday’s other games, goals from Jeff Chabot and Chris Fuehrich sealed a comfortable 2-0 win for Stuttgart at Paderborn, while Livan Burcu struck late to hand Union Berlin a nervy 1-0 win at home to Elversberg.

Sports.title: Ipswich stun Fulham with last-gasp comeback to increase heat on Arbeloa
Sports.content:
Álvaro Arbeloa bristled at suggestions he cannot handle the pressure after Fulham’s at Ipswich extended their winless start in the Premier League to six matches. The former Real Madrid manager was minutes away from a first managerial victory in the competition after Ryan Sessegnon’s brilliant 55th-minute strike, but the visitors collapsed late on in abject fashion.

Abdoul Ouattara produced a thunderbolt from 30 yards to level for Ipswich after 88 minutes and Dara O’Shea headed home Jack Clarke’s free-kick in the second minute of stoppage time to consign the visitors to a painful loss. Tottenham securing a point at Manchester United pushed Fulham to the bottom of the table.

With his side facing another week in the relegation zone, Arbeloa pushed back at suggestions he is feeling the scrutiny, saying: “I never worry about my position.

“I don’t feel fear. You cannot be a coach if you feel it. You have to work, take the decision and you need to show confidence to your players. I am so happy with many things they are doing. I know it is not easy for them.

“It’s not about my position, it is about Fulham’s position. That is the most important thing. It is just six games, but it is true we need points.”

View image in fullscreen Álvaro Arbeloa reacts during Fulham’s defeat at Ipswich. Photograph: MB Media/Getty Images

Arbeloa walked straight down the tunnel at full-time after shaking hands with his opposite number, Gary O’Neil. Fulham are seven points behind promoted Ipswich as they switch focus to Saturday’s visit of Hull.

Asked how he would block out the noise, Arbeloa said: “Maybe you don’t know me, but I played for the best team in world. I have coached the best team in the world. Maybe you don’t know, but just to let you know, that pressure is part of my life since I was a kid.

View image in fullscreen Dara O’Shea (centre) scores Ipswich’s dramatic late winner at Portman Road. Photograph: Ben Whitley/PA

“It is normal in football. It is normal for players, it is normal for coaches and everybody that is around a team. Pressure is something that is important for me and I like it.”

This defeat made it four league losses this season for Fulham and they have conceded after 75 minutes in matches with Sunderland, Crystal Palace, Manchester United and now Ipswich.

O’Neil struck a different tone after he celebrated a third victory of the campaign with substitutes Chuba Akpom and Clarke able to make telling contributions during a dramatic finale.

“On the result, I’m proud of the players and proud of the way we finished the game,” O’Neil said. “They showed exactly what they are – together, hard-working, have quality, never going to stop.

“Looked fitter than the opposition, I thought. The last 20 minutes, it looked like they were starting to tire and we were able to keep pushing. The subs helped with that.

“That Fulham side have been in the Premier League for a while now and for us to be able to compete with them the way we did was impressive.”

Sports.title: Championship roundup: Swansea fight back to beat Norwich; Middlesbrough go second
Sports.content:
Vítor Matos praised his Swansea side for overcoming a lack of training as they strengthened their position at the top of the Championship with a 2-1 comeback win over Norwich. Second-half goals from Moussa Yeo and the Republic of Ireland striker Adam Idah wiped out Jacob Wright’s strike just before the half-hour mark.

It was the third time Swansea had come from behind this season to win, and, after West Ham’s draw the previous night, it gave them top spot in the table. Idah, though, limped out of the action and could be a doubt for Tuesday’s visit to Millwall.

“I’m really happy with the boys,” said Matos. “Players had been flying around because of the international break, joining on the last days of training as well before the game. It’s not the easiest way to prepare. It’s all about trying to reconnect everyone.”

It was a fourth defeat in a row in all competitions for Norwich, who have now conceded 19 goals in nine league matches.

Middlesbrough celebrated their 150th anniversary game in style as Will Lankshear’s second-half header secured a 1-0 victory over Wolves at the Riverside Stadium. A sold-out crowd helped mark the occasion, and Lankshear’s header from Tommy Conway’s cross ensured the home fans went home happy. The win enabled Middlesbrough to climb above West Ham into second spot. Wolves were second best as they suffered a second league defeat since their relegation last season.

View image in fullscreen A tifo marks Middlesbrough’s 150th anniversary before their win over Wolves at the Riverside. Photograph: Richard Sellers/PA

West Brom’s head coach, James Morrison, defended Nat Phillips as a “strong character” after a second successive derby mistake led to the only goal in a 1-0 defeat to Birmingham at The Hawthorns. Phillips gave away the 41st-minute penalty when he fouled August Priske, who slotted home from the spot. The former Liverpool defender’s back pass let in Fer Lopez to win the Black Country derby for Wolves last time out, but Morrison said: “I understand he’s made two errors but it was just a misjudgement.”

Quick Guide League One: Plymouth on top; dream start for Savage Show Plymouth came from behind to beat Wimbledon 2-1 with a stoppage-time goal from substitute Xavier Amaechi which put them clear at the top of League One. Jayden Stockley had put the Dons ahead in the 16th minute, with Caleb Watts equalising ahead of the break. It looked like the points would be shared before Amaechi swept the ball home in the fifth minute of added time. New Peterborough manager Robbie Savage had a dream start with a 3-1 win at Leicester, to pile more pressure on Foxes’ manager Russell Martin. Posh took an early lead through Owura Edwards and Harry Leonard before an own goal from Warren O’Hora made it 3-0 just before the break. Emil Riis scored a second-half consolation for the hosts. Mark Harris and Cameron Brannagan scored as high-flying Oxford secured a 2-1 win over Notts County at Meadow Lane. Bradford were held to a goalless draw by Leyton Orient at Valley Parade, slipping two points behind Plymouth. Huddersfield missed the chance to go second after Sheffield Wednesday fought back with two late goals to snatch a 2-2 draw at the Accu Stadium after Jamal Lowe scored a penalty deep into stoppage-time. Kyle Wootton scored twice as Stockport came from behind to beat Barnsley 3-1 at Edgeley Park to sit third. Gassan Ahadme’s late goal gave fifth-placed Cambridge a 1-0 win over 10-man Blackpool at the Abbey Stadium, where there had been a 15 minute delay to kick-off because of issues affecting supporters entering the ground. Reading are sixth after a 5-1 away win at strugglers MK Dons while Luton were comprehensive victors at Wycombe with a dominant 4-1 display to spoil a day of celebration for Tom Hounsell. Efforts from Kasey Palmer, Nahki Wells, Jamie Donley and Devante Cole were more than enough against a home side who announced Hounsell as permanent head coach before the game. Leon Ayinde’s first EFL goal was enough to move Doncaster out of the bottom four with a 1-0 home win over Burton. Mansfield edged home 2-1 in their first ever game against Bromley to halt a run of four games without a victory. Wigan remain adrift at the bottom of the table after a 1-0 defeat at Stevenage. Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Burnley’s first win of the season, and their first away from home since February, sent Watford fans into open revolt as the Clarets cruised home 4-0 at Vicarage Road. While Alessio Dionisi’s fifth defeat in six games increased the pressure on the Hornets head coach, counterpart Nicky Hayen’s first victory lifted Burnley off the bottom.

Three goals in the space of 12 first-half minutes put the visitors out of sight and extended the Hornets’ wretched defensive record to 29 weeks without a clean sheet. When Stoke won 2-1 at Vicarage Road last month, it ended 251 days without a win on the road for the Potters. Here, Watford extended more charity to the Clarets, who ended 241 days without an away win comfortably.

Asked about the furious reaction of fans, and the rising tide of opinion on social media that his job was at risk, Dionisi said: “In football it’s normal. It’s probably better to say only one thing – I’m sorry for this match. I’m very angry because after 30 minutes the match was finished, it was impossible to come back. But I believe in my team and I believe in my job. I’m here and we work every to improve: now it is important to work well, to work better.”

Dionisi’s decision to take off popular Spaniard Iker Bravo after just 35 minutes was roundly booed, and he admitted: “Iker is a good player and, for me, he must play every match, but I had to change something and it was impossible to change everyone.”

View image in fullscreen Watford fans leave early as their side crumbles at home to Burnley. Photograph: Peter Tarry/PA

Bristol City’s manager, Michael Skubala, felt Charlton goalkeeper Arthur Okonkwo should have been sent off in the 1-1 draw at The Valley. Referee Tom Reeves did not give a foul after the Wrexham loanee raced out of his box to halt Japanese winger Yu Hirakawa in the 15th minute. By that stage the Addicks already had a lead through Karlan Grant’s smart finish but Scott Twine’s penalty in the 27th minute put City back on level terms after Conor Coventry brought down Dom Ballard.

Patrick Bamford scored twice to help Sheffield United to a comfortable 3-0 victory over Lincoln. The result, with Tahith Chong also on the scoresheet, ended a three-match losing run for Chris Wilder’s men in all competitions against a side which had won three of their previous four away matches.

Quick Guide League Two: Grant strikes twice to keep Salford top Show Jorge Grant’s late double sealed a 2-0 win for Salford at 10-man Cheltenham to keep them top of the table. The result extends the Ammies’ winning run in League Two to four and it was also their first victory at Cheltenham. Kabongo Tshimanga’s stoppage-time strike sealed an impressive 3-1 come-from-behind victory for Barnet at Bristol Rovers. Rovers’ record home winning streak came to an end after a two-on-one counter-attack resulted in Tshimanga tucking home under Brad Young to seal all three points. Crewe kept up the pace with a 1-0 away win over Swindon, who suffered a fourth defeat in five league games. Gillingham moved into fourth spot after a 4-1 win at Rotherham and Port Vale climbed out of the bottom two after a 1-0 win over Grimsby. Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Lamine Cissé and Ben Wilmot were on target as 10-man Stoke extended their unbeaten league run to six games with a 2-1 win over Bolton. Mark Robins’ in-form side played for 70 minutes without Maksym Talovierov after the defender’s dismissal for bringing down Kyliane Dong. However, the Potters shrugged off the disadvantage to gain a first win in Bolton since October 1990. Their fifth win in six games lifted them up to fourth while Bolton dropped to 17th.

Blackburn made it back-to-back home wins with a battling 2-1 victory over Cardiff. Andri Gudjohnsen gave Rovers the lead with a composed finish just before the half hour and Todd Cantwell doubled the advantage 10 minutes later with a shot that Bluebirds goalkeeper Nathan Trott will be disappointed not to have saved. The visitors struck just after the break through Callum Robinson’s first of the campaign.

View image in fullscreen Todd Cantwell watches his effort cross the line, putting Blackburn two up against Cardiff. Photograph: Dave Howarth/CameraSport/Getty Images

Derby are still without a home win after Ollie Rathbone scored late on to earn Wrexham a 1-1 draw at Pride Park. The Rams were on course for victory through Sam Szmodics’ superb early strike only for the Welsh side to rescue a point two minutes from the end.

Camiel Neghli ensured it was a baptism of fire for the new Preston manager, Graham Alexander, as his late strike sealed a 1-0 win for Millwall at Deepdale. It was coolness personified from the Dutch-born Algerian, who slotted Luke Cundle’s cut-back into the far corner for what turned out to be a 79th-minute winner.

Sports.title: Northampton's try-fest victory over Bath took the biscuit and proves one thing: rugby's lawmakers have shifted the balance TOO FAR in favour of attacking play, writes NIK SIMON
Sports.content:
At 7am on Saturday morning, Johann van Graan sat down for breakfast with Ben Spencer at Bath’s team hotel to watch the All Blacks’ 50-19 victory over Australia.

Hitting half a century in Test rugby used to be something spectacular but, in the current climate, it is becoming the new normal.

Tries are coming thick and fast across the rugby world but this PREM fixture at Franklin’s Gardens - a 71-48 victory for the Saints - took the biscuit.

There were exceptional attacking skills on show from Fin Smith and Finn Russell but this felt more like a basketball game.

It was the second highest scoring game in the league’s history and by the time Tommy Freeman touched down the 18th try of the afternoon it all seemed a little bit too easy.

Defence and tension are fundamental to rugby’s DNA but right now the lawmakers have shifted the balance towards attacking play.

Breakdowns are refereed more harshly, tackle laws make it easier to offload, mauls are difficult to stop and teams are gearing up to attack from deep.

Fin Smith showed his attacking flair in Northampton's victory over Bath

But the sheer number of points scored raised questions over whether the balance of attack and defence is out of kilter

There were 58 missed tackles at Franklin’s Gardens - 21 by Northampton and 37 by Bath – but the audience were treated to an exhibition of dazzling tries.

Northampton ultimately came out on top – thanks to a hat-trick by Ollie Sleightholme – but it left people questioning if the game is falling out of kilter.

‘There have been trends,’ said Van Graan. ‘To get 50 points at some stage was a big achievement but now we score 48 points away from home. If you look at South Africa v Australia two weeks ago, Australia were 42-17 up and South Africa could have won it with the last play of the game.

‘From an officiating point of view, attack is definitely on top. You get rewarded to keep the ball in hand. From a PREM point of view, all 10 teams want to play a certain brand of rugby. Our challenge is to adapt to this better than the other nine teams to stop the flow of it.

‘I’m a purist. I love the scrum and I love the maul. Unfortunately, if I put it that way, you’re not going to get a low scoring game between Bath and Saints. I’m pretty happy to score 48 points away from home. I’m not going to accept 71 points.’

Both teams were given time and space to offload. Defences are more disruptive at Test level but the confidence flowing through the likes of Smith, Freeman and Alex Coles proves that England are blessed with attacking talent.

‘I know people will say it is too easy to score, but you’re not going to please everybody,’ said Northampton coach Phil Dowson. ‘I think there’s a balance. We don’t want it to be 99-88. It’s not basketball, but we also don’t want a 9-3. I used to have a coach called Mike Friday and one of his sayings was that ‘you can’t defend good rugby and there’s lots of good rugby being played’.

‘I have no doubt there will be some games this season that will be tough, ugly, horrible and nasty. But I also think we want to be able to enjoy and reward great rugby. And by the way, basketball is selling loads of tickets to sold out arenas.’
