Sports.title: Jack Catterall Demands His Turn Against Teofimo Lopez
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall insists his title fight with Teofimo Lopez must come next, while Teofimo’s manager Keith Connolly left the outcome open with a brief response on X: “Let’s see how it all plays out.”

The comments follow FazSportz’s report that Teofimo has appealed the WBA’s September 22 order to face Catterall, seeking permission to pursue bigger fights. The October 22 negotiation deadline is approaching.

“Was awarded a voluntary title shot coming off a loss. Im next,” Catterall wrote. “I’ve got no doubts the WBA will honour what they said and agreed before I boxed Giyasov. More waiting around but it is what it is.”

Connolly’s response stopped short of promising that Catterall would get the fight. It also offered no explanation of how Teofimo’s team expects the dispute to end, leaving Catterall waiting while the champion pursues an exception.

The WBA’s published ruling supports Catterall’s account of the arrangement. When Rolando Romero was elevated to super champion at welterweight, the organization allowed him one optional defense, with the Giyasov-Catterall winner due to face him afterward. Teofimo defeated Romero on August 22 and inherited that obligation.

Teofimo’s appeal seeks permission to pursue bigger fights. That may make commercial sense for his team, but Catterall completed the route the WBA established. Allowing another opponent would mean extending his wait after the optional defense had already been used.

Catterall’s reference to Teofimo receiving a title shot coming off a loss sharpens his complaint. Teofimo received an opportunity without having to rebuild first. Catterall now wants the opportunity attached to his own win over Giyasov.

The sides have until close of business, Eastern Time, on October 22 to reach an agreement. If negotiations fail or either side withdraws, the WBA Championship Committee may order a purse bid with its president’s approval. That is a possible next step, rather than an automatic event on deadline day.

Teofimo could relinquish the belt to pursue another opponent. Keeping it while avoiding Catterall, however, would require the WBA to change the conditions it had already attached to the title.

Sports.title: Osleys Iglesias Wants Canelo Or Mbilli Winner
Sports.content:
Osleys Iglesias wants a unification against the winner of Canelo Alvarez’s October 31 fight with Christian Mbilli. Getting that fight could prove harder than defending his IBF title. Canelo has bigger commercial options, while Mbilli could be drawn into a lucrative rematch if he wins.

“I hope the winner [of Canelo-Mbilli] faces me. I’d like my next fight to be a unification,” Iglesias said after stopping Oliver Zaren in Quebec on Thursday.

The seventh-round stoppage lifted Iglesias to 16-0 with 15 knockouts. Those numbers help explain the difficulty of finding a willing opponent. He brings a world title, southpaw skills and heavy power, but lacks the name recognition that would turn a Canelo fight into a major event.

Canelo would be risking more than another points defeat. Iglesias has the power to hurt him and force a punishing fight, with a stoppage a serious possibility. Another belt might not be enough compensation when better-known opponents could offer more money and a better chance of winning.

Hamzah Sheeraz and Chris Eubank Jr. would give Canelo fresh opponents with British interest behind them. Neither is a guaranteed victory, but his team could view both as less dangerous choices than Iglesias.

Canelo also has a remaining fight under his agreement with Turki Alalshikh’s boxing operation. What Alalshikh wants to fund will influence the selection, leaving Iglesias competing against names that could sell a bigger show.

Mbilli appears more likely to accept a unification, but beating Canelo could change his immediate plans. A rematch would be difficult to turn down financially, provided Canelo wanted another attempt. His defeats against Floyd Mayweather and Dmitry Bivol did not produce second meetings.

If Canelo moves on, Mbilli against Iglesias would offer plenty in the ring. Mbilli’s relentless pressure would test the Cuban, while also bringing him within range of dangerous southpaw counters.

That is Iglesias’ best opening. A Canelo victory could leave him making another defense while the Mexican pursues a more profitable opponent.

Sports.title: Amir Khan Rules Out December Manny Pacquiao Fight
Sports.content:
Amir Khan is interested in facing Manny Pacquiao, but says he would not be ready for December 11. His admission leaves the proposed comeback dependent on more than agreeing on a payday, with the former light welterweight champion approaching five years out of the ring.

“That’s a rumor,” Khan told Metro about appearing on the Tyson Fury–Anthony Joshua undercard. “Even if it was for that fight night, I wouldn’t be ready for it, and I don’t think Manny would be either. “We’ve both been traveling, and we’re obviously not back in camp. It’s only about nine weeks away. I don’t know where that came from.”

Khan says talks are taking place and that he is happy with the money and location discussed. That establishes interest, but no signed fight or date has been announced.

The preparation question is particularly significant for Khan. He has not fought since Kell Brook stopped him in February 2022, and his last victory over a leading opponent came against Chris Algieri in 2015.

A longer camp could help Khan recover his conditioning. Whether he can regain the timing and reactions needed against Pacquiao is harder to judge. His best boxing depended on fast combinations and getting out before opponents could answer. Returning after years away would test both parts of that approach.

Pacquiao has been inactive too, but his July 2025 draw with Mario Barrios provides more recent evidence that he can compete over 12 rounds. Khan would enter negotiations without a comparable performance to point to since his retirement.

That difference makes a return fight worth considering before Khan commits to Pacquiao. Sparring can help him prepare, but an actual bout would offer a clearer picture of what remains.

Khan has always wanted the matchup, and the proposed terms appear attractive. His decision to dismiss December is sensible. The next question is whether additional time produces a prepared fighter or simply delays a difficult comeback.

Adding Pacquiao against Khan, who hasn’t fought since Brook stopped him in 2022, would turn the Cardiff card into an expensive nostalgia show. Fury–Joshua is already years overdue, and the proposed Jai Opetaia–Deontay Wilder fight features a faded former champion who turns 41 before December 11. Another pairing built around aging stars would leave the event trading heavily on what these fighters used to be.

Sports.title: Joshua-Fury Needs Promotion as Dana White and Eddie Hearn Bicker
Sports.content:
Dana White now describes himself as one of the promoters of Anthony Joshua’s December 11 fight with Tyson Fury, saying that his team will produce the event that night.

White’s latest comments put him alongside Eddie Hearn and Frank Warren in his description of the operation, although his clearest commitment concerns production.

“I’m producing the fight. Me and my team will be producing the fight that night. And I guess we’ll call me one of the promoters of the event because you do have Frank Warren and Eddie Hearn that are both promoters too, promoting the event,” White told BBC 5 Live.

The heavyweight fight is scheduled for Cardiff’s Principality Stadium. White also credited Hearn with securing the UK location during his interview with Steve Bunce.

The wording deserves attention. “I guess we’ll call me” sounds like White describing how he sees his involvement rather than announcing a newly agreed contractual position. It leaves the formal promotional arrangements unresolved, but makes clear that he expects a substantial role when the fighters enter the ring.

White and Hearn’s continuing argument over their roles is becoming tiresome. Every interview spent discussing who gets to call himself a promoter is another opportunity lost to explain why Joshua-Fury is still worth watching in December.

The names are familiar, but that does not mean the fight sells itself. Many fans see Joshua and Fury as two former champions meeting years after the contest should have happened. The promotion needs to address that skepticism rather than assume their past achievements will be enough.

There is still a fight to sell: the rivalry, the contrasting styles and the consequences of defeat for both men. Fans want to know what Joshua and Fury have left and whether either can produce something better than their recent performances suggest.

White and Hearn arguing over credit gives those viewers little reason to get excited. They need to spend more time promoting the fighters and less time promoting their own involvement.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Camp Threatens Cancellation Over Bahdi Weight
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield’s father is threatening to pull Saturday’s fight against Lucas Bahdi if the Canadian exceeds 146 pounds at the second-day weight check, according to Chris Mannix. Bahdi’s team disputes his account of the negotiations and insists its fighter will come in at 145 or below.

The disagreement emerged Friday night ahead of their vacant WBA lightweight title fight in Chicago. Mannix reports that Illinois requires fighters in championship bouts to come in within ten pounds of the contract weight at a second-day check. For a fight contracted at 135 pounds, that means a 145-pound limit.

Floyd Sr. claims Bahdi’s side tried to negotiate a 15-pound allowance, which would permit him to reach 150 pounds. He also alleges they offered an additional $250,000 for each extra pound Bahdi was allowed.

According to Floyd Sr., Schofield’s camp agreed to 146 pounds but would refuse to proceed if Bahdi came in any heavier.

A representative from Bahdi’s side called Schofield’s version “total bullshit” and told Mannix that Bahdi would come in at 145 pounds or less.

That leaves two different accounts of what happened behind the scenes. The alleged financial offer comes from Floyd Sr., and Bahdi’s representative denies his version. It cannot be treated as an accepted account of the negotiations.

There is also an unanswered question about the 146-pound allowance. That figure exceeds the Illinois limit Mannix describes by one pound. His report does not establish whether the commission approved an exception or whether Floyd Sr. was describing only an agreement between the camps.

For Schofield, the concern is how much weight Bahdi can regain before they enter the ring. His father has now attached a cancellation threat to that concern, putting additional pressure on Saturday’s check.

Bahdi’s side has given itself a clear number to meet. If he comes in at 145 pounds or below, he would satisfy both the reported state limit and Schofield Sr.’s stated demand. Anything above 146 would test whether Schofield’s camp follows through on its threat.

Ghana News.title: Late Solanke strike salvages 10-man Spurs draw at Man United
Ghana News.content:
Dominic Solanke scored in stoppage time to salvage a point for 10-man Tottenham as they snatched a draw against Manchester United in a feisty encounter at Old Trafford.

It looked as if United were about to pile more misery on the visitors following their pitiful start to the Premier League season when Bryan Mbeumo broke the deadlock in the 73rd minute.

Things went from bad to worse for Spurs when Rodrigo Bentancur was sent off five minutes later for headbutting Luke Shaw, who had shoved him over after a reckless challenge from the Uruguay midfielder.

But Solanke, who was captaining Tottenham for the first time, nodded Sandro Tonali's cross into the back of the net in the second minute of added time to lift Spurs off the bottom of the table.

Roberto de Zerbi's side remain winless, however, and stay in the relegation zone - above both Fulham and Coventry City - with just three points from the first six games.

United have suffered their own shaky start to the campaign with just one victory and a sluggish first-half performance was met with boos by the home fans on Saturday.

They were much improved after the break, but jeers once again echoed around Old Trafford at full-time. This was the second successive league game they have dropped points against a team that were reduced to 10 men - following their 1-0 derby defeat by Manchester City last month.

Ghana News.title: Gender Ministry to monitor welfare of Nana Akua Addo’s children amid domestic violence case
Ghana News.content:
Gender Minister, Agnes Naa Momo Lartey

The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection says it will deploy social welfare officers to monitor the welfare of the children of Ghanaian fashion personality Nana Akua Addo and her husband, Harold Norman, amid a domestic violence case involving the family.

The decision follows a meeting between the Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, and Mr Norman after his discharge from hospital.

Dr Lartey had earlier visited the family and interacted with Nana Akua Addo.

However, Mr Norman was unavailable at the time as he was receiving medical care.

During her subsequent engagement with Mr Norman, the Minister emphasised the need to protect the children from conflict and situations that could compromise their safety, emotional wellbeing and development.

The Ministry said social welfare officers would monitor the children’s welfare to help safeguard their interests and ensure their safety remains a priority.

It added that it would continue collaborating with the Police and other relevant institutions to support the family while investigations into the domestic violence case continue.

Ghana News.title: Benedict Okyere Yeboah: Ghana’s football problem goes beyond sacking a coach
Ghana News.content:
Sacking the coach is the easiest answer to Ghana’s football problems.

It is also unlikely to be the solution.

Carlos Queiroz has now left his position after Ghana opened the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign with defeats to Côte d’Ivoire and The Gambia. His seven-match spell produced one win, one draw and five defeats.

Those numbers are poor. They justify serious questions about the coaching period.

But they should not end the conversation.

Because Ghana's decline did not begin with Queiroz.

The evidence points to a deeper problem.

Ghana failed to qualify for AFCON 2025 after a qualifying campaign in which the Black Stars recorded three draws and three defeats, scoring only three goals in six matches and conceding seven.

That was before Queiroz's second spell.

At AFCON 2023, Ghana managed only two points from three group matches, failed to win a game and conceded six goals.

The pattern therefore stretches across different competitions and coaching periods.

Changing the manager repeatedly may change the tactics. It does not automatically change the football ecosystem producing the players, developing the clubs or preparing the national teams.

How many coaches do we need to change before we change the system?

Ghana has increasingly treated the national team coach as the central explanation for every failure.

But if different coaches inherit similar structural problems, eventually the question has to move beyond the dugout.

The Black Stars have experienced repeated coaching changes in recent years, while the underlying concerns around player development, club sustainability, infrastructure and football administration have remained.

The GFA itself acknowledged the seriousness of the problem after the AFCON 2025 failure.

In November 2024, it dissolved the Black Stars Management Committee and announced a Ghana Football Retreat involving stakeholders from football, government, education, finance, economics, marketing, former players and other sectors. The stated objective was to develop a roadmap for improving Ghana football.

That is significant.

It means the problem was already being recognised as bigger than the head coach.

The local league is part of the national team equation.

A national team cannot permanently operate as an island.

The domestic football system is supposed to develop players, coaches, referees, administrators and clubs capable of feeding the national teams.

Yet in March 2026, the GFA's Club Licensing Manager said that among the 18 Ghana Premier League clubs, only seven owned their own facilities and only four owned their own stadia.

That is a structural issue.

If elite clubs lack adequate infrastructure and sustainable commercial foundations, the national team cannot simply be expected to produce a continuous pipeline of elite players.

The government’s 2026–2029 Medium-Term Development Plan also identifies inadequate sports infrastructure in schools as a problem for early talent identification and systematic athlete development.

So the question is not simply:

“Who should coach the Black Stars?”

It is also:

“Where are we developing the next generation of Black Stars?”

Ghana has talent — but talent is not a development system.

This is perhaps the most important distinction.

Ghana continues to produce talented footballers.

Mohammed Kudus, Thomas Partey, Antoine Semenyo and numerous other Ghanaian players demonstrate that the talent pool has not disappeared.

The problem is whether Ghana consistently converts that talent into a strong national football system.

Interestingly, the GFA announced in August 2026 that it had invested GH¢1.8 million to train 600 Colts coaches through its CAF Licence D programme over two seasons. It also announced continued investment in youth competitions, equipment and regional development.

Those investments matter.

But they also highlight the scale of the challenge.

If grassroots coaching, facilities, scouting, competitions and player pathways are weak or inconsistent, improving one national-team camp will not fix the entire production line.

Money alone is not enough either

The GFA announced that every Ghana Premier League club would receive at least GH¢1 million ahead of the 2025/26 season, alongside equipment and logistical support.

That raises another important question:

What does the money build?

Does it create better academies?

Better pitches?

Professional commercial departments?

Improved scouting?

Youth development programmes?

Medical and sports-science structures?

Or does it simply help clubs survive another season?

Ghana's Sports Minister Kofi Iddie Adams raised essentially this issue in August 2026, arguing that football requires rebuilding from grassroots to the national level and questioning whether financial interventions were producing lasting institutional improvements.

That is where the conversation needs to go.

The Black Stars are a symptom, not the entire disease.

Consider the numbers.

AFCON 2023:

3 matches — 0 wins — 2 draws — 1 defeat — 5 goals scored — 6 conceded.

AFCON 2025 qualifying:

6 matches — 0 wins — 3 draws — 3 defeats — 3 goals scored — 7 conceded.

Queiroz's 2026 spell:

7 matches — 1 win — 1 draw — 5 defeats.

These numbers cannot simply be explained by one tactical system.

They represent a longer period of instability.

And that is why Ghana's next coaching appointment should be viewed as one component of a much larger football reform programme.

What actually needs fixing?

Ghana needs to examine the entire football pyramid:

Grassroots development

Identify talent earlier and create structured pathways from schools and Colts football into professional academies. Club development

Clubs need stronger ownership models, academies, facilities, commercial departments and revenue streams. Coaching development

The country needs more high-level coaches at youth and senior levels — not just a succession of expensive solutions for the Black Stars. Scouting

Ghana must build a modern national scouting network capable of identifying talent domestically and across the diaspora. Infrastructure

Training pitches, academies, medical facilities and performance centres cannot remain secondary issues. National-team continuity

The Black Stars need a football philosophy that survives individual coaching changes. Accountability

Success should be measured not only by whether Ghana qualifies for the next tournament, but by whether the football system is becoming stronger.

The uncomfortable truth

Ghana can sack Queiroz.

It can appoint another coach.

It can change the technical team.

It can even change the Black Stars management committee.

But if the same weaknesses remain underneath, the cycle simply starts again.

A new coach can improve a team.

A new football structure can improve a country.

That distinction matters.

The Black Stars' recent numbers are serious enough to demand action. But the statistics also tell us something else: the problem has lasted longer than any single coach.

Ghana therefore needs more than another coaching appointment.

It needs a football development strategy that connects schools, Colts football, academies, clubs, the Ghana Premier League, the diaspora and the national teams into one functioning pathway.

Because if Ghana only changes the man on the touchline, it may change the face of the problem without changing the system producing it.

The next coach should not be expected to rescue Ghanaian football alone.

That job belongs to the entire football system.

Ghana News.title: GPL 2026/27: Darkwah Wiafe’s winner sees All Blacks beat Kotoko
Ghana News.content:
Asante Kotoko suffered defeat on matchday six of the Ghana Premier League (GPL) following their loss to Swedru All Blacks.

The two teams faced off on Saturday, October 10, with Asante Kotoko hoping to make it two wins out of two since the departure of Eric Tinkler.

However, All Blacks condemned them to their second defeat of the camp, as they claimed a 1-0 win at home.

The Porcupine Warriors came into the fixture on the back of a narrow win over Karela United in their last game, while All Blacks came into this game having lost to Aduana Football Club in their last league outing.

Despite a confident start to the game in Swedru, Kotoko created very few chances but were kept in the game by their goalkeeper, who made numerous saves to keep out the threat of the home side, heading into the break at 0-0.

The return from recess saw a similar style, with All Blacks throwing everything at Kotoko, but once again Aziz Dari was on hand to keep his side in the game.

When it looked as if the Kumasi-based side were going to leave Swedru with a point, they conceded a penalty.

The penalty was converted by Darkwah Wiafe to give All Blacks all three points and move them to eight points after six games played.

They also go level with Kotoko who now have two wins, two draws and two defeats from six games so far this season.

Ghana News.content:
In an all-Indian clash for the boys’ singles title, Dev Vipul Patel won the final-week title of the Junior World Tennis Tour (J100 Accra), defeating compatriot Om Verma in a hard-fought, three-set battle: 6–3, 0–6, 6–4.

Patel seized the early momentum, controlling the opening set to win 6–3.

With ranking points and championship titles secured, these rising international stars delivered a memorable finale in Accra, leaving Ghana with renewed momentum as they continue to chase their professional tennis dreams.

The ninth edition of the ITF World Tennis Tour Juniors came to a thrilling conclusion on October 10 at the Accra Sports Stadium National Tennis Centre.

Organised in partnership with Tennis Foundation Ghana and the Ghana Tennis Federation, the six-week tournament reached its ultimate climax with high-stakes championship action.

Ghana News.title: Ghana must pursue BRICS partnership if it brings economic benefits – Kpebu
Ghana News.content:
Martin Kpebu

Legal practitioner and analyst Martin Kpebu says Ghana should pursue a partnership with the BRICS economic bloc if it offers tangible economic benefits to the country.

He argues that Ghana’s foreign policy should be guided by national interest rather than an exclusive alignment with traditional Western partners.

Speaking on TV3’s The Key Points, Mr Kpebu said the country must be willing to explore opportunities with different international partners, just as major global powers pursue relationships based on their own interests.

“I support Ghana becoming a partner, as long as it brings us economic development. We don't have much so if there is something to be gained from it, why not?” he said.

His comments come after Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa announced that the government had decided to formally apply for Ghana to join BRICS.

The government says the move is intended to diversify Ghana’s international partnerships, expand economic opportunities and strengthen cooperation with countries in the Global South.

Mr Kpebu dismissed concerns that Ghana’s engagement with BRICS would automatically undermine its longstanding relationship with the United States.

He noted that Ghana and the US have maintained diplomatic and economic ties over several decades, arguing that those relationships would not necessarily collapse because Ghana sought cooperation with other economic blocs.

“The U.S. is not going to run out of Ghana overnight because we join BRICS,” he said.

According to him, Ghana’s engagement with alternative economic partners could also encourage traditional allies to attach greater value to their relationship with the country.

He argued that international relations are driven largely by national interest, and Ghana should adopt a similar approach in determining its partnerships.

“What do we gain by continuing to say, ‘Oh, we are with the U.S., we are with the UK, so we can’t join BRICS?’” he asked.

Mr Kpebu further compared international relations to competition for attention, suggesting that Ghana’s willingness to explore other partnerships could strengthen its position in dealings with existing allies.

He clarified that his support was for Ghana pursuing partner status with BRICS rather than necessarily seeking full membership immediately.

“ As long as we’re going to get benefits, let’s go for it,” he said.

BRICS, originally formed by Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, has expanded to include additional members. The grouping seeks to strengthen economic cooperation and increase the influence of emerging economies in global affairs.

Mr Kpebu’s comments add to the debate over how Ghana can pursue new economic opportunities while managing its existing diplomatic relationships.

Ghana News.title: Success and Wright Claims J100 Accra Girls’ Doubles Championship

Success Ogunjobi of Nigeria and Sydney Wright of the United States were crowned Girls’ Doubles champions at the J100 Accra, Tennis Foundation Ghana Open .

Sydney Wright and Success Ogunjobi defeated Poland’s Alisha Ndukwu and Russia’s Milana Kolesova 6-3, 6-1 in a dominant final display at the Accra Sports Stadium National Tennis Centre.

Determined to complete a back-to-back title run, Wright set the tone alongside Ogunjobi with sharp communication and aggressive baseline play.

The pair worked in flawless sync, refusing to allow their top-ranked opponents any margin for error.

Success and Sydney started the match with total confidence dominating the opening set 6-3.

Ogunjobi and Wright accelerated through the second set, dropping just one game to wrap up the championship match with clinical efficiency.

Building on her doubles' victory,Wright maintained her winning streak with to win the girls' singles title.

For Ogunjobi, lifting the trophy showcased her great skill, teamwork, and determination on the big stage.

The tournament draws the curtain on a great six-week junior tour in Accra, marking the successful conclusion of the ninth edition of the ITF World Tennis Tour Juniors in Accra.

A major tournament on the international junior calendar, the Tennis Foundation Ghana Open continues to serve as a vital pathway for high-performance for junior players striving to make their mark on the global stage.

Ghana News.title: ITF J100: America’s Wright wins J100 Accra Girls’ Singles Title
Ghana News.content:
Third-seeded American Sydney Wright proved unstoppable at the ITF J100 Accra, concluding a six-week tournament run by defending her girls’ singles title in a thrilling final against Zimbabwe’s Kuzivaishe Chappa.

Wright reached her second consecutive Accra final after beating Poland’s top seed Alisha Ndukwu in a dramatic three-set semifinal.

Following her victory over Ndukwu in the previous week's championship match, a long, three-hour and 40 minute battle.

Wright showed great confidence once again.

In a tough match lasting 2 hours and 48 minutes, the American fought back from a set down to win 5-7, 6-2, 6-3.

Standing in Wright’s way was Chappa, who delivered a strong performance to eliminate seventh seed Parish Nikhil Shinde of India.

The Zimbabwean won a close first set in a tiebreak before Shinde took the second.

Staying focused on the final set, Chappa got a late break to claim a hard-fought 7-6(4), 4-6, 6-4 victory.

For Chapepa, reaching the singles final offered a chance at redemption after losing a close double final the week before alongside her sister, Kudzai Erin Patience Chapepa, against Ndukwu and Yelyzaveta Kolesova (7-6(4), 6-3).

In the Girls’ Singles final on October 10, Sydney Wright proved too strong, defeating Kuzivaishe Chappa in a fast and dominant performance giving Chappa no space to breathe in a 6-2, 6-0 victory to claim back-to-back J100 Accra Girls’ Singles titles.

The singles triumph completed a doubles sweep for Wright, who also lifted a trophy on October 9, alongside her doubles partner Ogunjobi, defeating top seeds Milana Kolesova and Alisha Ndukwu with a convincing 6-3, 6-1 win.

Now a multiple titleholder, Sydney Wright’s dominant week highlighted the big dreams of these rising young stars, who continue to chase global success, break barriers and inspire the next generation of tennis players across Africa and around the world.

Organised by Tennis Foundation Ghana in partnership with the Ghana Tennis Federation.

The ninth edition of the ITF Juniors World Tennis Tour came to an exciting end at the National Tennis Centre, Accra Sports Stadium.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Photos: Thousands march across Europe to demand end to Israel’s war on Gaza
World.content:
Several thousand pro-Palestinian protesters have marched through European capitals, demanding an end to Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

In London, demonstrators moved past the British parliament carrying placards reading “End the genocide” and “Free Palestine”.

“We are here today to mark three years of the ongoing genocide in Gaza,” Aimee Shalan, director of the Palestine Solidarity Campaign, told the AFP news agency, calling for “full sanctions on Israel”.

A so-called ceasefire took effect a year ago, but Israel continues to strike Gaza on a near-daily basis. The attacks have killed some 1,450 Palestinians since the truce began, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry.

London’s Metropolitan Police said they made “several arrests”, including a man and a woman holding placards supporting Palestine Action, a group banned under UK law.

Officers had also warned they would use public order powers to compel anyone wearing face coverings to remove them, pledging “zero tolerance” for hate crimes.

In Berlin, about 3,500 people joined a march organised by United for Palestine, police said, setting off from a square between the chancellery and parliament. Many condemned Germany’s arms exports and longstanding military support for Israel.

Similar marches were held in Warsaw and Rome, where protesters denounced ongoing Israeli bombardment and their governments’ ties with Israel, echoing calls for an immediate and lasting ceasefire.

Israel’s genocide has left most of Gaza in ruins and killed more than 74,200 Palestinians since October 2023.

World.title: Attack on airport in Saudi capital, Riyadh, leaves several injured
World.content:
Operations suspended at King Khalid International Airport after another attack this week, Civil Aviation Authority says.

Share Attack on airport in Saudi capital, Riyadh, leaves several injured on social media

The latest attack on King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia’s capital has injured several people, according to the country’s Civil Aviation Authority.

Operations at the airport in Riyadh were temporarily suspended after the attack on Saturday afternoon, said the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA). Its statement added that officials were assessing the damage and determining the exact number of injuries.

On Thursday, at least three Saudi citizens, including a pilot, were killed in Houthi attacks at the airport, according to GACA.

Those attacks were launched by Yemen’s Houthi group, which is at war with Riyadh and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government in Aden.

Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry, reporting from Yemen on Saturday, said the Houthis have yet to claim responsibility for the latest attack.

But the Iran-backed group has warned aviation companies to avoid using Saudi airspace, saying any aircraft operating there – except over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina – is a target.

Earlier on Saturday, King Khalid airport urged passengers to contact their airlines directly and check their flight status before heading to the airport amid reports of disruptions to air traffic. The airport did not specify the cause of the disruptions in its initial advisory.

Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs also instructed Saudi citizens travelling to the kingdom to contact local embassies if their travel itineraries have been disrupted following the attack.

Following reports of the latest attack, President Donald Trump was asked by reporters outside the White House whether the United States planned to join Saudi strikes on the Houthis.



“We may. We’re going to look at it. We just found out about the ⁠⁠⁠⁠recent attack, so we’ll make a decision. We move very quickly,” he said.

A ‘security situation’

At the same time, foreign embassies in Riyadh, including those of the US, the United Kingdom, Ireland and Canada, issued advisories on social media to their citizens in the kingdom.

The US mission said it was “aware of attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh” and “strongly recommends” all US citizens avoid the airport and surrounding areas.

The British and Irish embassies advised their nationals about “a serious incident” at the airport. Canada’s embassy advised citizens in Riyadh to avoid all travel to the airport, noting “ongoing military activity”.

Japan’s embassy “strongly” condemned Houthi attacks on airports and other Saudi civilian facilities.

Kuwait Airways said it was cancelling flights because the airport had closed due to a “security situation”.

On Thursday, the Houthi military spokesperson said that the Yemeni armed group had launched a ballistic missile towards the airport in Riyadh, claiming that the missile successfully hit its intended target, causing damage and disrupting air traffic.

Days earlier, alleged Houthi attacks on Abha and King Khalid airports killed three civilians and injured 36 others.

World.title: Nine killed in shooting in US state of Pennsylvania, including two children
World.content:
The shooting in Erie, Pennsylvania happened on Friday, according to state officials.

Share Nine killed in shooting in US state of Pennsylvania, including two children on social media

Nine people were killed Friday in a shooting in the US state of Pennsylvania, according to Governor Josh Shapiro. Police said the suspected shooter was among the nine dead.

Local media reported that two children were also among those killed at a home in Erie, Pennsylvania, which is 188 kilometres (117 miles) north of Pittsburgh.

Police in the city of Erie were called Friday around 5:00pm local time (21:00 GMT) to reports of shots fired and discovered two women dead in the street, the Erie News Now outlet said.

The attacker barricaded himself inside the home as police surrounded the building and ordered him to exit.

More gunshots were heard during the standoff, Erie News Now reported.

When police eventually entered the building, they found several more victims around the home, including the two children. The deceased attacker had an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, the outlet said, citing police.

Erie News Now said that police officers who responded to the scene were being offered counselling over the horrifying incident.

“I have not seen anything like this in my 28-plus years,” Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah told a local news station on Saturday. “I’m not sure that the city of Erie has ever seen the loss of life and the devastation that we just witnessed.”

Lorah declined to provide more details but said the circumstances of the shooting were “deeply disturbing”.

Shapiro said Saturday he offered his administration’s “full support” to Erie Mayor Daria Devlin.

Mass shootings occur frequently in the United States, where guns vastly outnumber the population and efforts to increase firearm restrictions face steep political and legal hurdles.

World.title: Pope says death penalty ‘inadmissible’ as US plans to livestream execution
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV describes capital punishment as an ‘attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person’ in post on X.

Share Pope says death penalty ‘inadmissible’ as US plans to livestream execution on social media

Pope Leo XIV has declared that the death penalty is “inadmissible” while his home country, the United States, announces plans to livestream an execution by firing squad.

Marking World Day Against the Death Penalty on Saturday, the pope reiterated the Catholic Church’s teaching on capital punishment, writing on X that it was “inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person”.

“The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment,” his post said.

“Effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption,” added the leader of the Catholic Church.

The American Pope’s comments come days after US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth said on Thursday that the firing squad execution of Nidal Malik Hasan on December 3 will be livestreamed.

Hasan was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 others in a shooting at the Fort Hood military base in 2009.

Pope Leo did not specifically refer to the planned execution, or last month’s botched execution attempt on Christa Pike, who survived two doses of the lethal injection in Tennessee.

But his post came hours after his top deputy, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican secretary of state, told Vatican News that the plan to livestream Hasan’s execution was “unacceptable”.

It was Leo’s predecessor, Pope Francis, in 2018 who first amended official Catholic teaching to declare capital punishment “inadmissible” in all circumstances.



Previously, the Catechism of the Catholic Church, the official compendium of church teaching, said the church did not exclude recourse to capital punishment “if this is the only possible way of effectively defending human lives against the unjust aggressor.”

The planned livestream of Hasan’s execution has sparked outrage across the US political divide. Republican representative Austin Scott said he supported executing Hassan but that “livestreaming executions is what Jihadists do. America is better than that.”

Senator Mark Kelly, a Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee, said Hasan should “face justice”, but that public executions are “the kind of thing that Iran and the Taliban do. Is this who we want to be associated with?”

On Thursday, a Pentagon official confirmed the plans, but on Friday, Vice President JD Vance, who is a practising Catholic, expressed doubt on whether the livestream would be going ahead, telling reporters that if it is, “I’m not going to be watching it.”

World.title: Christa Pike discharged from hospital and returned to Tennessee prison
World.content:
Christa Pike has been discharged from hospital and returned to a Tennessee women’s prison after surviving the US state’s attempt to execute her by lethal injection, her lawyers said on Saturday.

The 50-year-old is back in the Deborah K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center where she had been incarcerated for 30 years. She had been in hospital since September 30 when officials administered two doses of pentobarbital in an attempt to execute her.

Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 beating and stabbing of her classmate, Colleen Slemmer.

Her lawyers said she was continuing to receive medical care in prison and that they would monitor her recovery. They also expressed gratitude to the first responders and medical team who treated her.

The failed execution has drawn attention to the US death penalty as a separate controversy unfolds over the military’s plan to livestream the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan. The former army psychiatrist was convicted of killing 13 people at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009. His execution is scheduled for December 3.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s announcement on Thursday of the livestream drew criticism, even from some supporters of capital punishment. Vice President JD Vance questioned on Friday whether it would happen and said he would not watch. In a social media post, Republican Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina called the proposal “beyond disgusting”.

Archbishop Paul S Coakley, president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops, also condemned the plan, calling it “a barbaric promotion of a culture of death”.



In Tennessee, however, Pike’s failed execution has not prompted Republican legislators to reconsider capital punishment. Instead, some have discussed alternative methods, including the electric chair and firing squads.

Support for the death penalty in the US has declined from its peak in the 1990s. Ten states have abolished capital punishment since Pike was sentenced in 1996, but executions continue nationwide.

Thirty people have been executed in the US this year, with eight more scheduled, mostly in Texas and Florida.

A Pew Research Center poll in July found that about two-thirds of US adults considered the death penalty morally justified for people convicted of murder. But roughly six in 10 said it did not deter crime, while about seven in 10 said there was some risk of an innocent person being executed.

World.title: Celebrations in Ethiopian city after reported Eritrean ‘incursion’
World.content:
NewsFeed Celebrations in Ethiopian city after reported Eritrean ‘incursion’

People in a city in northern Ethiopia have been celebrating after the reported withdrawal of Eritrean forces accused of an incursion. Pro-government troops were seen on the streets of Adigrat, but Eritrea has denied its forces have entered the region of Tigray.

World.title: Eritrea urges UN to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia
World.content:
The neighbouring countries blame one another for starting war amid heightened tensions and fears of a wider conflict.

Share Eritrea urges UN to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia on social media

Eritrea has asked the United Nations to take “deterrent measures” after what it called Ethiopia’s “declaration of war” in the conflict over the Tigray region.

Eritrea’s request comes a day after Addis Ababa, in a letter to the Security Council, accused Asmara of launching an “all-out invasion”, saying Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 kilometres (37 miles) into Ethiopia’s Tigray.

In a separate letter to the council on Saturday, Eritrean Foreign Minister Osman Saleh said the claims of an Eritrean incursion were part of an Ethiopian plan to justify a war of aggression and urged the UN to intervene, invoking Chapter VII of the UN Charter, which allows measures from sanctions to military action.

The neighbouring countries have accused each other of starting a war over Tigray, where Ethiopia says Eritrea is backing rebels.

An alliance of seven armed groups launched attacks against federal Ethiopian forces in the northern region last month, as they attempt to overthrow Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government.

Eritrean forces have since reportedly intruded into Ethiopian territory, with Addis Ababa accusing Asmara of backing the rebel Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF).

The Ethiopian army pushed TPLF rebels back this week and seized the region’s capital, Mekelle. It also said it launched drone strikes against Eritrean troops in the region.

“Eritrea requests the UN Security Council to forcefully condemn Ethiopia’s deplorable declaration of war against Eritrea … and take the requisite deterrent measures,” Eritrea’s Saleh said in the letter on Saturday.



He said Ethiopia’s action would cause “huge devastation to the peoples of both countries and destabilise the whole region”.

Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos on Friday accused Eritrea of “a blatant act of aggression that engages Ethiopia’s inherent right to self-defence”.

Timothewos invoked Ethiopia’s right to self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter, but he did not specify what measures the country was taking.

Faisal Roble, a Horn of Africa specialist, believes both sides are “preparing for the last phase of an open conflict”.

“There is really no doubt that both of them are inching towards an open conflict,” he told Al Jazeera from the Kenyan capital, Nairobi.

“Whatever they write to the United Nations, it is just posturing and making sure that they have some sort of international support on their side,” the analyst added.

‘Deceitful attempts’

In his letter, Saleh called Ethiopia’s actions “deceitful attempts to rationalise its brazen acts of war”, claiming that they were “hollow in substance”.

Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel accused Ethiopia on Friday of pursuing aggression against Eritrea through its demands for sovereign access to the Red Sea. Writing on X, he did not explicitly confirm or deny the reported troop crossings.

Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy reiterated on Monday that Ethiopia must have access to the Red Sea.

Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993, and they fought a deadly border war from 1998 to 2000.

Relations improved after Abiy came to power in 2018, but have soured again in recent years.

Landlocked Ethiopia has repeatedly insisted that it has a right to direct sea access, which Eritrea interprets as a threat to invade and seize its port at Assab.

TPLF fighters battled Ethiopian government forces, then backed by Eritrea, in a devastating 2020-2022 war.

World.title: Hurricane Isaias leaves two dead and 800,000 without power in US Southeast
World.content:
Storm damage stretches across Florida and Alabama as officials warn of continued flooding and possible tornadoes.

Share Hurricane Isaias leaves two dead and 800,000 without power in US Southeast on social media

Hurricane Isaias, the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season, has killed two people and left hundreds of thousands of customers without power across the southeastern United States.

The storm made landfall near Destin, Florida, on Friday evening as a Category 2 hurricane before weakening as it moved inland through Alabama overnight.

One person died in Birmingham, Alabama, when a tree fell on a house overnight, according to local emergency officials. A second person was killed in Escambia County, Florida, after a tree fell during the storm, according to local authorities.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said on Saturday that state officials had not confirmed any storm-related fatalities, including the report from Escambia County.

Isaias hit land with sustained winds of 169km/h (105mph), bringing powerful gusts and heavy rain to the Florida Panhandle. By Saturday morning, the storm had weakened to a post-tropical cyclone with wind speeds of about 55km/h (35mph).

More than 900,000 electricity customers in Florida, Alabama and Georgia were without power early Saturday morning. That number has since gone down to under 800,000, according to PowerOutage.us.

Fallen trees and downed power lines caused widespread disruption, while flooding forced road closures in parts of southern Alabama, including Houston County. Alabama Governor Kay Ivey said on Saturday morning that her team was concerned about “strong winds, heavy rain and possible spinoff tornadoes”.



Local officials in Pensacola, Florida reported strong winds that damaged an airport and tore the roof off a hotel. Trees and power lines also came down across the city, leaving some residents without electricity and roads blocked.

Despite the storm’s weakening, officials warned that dangerous conditions could persist. Heavy rainfall threatened flash flooding across parts of the Southeast.

“The flooding story is not over,” DeSantis said on Saturday, warning that saturated ground and continued rainfall could cause dangerous flooding a day or two after the storm passed. He said state search and rescue resources would remain available in case rapidly rising waters required emergency rescues.

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier also warned residents to be alert for contractors seeking to exploit storm victims as homeowners begin repairing damaged properties.

World.title: 'Time for Ukraine to get new president,' says Trump after Zelensky condemns diesel deal
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has said he thinks "it's time for Ukraine to get a new president" as he responded to Volodymyr Zelensky's criticism of the US diesel deal with Russia.

The Ukrainian president warned a new deal to release millions of tonnes of Russian diesel into the US would provide Moscow with money to continue its war against his nation, calling it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Trump told reporters outside the White House on Saturday that Zelensky "wants to make problems for the world" by continuing to authorise attacks on Russian refineries.

"He'd better damn well stop," Trump said, before suggesting Ukraine should "get a new leader who can make a deal".

Russia and Ukraine have recently intensified their strikes, targeting energy-generating and transport facilities, as well as major logistics hubs.

"We said, 'you can do whatever you want to Russia, don't hit the refineries', because that's a world problem that's caused," he said.

"He could have made many deals and for some reason, he never does."

Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev described Trump's intervention as "iconic and historic", saying that Ukraine "needs leadership actually focused on peace".

The US president confirmed on Friday that an agreement had been reached with Moscow to suspend sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April.

Zelensky reacted by saying it would allow Moscow to raise new funds to source new military equipment to continue the war.

He also accused Moscow of taking the deal "to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they keep dropping bombs on cities" following deadly new strikes on Zaporizhzhia.

World.title: Russian glide bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia kills at least 15 people
World.content:
Russia has attacked the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia with five glide bombs, killing at least 15 people including three children, officials said.

The glide bombs hit residential buildings in the south-eastern city on Saturday morning. At least 16 others were injured in the attack, with more still missing and believed to be under the rubble.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the attacks on Zaporizhzhia were Russia expressing "its thanks" for a deal announced by US President Donald Trump last night easing sanctions on Moscow to import Russian diesel.

He added that 13 other regions had come under attack overnight, arguing this demonstrated Russia took "any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting".

Photos and videos from the site of one of the strikes in Zaporizhzhia show an apartment block mostly destroyed.

"The ground floor was hit, and the floors above just collapsed," acting Mayor Regina Kharchenko told Ukrainian television from the scene.

She said more than 80 workers were involved in ongoing search and rescue operations which are expected to continue throughout the day.

The rescuers regularly stop to listen for any noises made by survivors who could be under the rubble.

Kharchenko said Russia had struck at "our very heart" and "our littlest ones" were among those killed, adding that their deaths were "awful grief for their families. For the city."

Zaporizhzhia is a major regional centre with more than 700,000 residents. It is located less than 10 miles (16km) from the front line and is frequently attacked by Russian drones and missiles.

World.title: Several injured in attack on airport in Saudi capital Riyadh
World.content:
Several people have been injured in another attack on an international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh, authorities say, days after Yemen's Houthis claimed to have carried out similar strikes on the hub.

Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh were suspended on Saturday after the attack, the Saudi Civil Aviation Authority said in a statement.

More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport, according to news agency Reuters, citing an eyewitness.

The US embassy said it was "aware of attacks on King Khalid International Airport" and urged American citizens to avoid the airport and surrounding areas.

The attack comes a day after authorities said three Saudis including a pilot were killed in two attacks on the airport by the Iran-backed Houthis the day prior. Another three people were killed in Houthi attacks on two Saudi airports on 6 and 7 October.

A source at a local hospital told AFP that dozens of people had been wounded in Saturday's attack.

"I saw 401 hit, I saw injured in front of my eyes. Everyone was running," an eyewitness who said they had been at gate 401 in the domestic terminal told the news agency.

Western embassies in Saudi Arabia have warned their citizens away from the airport, while the UK Foreign Office told British nationals to stay away "until the airport is secure and to monitor the advice of the Saudi authorities".

Several Gulf airlines said they had cancelled their flights to and from the airport, with Kuwait Airways citing the "security situation" there.

All flights to Riyadh have either been diverted or cancelled, aviation tracker Flightradar shows.

Doctors had been asked to report to hospitals to address the situation, a medical source told AFP.

"We were told we are dealing with a 'serious emergency situation'," the medical source told the agency.

The suspected attack comes during a marked escalation in renewed fighting between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the Houthis, who control most of the country's north-west.

The Houthis say they are targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war.

The conflict worsened after the Houthis seized strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast in a rapid offensive.

That included the port of Mokha on the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which is the narrowest point of the Red Sea and a chokepoint for global shipping. Yemeni pro-government forces have since said they had "secured" the strait at the southern end of the Red Sea.

A Saudi-led coalition was formed in 2015 after Arab countries joined forces to stop the Houthis taking over Yemen from the country's internationally recognised government.

A temporary ceasefire was brokered in 2022 after years of air strikes and ground fighting led to the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people, triggering one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

But the informal truce began to unravel in July.

The Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. They said they were retaliating against what they described as a years-long Saudi blockade and for an air strike on Sanaa airport.

World.title: US murderer Christa Pike discharged from hospital 10 days after failed execution
World.content:
US death row inmate Christa Pike has been discharged from hospital following her botched execution at the end of last month, her lawyers have said.

Pike, 50, has been sent back to the prison where she has spent the last 30 years and is continuing to receive medical care, according to a statement from her lawyers on Saturday.

She survived two lethal injections of the drug pentobarbital on 30 September, which left her in a critical condition.

Pike regained consciousness earlier this week and began speaking - stunning experts, medical staff and her lawyers.

Her case is now in uncharted territory as she is thought to be the only person to have survived an execution attempt by lethal injection.

Pike's lawyers said in their statement that she was "grateful to the first responders and her medical team for their care in these extraordinary circumstances".

It is unclear what medical care Pike is receiving now that she is back in prison but her lawyers previously said she faced a "long road to recovery".

The Tennessee Department of Correction is yet to say why the execution did not go as planned, though it has defended the method it used.

World.title: 'Cockroach' group leaders among hundreds detained in Delhi protest
World.content:
Hundreds of protesters have been detained in Delhi during the latest demonstration by the Gen-Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) calling for electoral reforms.

The group said its founder Abhijeet Dipke - who began the movement in May after India's Chief Justice likened some jobless young people to "cockroaches" - was detained with other leaders shortly after landing in Delhi.

Tens of thousands of security personnel were deployed and roads barricaded ahead of the demonstration, though the CJP insisted it would go ahead.

Delhi Police has not commented on the detentions, but had refused permission for the protest to take place at Jantar Mantar, a landmark in the Indian capital.

The group - who are not registered as a political party in India - are seeking electoral reforms just months before crucial state elections.

It has also demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of manipulating voters' lists - which the Election Commission has denied.

Under Kumar's leadership, India's election commission has undertaken a mammoth exercise to update electoral rolls nationwide - it said this was a routine exercise to weed out dead, duplicate or ineligible voters.

But in many states, the exercise has been shrouded in controversy, with tens of thousands of people alleging they have been wrongly removed.

The CJP - and opposition parties - accuse Kumar of favouring Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in the way the electoral rolls are being updated.

The Election Commission and the BJP have denied this.

Before arriving in Delhi, the CJP's founder Dipke said: "If you think you can stop us by threatening us with jail or trying to intimidate us with the fear of imprisonment, you are mistaken."

He and and two other leaders, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, were detained on their flight from Mumbai on Saturday.

The group claimed the three men have been taken to an undisclosed location. Delhi Police have not commented.

World.title: Woman injures three people in third Poland school knife attack in a week
World.content:
A woman has been arrested after injuring three people in a third knife attack recorded at schools in Poland this week.

The 21-year-old used a "dangerous object" to attack a 17-year-old girl at an educational institution in the capital, Warsaw, police told news agencies PAP and AP.

It comes a day after thousands of police visited schools across Poland, following two stabbing attacks earlier in the week, one of which led to the killing of a female caretaker.

A Warsaw police spokesperson said they could not confirm whether the latest incident was related to the two previous attacks.

Authorities told local media that the 17-year-old injured on Saturday had been taken to hospital, but her condition was not life-threatening.

Two other women aged 17 and 24, who had gone in to submit enrolment documents, were also injured, Poland's state news agency reported.

Police told local media that the suspected attacker was a student at the school and initial findings suggested that she did not know the three victims.

Schools in Poland had been stepping up security following knife attacks at schools across the country on 7 and 8 October. Polish police said they had detained 76 people after deploying to schools across the country.

"When it comes to the safety of Polish children and peace in our schools, there is no room for compromise," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said ahead of the operation.

Local media, citing a police spokesperson, reported authorities had information to suggest incidents this past week could be related to an internet challenge.

On Wednesday, a 19-year-old student attacked and injured nine people at a vocational school in the central Polish province of Mazovian.
