A day later, a 37-year-old caretaker was killed after a 15-year-old entered a primary school in LeszczydÃ³Å-Nowiny, north of Warsaw.

Interior Minister Marcin KierwiÅski also said a 17-year-old was detained in the town of Sierpc, north-west of Warsaw, after allegedly stating "on school grounds that he planned to do something... dangerous - that he intended to harm someone".

World.title: Expedition hopes to find aviator Amelia Earhart's plane on remote island
World.content:
A team of researchers are on their way to a remote island to inspect what they think could be the wreckage of famed aviator Amelia Earhart's plane.

The group, from the US-based Archaeological Legacy Institute (ALI) and Purdue University, are expected to arrive at Nikumaroro Island in the Pacific Ocean by Monday in the hopes of solving the mystery of her disappearance.

The American pioneer vanished while attempting to circumnavigate the globe in 1937, spawning decades of speculation on her fate.

The team are aiming to find what has been called the Taraia Object, first spotted sitting on the edge of a lagoon off Nikumaroro in satellite imagery in 2020.

Purdue University said the object had since been confirmed to have been visible in aerial photography of the area dating back to 1938.

The researchers are currently roughly halfway through their journey to the remote atoll aboard the Marin Mainiku, a Kiribati National Shipping Line vessel.

They departed the capital of Kiribati on Wednesday to begin the 830-mile journey to Nikumaroro, which is also part of the multi-island country.

When they eventually arrive, they will have to navigate through a narrow gap created in the atoll's reef created by the British in 1963 - the last time the island was inhabited.

"Finding Amelia Earhart's Electra aircraft would be the discovery of a lifetime," Richard Pettigrew, head of the ALI and the expedition lead, said.

World.title: Nobel peace laureate says US sanctions on ICC 'unacceptable'
World.content:
Navi Pillay, the winner of this year's Nobel Peace Prize, has called US sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) "unheard of" and "unacceptable".

The South African former ICC judge was awarded the prize on Friday "for her efforts to promote peace and international law", which paved the way for a "more comprehensive global legal order", the Nobel committee said.

US President Donald Trump expressed his disatisfaction with the pick and hours later the US unveiled sweeping sanctions in a significant acceleration of its attempt to "dismantle" what it described as a "rogue" institution.

The ICC said the measures were an assault on the rule of law and the foundations of the international legal order.

Pillay, speaking via video link during an event at the Nobel Peace Center in Oslo on Saturday, said: "There is so much tension and anxiety over the continued existence of international courts, mainly the International Criminal Court in The Hague.

"Most importantly, sanctions have been announced by one country against the judges, just for the judicial orders they issue. This is unheard of, unacceptable."

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio earlier said the sanctions - which include a ban on US entities making transactions with the ICC - were intended to "defend US sovereignty" and accused the court of seeking to prosecute Americans.

The US has already sanctioned 17 ICC judges and officials, but this move sanctions the court itself as an institution and is intended to inhibit its ability to operate financially.

However, the US has provided a six-month grace period before some of these latest sanctions kick in, meaning member states can keep paying for its operations - a move Washington says is to allow countries time to negotiate a "solution to address" US concerns.

The Trump administration claims that the ICC is run by what it calls globalists who threaten American sovereignty.

It is furious over a past investigation into actions of US soldiers in Afghanistan the court has since closed and by its arrest warrants for Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The new sanctions, however, do not say that those warrants must be withdrawn before the measures can be lifted.

UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres called the US decision "a serious blow to our collective pursuit of international criminal justice, of which the ICC is a key pillar".

The UK joined Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan and the Netherlands in saying they "regret and strongly disagree with" the sanctions.

World.title: Military troops kill 36 terrorists, rescue 50 abductees, achieve other successes – DHQ
World.content:
The Defence Headquarters (DHQ) says troops rescued no fewer than 50 abducted persons, killed 36 terrorists and arrested several suspected terrorists and collaborators during operations across the country from 2 to 8 October.

The Director, Defence Media Operations, Michael Onoja, a major general, said this in a statement on Saturday about ongoing military operations during the period under review.

Mr Onoja said the troops recorded significant successes across various theatres, including foiling an ISWAP assault on Kukawa, Borno, rescuing 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members in Imo and ‘neutralising’ a senior ISWAP commander in Ondo.

He said troops of Operation Hadin Kai killed 26 terrorists during engagements in Borno and Yobe, including 25 who attempted to infiltrate Kukawa town.

According to him, troops also rescued several abductees, including three persons held for seven years, while arresting suspected terrorist collaborators, logistics suppliers and smugglers in Borno, Yobe and Adamawa.

In the North-west, Mr Onoja said the troops of Operation Fansan Yamma killed 10 Lakurawa terrorists during an encounter with a large group of fighters in Maiyama Local Government Area of Kebbi State.

He added that troops recovered 17 motorcycles, a machine gun, an AK-47 rifle, ammunition and a communication device during the operation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“They also rescued 18 kidnap victims in Katsina and a seven-year-old boy abducted in Kaduna, while arresting suspected terrorists and collaborators.

“In the South-east, troops of Operation Udo Ka rescued 20 prospective corps members abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha Expressway in Imo, alongside a local woman abducted while travelling to the market.

“The victims were rescued at Ndegwu Community in Owerri West LGA following sustained pressure by troops and other security agencies,” he said.

The defence spokesperson said a combined security team killed Abdussamad Ohida, a senior ISWAP commander, in Owo forest, Ondo State, on 2 October.

He said Ohida was deputy to the ISWAP Central Nigeria leader and assumed leadership after the leader was arrested by the State Security Services in 2023.

He said investigations revealed that the commander had been planning large-scale attacks on citizens in some southern states ahead of the forthcoming festive season.

In the North-central, Mr Onoja said troops of Operation Savannah Shield arrested a wanted terrorist in Niger State and rescued three persons who had escaped from their abductors in a forest in Kwara State.

He added that troops of Operation Enduring Peace also arrested two suspected kidnappers in Kaduna, while Operation Whirl Stroke recovered illegal firearms and ammunition during raids in Taraba State.

In the South-south, Mr Onoja said that troops of Operation Delta Safe discovered three illegal refinery sites in Rivers and recovered about 2,500 litres of suspected stolen Premium Motor Spirit.

He said the successes reflected the military’s sustained efforts to dismantle terrorist networks, rescue abducted citizens and disrupt criminal logistics.

Mr Onoja said the Chief of Defence Staff, Olufemi Oluyede, commended troops for their courage and professionalism and urged them to remain vigilant as the festive season approaches.

He added that Mr Oluyede, a general, also called for stronger collaboration among security agencies and urged community leaders and citizens to report individuals providing support to terrorists and other criminal groups.

(NAN)

World.title: 2027: Makinde promises four-year transitional Government of National Unity if elected president
World.content:
The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has promised to establish a four-year transitional Government of National Unity (GNU), if elected President in 2027.

He said his administration would promote inclusivity and prevent the concentration of power in one part of the country.

Mr Makinde who is also the governor of Oyo State, made the promise on Saturday at the APM North-east 2027 Town Hall Meeting in Yola, Adamawa State

He said the proposed GNU, which he promised would not last beyond four years, would prioritise national unity and address concerns about political representation and the exclusion of some sections of the country.

“I stand before you today to tell you that the government you will put in place from May 29, 2027, will be a transitional government of national unity. Our government will not last beyond four years. And it will be an all-inclusive government,” he said.

The APM flagbearer explained that the arrangement was intended to address concerns, particularly in Northern Nigeria, about ensuring that political power was not concentrated in one part of the country to the disadvantage of others.

Mr Makinde also pledged that his administration would pursue solutions to Nigeria’s security and economic challenges through public consultation, transparency and what he described as sincere leadership.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the party had delayed releasing its manifesto to allow its presidential candidate to listen to citizens and understand their concerns before finalising its policy proposals.

“Our manifesto is on the way. We have deliberately delayed its release because we wanted to hear from you at this level,” he said.

Mr Makinde said his proposed administration would avoid what he described as the politics of lies and deceit, adding that it would listen to citizens and consider solutions from different sections of the country.

“2027 will mark the end of the politics of lies and deceit. It is a time when we will all come together to establish a reset agenda and tell Nigerians the whole truth,” he said.

Makinde demands disclosure of petrol pricing template

The APM candidate also challenged the federal government to publish its petroleum pricing template to enable Nigerians to understand how the prices of petroleum products are determined.

He said the government should make the document available for public scrutiny, arguing that citizens outside government could also contribute ideas towards resolving the country’s economic problems.

Mr Makinde made the demand while criticising the federal government’s handling of electricity, energy security and petroleum pricing.

He recalled President Bola Tinubu’s campaign promise to fix Nigeria’s electricity supply within four years, saying the administration had failed to fulfil its commitments.

“The current administration came in and told us that it had the magic wand to solve the challenges confronting us. As a matter of fact, the president said that if he failed to fix electricity for Nigeria in four years, Nigerians should not vote for him again.

“So, we are all aware that they have failed to provide electricity and other things they promised,” he said.

He also criticised the government’s Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) and electric vehicle policy, as well as its Naira-for-Crude initiative, describing the policies as failures.

The presidential candidate said he had listened to concerns about insecurity and poverty during visits to the North-west and North-central regions, while participants at the Yola meeting also raised concerns about electricity and energy security.

He urged the federal government to explain the basis for its petroleum pricing decisions, particularly following the finance minister’s reported comments on adopting price modulation for petroleum products.

“We are asking for only two things. We do not want too much grammar; we just want relief for Nigerians. So, we ask the federal government to release its pricing template so that citizens will know how they arrived at the current petroleum price,” Mr Makinde, who was a player in the oil sector, said.

He added that Nigerians with relevant knowledge and expertise should be allowed to contribute to policy discussions, regardless of whether they held public office.

“The fact that you are in government or the Presidential Villa does not make you the only Nigerians with sense. We have other citizens who can dissect issues and proffer solutions,” he said.

Mr Makinde said his proposed administration would seek solutions to the country’s challenges without undermining citizens’ rights or playing politics with issues affecting their welfare.

Bala Mohammed backs Makinde’s presidential ambition

The National Leader of the APM and Governor of Bauchi State, Bala Mohammed, expressed support for Mr Makinde’s presidential ambition, describing the party as a political force with elected officials and members experienced in governance.

Mr Mohammed said the party had continued to attract new members and expressed confidence in its capacity to contribute to Nigeria’s political development.

He welcomed the presidential candidate to the North-east and said the party supported inclusivity, mutual respect and opportunities for people from different parts of the country.

“We believe in Nigeria. We believe in the Nigerian state. We are patriots. We believe in giving people opportunities from all sections of the country,” he said.

Mr Mohammed also expressed support for Mr Makinde’s proposed agenda to reset the country.

The APM’s vice presidential candidate, Lawal Daura, said the party intended to campaign on a platform of honesty, patriotism and a commitment to addressing Nigeria’s challenges.

He said the party would present details of its proposals when its national campaign commenced.

Mr Daura argued that Nigeria needed a reset to address its persistent challenges and called on Nigerians committed to public service to support the party’s agenda.

“It is not an easy task, and it will only require very serious-minded Nigerians to be in APM. But we are determined to reset Nigeria for the good of all,” he stated.

World.title: Ondo govt, police commence investigations as Akure residents choke under recurring offensive odour
World.content:
Some residents of Akure, the Ondo State capital, have cried out for help over a “mysterious” gaseous emission, accompanied by a pungent and poisonous odour, sporadically released into the air.

Reports from different parts of the town where the smell has been noticed indicated that the emission curiously occurs in the wee hours when residents are asleep.

Residents who perceived the smell reported that the emission, which slowly diffuses through windows, has suffocating properties, thereby aggravating the medical conditions of those with health challenges.

Although the residents started perceiving the odour about a month ago, the Ondo State Government and its relevant agencies have yet to properly designate the properties of the emission or pinpoint the its actual source. Complaints and enquiries from the residents have also remained largely unattended to.

Meanwhile, the suspicion that the emission could be a likely attack from mischief makers is gaining ascendancy given the choking effect of the smell.

A former Commissioner for Information in the state, Bamidele Ademola-Olateju, who said she percieved the odour at about 12.30 a.m. on Saturday 3 October, suspected it was coming from a poisonous gas.

Mrs Ademola-Olateju, who resides in Alagbaka 2 area of the city, said she suffered a severe attack that night, noting that it was aggravated by her asthmatic condition.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“It is a gas coming from somewhere. I have been noticing the odour for some time now, but the early hours of Saturday were particularly bad.

“I think it started around 12.30 a.m., I could not sleep through the night. By 2 a.m, I was choking. Being asthmatic, I used my inhaler, but the e inhaler did not work. I was miserable. Trying to close the windows and doors did not help. The gas only petered out at about 4 a.m.,” she said.

The former commissioner said the intensity of the smell could have killed a toddler suffering from the same medical condition.

She noted that speculations from the authorities that the odour could be emanating from organic materials may not be true, as organic materials could also be poisonous.

Mrs Ademola-Olateju warned that those releasing the poisonous gas could have sinister motives and could endanger the lives of the people, if nothing is done urgently to address the situation.

She further highlighted the curious coincidence of a similar occurrence in Ekiti which started in April this year, with reports that residents of Ado Ekiti are still being subjected to the same odour.

“This might be the work of terrorists, who might be testing things in the South-west region. It is happening in Ondo and Ekiti states at the same time,” she said.

Busuyi Mekusi, a professor of African Literature at the Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba Akoko, told PREMIUM TIMES that despite the complaints more than a month ago, “the offensive odour is still there, but comes in scattered days and night hours.”

Mr Mekusi, who lives in Gloryland Community, Sango, off Ado Road, Akure, said he and members of his family are among the many residents going through the harrowing experience.

“The one for last night was mild, but last Saturday/Sunday was terribly awful, with suffocating effects,” he said.

“Closing windows did not help, and I had to wear a nose mask to ensure a little sleep. I always pity my wife, who is always worse hit, as she could not stand wearing a mask to sleep.

“I must confess to you, it is simply distressing, and I only hope it does not pose existential threats, even as we seem helpless.”

Moses Ozonuwe, a police officer, lives in Igoba, in Akure North Local Government Area. Although, he was recently transferred out of Akure, Mr Ozonuwe received a complaint from members of his family concerning the pungent smell.

“My people reported to me that the pungent smell is real, especially during the night,” he told this newspaper.

“Since it is predominantly strong mostly in the night, I have advised them to ensure that all windows and doors are properly closed.”

Meanwhile, residents have criticised the state government for its slow response to the situatiom, and called for urgent action in order to forestall epidemiological issues.

Preliminary findings by the government in its initial response ruled out the Ala River as the source of the emission, but it described the situation as “purely a case of air pollution arising from the release of certain organic compounds into the atmosphere.”

The state Commissioner for Environment, Tob Loko, in a statement, merely advised residents in affected areas to limit their exposure and wear nose masks while investigations continued.

On his part, the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Idowu Ajanaku, said recently that the government had taken steps to clear the environment of any likely source of poisonous odours, and clearing of canals, assuring that the Akure environment is safe and clear enough for public safety.

He noted that if smells were still perceived anywhere, residents should check for dump sites and other likely sources of dirt for the purpose of clearing them.

“The government has taken steps to ensure a clean and safe environment,” Mr Ajanaku said. “We have also ensured that industries that could emit poisonous gases are not situated near residential areas of the city.”

READ ALSO: Security forces kill ISWAP commander in Ondo forest

The state police command said it has commenced an investigation to ascertain the facts surrounding the emission just as it called for calm.

“The Ondo State Police Command is aware of complaints by residents of Akure concerning the offensive odour reportedly experienced in some parts of the city,” police spokesperson, Jimoh Abayomi, said.

“The command considers the situation a matter of public concern, particularly in view of its potential health and safety implications and has commenced an investigation in collaboration with relevant government agencies to ascertain its source and determine whether any criminal elements are involved.

“The command assures the public of its unwavering commitment to protecting lives and property. Residents are urged to remain calm, refrain from spreading unverified information and promptly report any suspicious activities or useful information that could aid the ongoing investigation to the nearest police station.”

World.title: Regina Daniels reveals why she’s celebrating her 25th birthday in wheelchair
World.content:
Nollywood actress Regina Daniels has spoken about her prolonged health challenges, revealing that she has endured intense pain and struggled with mobility for months.

She shared this in a video on Instagram on Saturday to celebrate her 25th birthday.

Regina, who said she was gradually recovering, also explained her lengthy absence from social media.

According to her, what began as a seemingly minor health problem deteriorated over time, leaving her unable to move around comfortably.

The mother of two said: “I know many of you may be surprised seeing me in a wheelchair. Well, welcome to another chapter of my life. Let me walk you through what my life has been since many of you have asked questions about my absence. So today is the perfect day to respond to those who genuinely care. For several months now, I have lost my freedom to move around as I please.

“It started as something minor, very minor, but eventually led to this. But things took a major turn after the last public gathering I hosted, my children’s day carnival. One test after another, I jokingly started calling myself elaborate. The pain became- how can I explain this? The pain became excruciating. Sometimes I can walk, and sometimes I can’t move. I cried.”

Healing

Regina added that she was seeking God’s peace and looking to Him for healing as she navigated this difficult period in her life.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She said her fate remained in God’s hands and questioned how her condition had left her incapacitated despite once being full of energy.

The actress also expressed concern about her growing dependence on outside help to do even the simplest tasks.

“Well, me sitting here today, in front of this camera, sharing this y’all, it’s because there’s been some really significant developments in my recovery. And I say, thank you, Lord. I decided to move somewhere closer to my loves, and most importantly, to my heart, my babies. At first, I rented this place.

“But from the moment I set foot here, I just, I just had this need to own. Now, here is the juiciest part. From the day I made a down payment on this house, everything in here came as a gift. Look at my furniture. I mean, this beautiful, timeless piece was gifted to me by an adorable woman who a very special somebody introduced me to. My hairstylist, Ellie.”

Backstory

The actress described this year as one marked by God’s abundant blessings, expressing gratitude for what He had done in her life and what He was yet to accomplish.

“In any situation I find myself, I will continuously give all glory and adoration to God Almighty for what He’s done in my life, what He’s doing, and what He’s yet to do. So help me, God.”

In May, Regina dismissed the possibility of remarrying following the collapse of her marriage to Ned Nwoko, the senator representing Delta North.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the actress and Mr Nwoko dominated public discourse between October 2025 and early 2026 amid allegations of drug abuse, domestic violence and other related claims.

Since the former couple threatened legal action against each other, neither has shared much about their relationship or family life, including issues concerning their children.

However, Regina’s mother, Rita Daniels, recently dismissed online reports that the actress had reconciled with the lawmaker.

World.title: Nigerian govt speaks on Fitch’s credit rating
World.content:
The Federal Government says Fitch Ratings’ decision to revise Nigeria’s credit rating outlook from Stable to Positive reflects progress in economic reforms, foreign exchange market adjustments and efforts to strengthen the country’s external position.

Fitch announced the revision on 9 October, retaining Nigeria’s long-term foreign-currency issuer default rating at ‘B’.

In a statement issued on Saturday, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said Fitch cited increased foreign exchange reserves, easing inflation and improved economic prospects among the factors supporting the outlook revision.

According to the minister, Nigeria’s gross foreign exchange reserves rose to $54.9 billion as of 25 September 2026, from $32 billion in mid-April 2024.

He attributed the increase to more formalised foreign exchange transactions, portfolio inflows, higher exports and remittances.

Fitch also projected that Nigeria would record a current account surplus equivalent to 6.4 per cent of gross domestic product in 2026.

Economic growth and inflation

The ratings agency projected that Nigeria’s real gross domestic product would grow by 4.3 per cent in 2026, compared with 4 per cent in 2025, with growth remaining above 4 per cent in 2027 and 2028.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Fitch expects non-oil activities to remain the main driver of economic expansion.

The projection comes as Nigeria’s economy recorded growth of 4.43 per cent year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS).

The figure was higher than the 3.89 per cent recorded in the first quarter of 2026 and the 4.23 per cent recorded in the corresponding quarter of 2025.

The World Bank’s October 2026 Nigeria Development Update projected average annual economic growth of 4.4 per cent between 2026 and 2028, identifying services and agriculture among the contributors to economic activity.

On inflation, Fitch projected an average rate of 15.4 per cent in 2026, less than half the level recorded in 2024.

The NBS reported that Nigeria’s headline inflation rate eased marginally to 15.39 per cent in August 2026, from 15.43 per cent in July.

The figures provide recent context for Fitch’s assessment of inflation, although the agency’s annual average forecast is different from the monthly inflation rate reported by the NBS.

Reserves, oil production and public debt

Fitch also noted developments in Nigeria’s oil sector, including crude oil production meeting the country’s OPEC target of 1.5 million barrels per day from May 2026.

Mr Oyedele said increased domestic refining was helping to reduce fuel imports and foreign exchange demand.

On public finances, Fitch expects Nigeria’s tax reforms to increase non-oil revenue relative to the size of the economy.

The agency projected that general government debt would average 32 per cent of GDP between 2026 and 2028, below the median of 56 per cent for countries with a ‘B’ rating.

Fitch also highlighted Nigeria’s domestic debt market and the banking sector recapitalisation exercise, noting that many banks had capital adequacy ratios above 20 per cent.

However, the agency identified persistent challenges, including inflation remaining above levels in peer countries, government revenue being low relative to the size of the economy, and interest payments accounting for a high proportion of government revenue.

The minister said the federal government would continue implementing reforms aimed at increasing revenue, improving spending efficiency, strengthening debt management and supporting non-oil economic growth.

Other rating developments

The Fitch decision follows other developments in Nigeria’s international credit assessments.

In May 2026, S&P Global Ratings upgraded Nigeria’s credit rating from ‘B-’ to ‘B’. In August, Moody’s revised its outlook on Nigeria to Positive while retaining its ‘B3’ rating.

Mr Oyedele noted that the government’s medium-term objective remained to improve Nigeria’s credit standing and work towards investment-grade status.

He said the administration would continue to focus on foreign exchange market reforms, tax revenue mobilisation, fiscal governance, more efficient public spending and growth in non-oil sectors.

The minister said its broader objective was to “translate economic reforms into jobs, food security, support for small businesses and improved living standards”.

World.title: SEC warns Nigerians against investing with unregistered WayvePay
World.content:
The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has warned Nigerians against investing through WayvePay, an online investment platform it said was not registered to solicit investments from the public or operate in any capacity in the Nigerian capital market.

The commission issued the warning in a statement, titled “Suspected Fraudulent Activities of WayvePay”, on Friday.

According to SEC, WayvePay operates through a website and various social media platforms, as well as a mobile application.

“The Commission hereby informs the public that WAYVEPAY is not registered by the Commission to solicit investments from the public or operate in any capacity within the Nigerian capital market,” the commission stated.

The regulator advised members of the public to refrain from investing through the platform or any of its representatives in matters relating to the Nigerian capital market, warning that anyone who engages with the entity does so at their own risk.

It added that dealing with unregistered and unregulated entities exposes investors to the risk of fraud and potential loss of their investments.

The commission urged Nigerians to verify the registration status of companies and entities offering investment opportunities through its official registration portals before committing funds.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The warning comes amid the activities of unregistered investment companies in Nigeria, which expose the public to the risk of fraud and potential financial losses.

On 21 August, the commission, in a notice, warned against Gvest Global and three associated entities over what it described as the promotion of unregistered investment schemes.

SEC said Gvest Global also operated under the names Gvest (Alausa) Cooperative Multipurpose Limited, Gvest Investment Limited and Gtext Holdings.

According to the commission, neither Gvest Global nor the three associated entities was registered to solicit investments from the public or operate in the Nigerian capital market.

The regulator said its investigations found that Gvest Global was actively promoted on social media platforms and online forums, while its operations exhibited “typical indicators and characteristics commonly associated with Ponzi schemes”.

It equally advised the public against engaging with Gvest Global, the associated entities or their representatives in connection with business in the Nigerian capital market.

World.title: 2027: Fintiri’s exit, Atiku, Ribadu’s interests set stage for tight Adamawa governorship race
World.content:
The 2027 gubernatorial election in Adamawa State is shaping up to be one of the most intriguing in the state’s history.

The impending exit of Governor Ahmadu Fintiri, whose second term ends next May, and the conflicting interests of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and the National Security Adviser (NSA) Nuhu Ribadu, as well as other local factors, have created a dynamic in which no party holds a visible advantage as campaign activities get underway.

In the 2023 general elections, Mr Fintiri and Atiku combined their forces under the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) to beat the All Progressives Congress (APC).

The political landscape has since shifted dramatically. Not only have those two allies parted ways, but other major realignments have also occurred across the state.

The political picture is such that six candidates now believe they can win the governorship election.

The power dynamics

Governor Fintiri defected to the APC in February. Combining his force with that of Mr Ribadu has strengthened the federal ruling party in the state it lost in 2019, when Mr Fintiri defeated the incumbent Jibrilla Bindow with a margin of over 40,000 votes in the governorship election.

Meanwhile, Atiku’s local and national clout means he remains a formidable force in his home state. Also, his presidential ambition offers a strong rallying cry that will benefit the African Democratic Congress (ADC) candidate.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

However, past elections demonstrate that Adamawa voters don’t always listen to godfathers in state-level politics. Consequently, having Mr Fintiri, Atiku, or Mr Ribadu behind a candidate may not guarantee victory in the 2027 governorship race.

Volatile politics

Adamawa State has a long history of political volatility, largely driven by its multi-ethnic composition. This was visible well before the creation of the current state structure.

During the transition to the Second Republic, under the former Gongola State, which comprised present-day Adamawa and Taraba states, the five registered political parties, NPN, GNPP, PRP, NPP, and UPN, fiercely contested the 1979 gubernatorial election.

Abubakar Barde of the GNPP won the election to become the state’s first executive governor. However, Bamanga Tukur of the NPN defeated him in the 1983 election, before Mr Tukur’s tenure was cut short by the 1983 military coup.

The political volatility was again on full display under the Ibrahim Babangida regime’s transition programme to the aborted Third Republic.

In the Social Democratic Party (SDP) gubernatorial primaries, the contest between Atiku and the late Bala Takaya was so fierce that the military junta cancelled it and disqualified the two men from the repeat exercise.

The SDP eventually nominated Boss Mustapha, but internal party divisions in the SDP helped the late Saleh Michika of the rival National Republican Convention (NRC) to win the 1991 governorship election.

Split-ticket voting is also a recurring theme in the state.

In 1979, while the NPN won the presidential election, in Gongola State, the GNPP secured the governorship. Similarly, in 1993, Moshood Abiola of the SDP won the presidential election in the state, when Adamawa was governed by Mr Michika of the NRC.

In the Fourth Republic, Boni Haruna completed two successive terms (1999–2007) after Atiku, who headed their winning ticket, was selected as vice-presidential candidate by Olusegun Obasanjo.

However, the 2007 election triggered another round of intense political rivalry. Murtala Nyako of the PDP was declared the winner, but the Election Petition Appeal Tribunal voided his election in February 2008 over the exclusion of some opposition candidates.

Mr Nyako won the subsequent re-run in April 2008, but his second term was plagued by instability, ultimately leading to his impeachment in July 2014.

Following Mr Nyako’s removal, the then Speaker of the State House of Assembly, Mr Fintiri, assumed office as acting governor. But his own interim tenure was also cut short when the Federal High Court ruled that Deputy Governor Bala Ngilari’s earlier resignation was invalid, paving the way for Mr Ngilari to serve out the remainder of Mr Nyako’s tenure.

In 2015, Mr Bindow won the governorship poll under the APC. He served only one term, as he was defeated in 2019 by Mr Fintiri of the PDP, who went on to secure a second term.

The candidates and the crises

Backed by federal power, ruling-party resources, and the newly absorbed state executive machinery following Mr Fintiri’s defection, analysts see the APC governorship candidate, Tijjani Galadima, as the frontrunner.

A scion of the aristocratic Galadima of Adamawa family, the APC candidate is an experienced technocrat and public administrator.

He studied Agriculture at Ahmadu Bello University (ABU), Zaria, and holds a master’s degree in Banking and Finance from the University of Ibadan.

He previously served as the Executive Secretary and CEO of the Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF), where he directed major human capital development projects and tertiary scholarship programmes.

Mr Galadima is campaigning on the “Adamawa Rising Agenda.” His campaign focuses on sustaining the infrastructure initiatives of the Fintiri administration, enhancing public-sector transparency, leveraging solid minerals, campaigning for local agriculture to enter industrial value chains, and advancing human capital.

His campaign also promises to consolidate urban-rural road network development, double crop yields through agro-industrialisation, enhance universal healthcare access, provide solar-powered clean energy, and maintain free secondary education.

However, his candidature faces significant challenges.

A prominent rival, Abdulrahman Haske, defected from the APC after disputing the outcome of the primary. He is now the candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM).

Mr Haske is an influential businessman. Educated at the American University of Nigeria (AUN) and Manchester Business School, he serves as the Group Managing Director of AA&R Investment Group.

His conglomerate holds major interests in oil exploration (via Etihad Oilfield Services and Mars E&P), large-scale agriculture (H&W Rice Mill), ICT, and logistics. He also holds the traditional title of ‘Ciroman Ganye’ in the state.

Three State House of Assembly members representing the Yola South, Nasarawo Binyeri, and Numan constituencies joined his defection train and also got APM tickets for reelection.

Mr Haske’s platform leverages strong youth appeal, extensive corporate exposure, and private-sector solutions.

His core profile focuses on industrialising Adamawa’s agricultural sector and instilling corporate efficiency into public administration.

The emergence of Mr Haske as the APM flagbearer and his selection of Safriel Glah, a retired general manager at NNPC Limited, as running mate make the party a serious platform.

The ADC

The ADC candidate, Hamman Modibbo, is a public finance administrator and pioneer director and chief executive officer of the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU).

He holds a Master of Science degree in International Business from the University of Salford, Manchester, and a Bachelor of Arts degree (B.A. Hons) in History from the University of Maiduguri.

As the first head of the NFIU as an independent body, Mr Modibbo led a transition team that transformed the small unit into an agency with the important responsibility of receiving, analysing and sharing financial intelligence with relevant agencies within and outside the country.

Mr Modibbo bases his campaign on transparency, financial discipline, institutional reforms, and community and border security.

However, his candidacy is also embroiled in an intra-party dispute. Umar Suleiman, former managing director of the Nigerian Ports Authority and former diplomat, had won the ADC primary election in May, defeating Mr Modibbo.

Mr Suleiman insists he remains the authentic candidate and has secured court injunctions against the party substituting him.

Despite these legal barriers, ADC national leaders, alongside presidential candidate Atiku, endorsed Mr Modibbo in August, sparking a full-blown factional conflict over the ticket.

Consequently, while Mr Suleiman is actively contesting his substitution in court, the party’s national leadership continues to back Mr Modibbo.

Adding to the rift, Muhammad Shuwa is the candidate backed by the Nafiu Bala faction of the ADC, bringing to three the candidates claiming the ADC ticket in the state.

The NDC, LP and PDP

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, Aishatu Ahmed, popularly known as Binani, is a formidable politician in Adamawa.

Mrs Ahmed, a former senator, is popular for her grassroots network and micro-empowerment projects. She promotes grassroots social welfare, healthcare access, and economic inclusion for women and micro-entrepreneurs across the state.

A civil engineer by training and former Member of the House of Representatives (Yola North/Yola South/Girei), the woman known across the state as Binani represented the Adamawa Central District in the Senate from 2019–2023.

She was the APC governorship candidate in 2023 and came under the spotlight when she was controversially declared the winner by a rogue electoral official.

Opponents also accused her of electoral fraud in the NDC party primary.

Another candidate, Ishaku Abbo, represented the Adamawa North District in the Senate in 2019-2023, and returned to the seat in 2023 until his election was voided by the courts. An outspoken political figure, Mr Abbo has a strong youth following across Northern Adamawa.

Flying the Labour Party (LP) banner, Mr Abbo brings a populist approach to the campaign trail.

His political strategy focuses on engaging young voters, championing social justice reform, developing rural infrastructure, and driving grassroots mobilisation across the northern senatorial zone.

Maurice Vunobolki, the candidate of the Nyesom Wike-backed Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), is a chartered accountant, financial management expert, and international development consultant.

He previously worked with foreign-assisted development projects, public procurement frameworks, and local government infrastructure initiatives in Northern Nigeria.

However, Mr Vunobolki faces an internal challenge from Caleb Myebangara of the Tanimu Turaki-led PDP faction.

Mr Myebangara, a professional banker, has fully resumed his campaign while awaiting the outcome of the Tanimu Turaki-led PDP case before the Court of Appeal in Abuja.

How the election will be fought and won – Analysts

Mahdi Abba, head of the Department of Political Science at Modibbo Adama University, Yola, noted that the major political parties each have distinct competitive advantages, setting the stage for a closely fought race.

According to Mr Abba, the APC candidate benefits from the formidable power of incumbency, backed by both state and federal government machinery and supported by a robust party structure and dedicated loyalists. He said Mr Galadima remains a strong contender for victory.

He also acknowledged that the ADC candidate, Mr Modibbo, is positioned to capitalise on the substantial political clout of the former vice president.

“Historical voting trends in the state demonstrate a strong correlation between Atiku’s party affiliation and gubernatorial success—evidenced by APC’s victory in 2015 when he was a member, followed by PDP’s victories in 2019 and 2023 after his return to the party. With Atiku now backing the ADC, the party is set to make a significant impact”, Mr Abba said.

On Mrs Ahmed, Mr Abba said the NDC candidate is a seasoned politician with a deeply rooted grassroots network, bringing strong electoral momentum to the party in Adamawa State.

“Her track record of successful campaigns for the House of Representatives and the Senate—particularly her solid base in metropolitan Adamawa—underscores her strong appeal among the electorate”, the political scientist said.

The PDP stands to gain a strategic advantage if ethno-religious dynamics shape the election.

According to Mr Abba, because the APC, NDC, ADC, and APM candidates are all Muslim Fulanis, a split in their shared voter base may work to the PDP candidate’s advantage

“Also, the Labour Party candidate commands significant regional popularity, particularly within his home zone comprising Mubi North, Mubi South, Maiha, Madagali, and Michika.

Having secured election victories twice from this district, his localised stronghold will play a decisive role if ethno-religious sentiments—a historically common feature in Adamawa State politics—come to the fore”, Mr Abba said.

World.title: Movie Review: Beyond 10 million views, ‘My 30th Wedding’ offers little surprise
World.content:
From ‘Breaded Life (2021)’ to Big Love (2023) and now ‘My 30th Wedding’, Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson have become a familiar on-screen pair, repeatedly drawing audiences into romances built on their easy chemistry.

Their latest outing, however, offers more of what fans already know than anything particularly new.

In ‘My 30th Wedding’, Ademoye plays a successful wedding planner racing against her 30th birthday to find a husband. In contrast, Egbuson plays a wealthy widower whose complicated family life threatens to derail their budding romance.

Written and produced by Ademoye, the 2026 romantic comedy capitalises on the actors’ established appeal, combining romance, family drama and comic moments in a polished but predictable Nollywood package.

Released on Bimbo Ademoye TV on 1 October, the film crossed 10 million YouTube views in roughly 48 hours, underscoring strong audience interest in the Ademoye-Egbuson pairing.

But while their chemistry remains one of the film’s strongest attractions, ‘My 30th Wedding’ ultimately settles for a familiar love story, relying on manufactured misunderstandings and an overly tidy resolution rather than taking its romance in a more unexpected direction.

However, the film’s publicity campaign had already generated considerable curiosity before its release, particularly through a series of carefully staged “pre-wedding” photographs featuring Ademoye and Egbuson. The images briefly led fans to speculate that the two actors had married in real life.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

That publicity stunt captured the central strength of My 30th Wedding: it understands its stars’ appeal and knows exactly what its audience wants from them. Yet, beyond the impressive numbers and attractive packaging, the film is a largely conventional romantic comedy, but unwilling to take many risks.

Plot

Ademoye plays Elamosi Ogbeta, a successful wedding planner who runs Xtra Brides and More.

After planning 25 weddings for other people, Elamosi has privately set herself a deadline: she must get married by her 30th birthday. Her determination is fuelled partly by her mother’s persistent matchmaking and the social pressure surrounding her unmarried status.

Among the men in her orbit is Osaze (Bryan Okoye), the son of a family friend. Unlike the complications that later define her relationship with Lekan, Osaze offers Elamosi something simpler: straightforward affection and an uncomplicated willingness to love her.

But her life takes a different turn when Lekan Wellington (Egbuson), a wealthy technology entrepreneur and widower, hires her to organise a memorial gala for his late wife. The relationship begins with professional friction before gradually developing into attraction.

Lekan, however, comes with baggage. He is a father, and his daughter Grace is protective of him and suspicious of Elamosi’s place in their lives.

The developing romance is further complicated by class differences, family expectations, misunderstandings, and a manufactured betrayal that eventually threatens to destroy the relationship. How long will this love relationship last?

Review

The film’s strongest element is undoubtedly the chemistry between Ademoye and Egbuson. Their performances give the romance much of its credibility. Their exchanges are playful without becoming excessively theatrical, while their quieter moments communicate attraction more effectively than some of the film’s dialogue.

Ademoye, in particular, gives Elamosi enough vulnerability to prevent her from becoming merely another ambitious, unmarried Nollywood heroine racing against a biological or social clock.

Egbuson also plays Lekan with restraint. His character is wealthy and accomplished, but the film does not make him completely invulnerable. His relationship with his daughter adds an emotional complication that goes beyond the conventional rich-man-meets-working-woman setup.

Gloria Anozie-Young, as Elamosi’s anxious and matchmaking mother, understands the comic possibilities of a parent who believes marriage is the ultimate solution to her daughter’s problems.

Elamosi is successful professionally, financially independent, and capable of running her own business. Yet those achievements do little to protect her from the constant question: ‘When are you getting married?’

The film captures the peculiar pressure unmarried women face when their professional accomplishments are still treated as secondary to their relationship status. It also explores another difficult question: what happens when love comes with responsibilities that already existed before the relationship?

For Elamosi, falling in love with him therefore means entering an existing family structure. The film’s recurring idea that “love marries a person and the people they love” is arguably its most interesting observation.

Unfortunately, the film does not explore that idea deeply enough. My 30th Wedding’s biggest weakness is its reliance on manufactured conflict.

The central breakdown in Elamosi and Lekan’s relationship is driven largely by a conspiracy involving the household staff. It is an old-fashioned romantic-comedy device that feels increasingly artificial as the film progresses.

More troubling is how quickly Lekan accepts the version of events presented to him.

For a man who has gradually developed feelings for Elamosi, his readiness to believe the worst of her weakens the emotional foundation of their relationship.

Once the deception is exposed, the consequences are also surprisingly limited.

The film moves quickly to forgiveness and reconciliation, leaving little room to examine the damage mistrust causes.

Osaze’s character presents another missed opportunity. Because he offers Elamosi a genuinely uncomplicated alternative, the story could have had greater emotional tension with a real romantic triangle. Instead, he largely functions as a convenient contrast to Lekan rather than a serious competitor for Elamosi’s heart.

The result is that the eventual romantic choice feels predictable long before the film reaches its conclusion.

The final stretch is perhaps the film’s most debatable section. Some viewers may find the resolution satisfying because it delivers precisely what a romantic comedy promises: reconciliation, emotional closure and a happy ending. Others may question whether the problems raised by the film have been resolved too neatly.

Stylistically, My 30th Wedding does not attempt to reinvent the Nigerian romantic comedy. Instead, it improves on a familiar formula. It has the wealthy man, the independent woman, family pressure, misunderstandings, social expectations, comic relief, emotional confrontation, and eventual reconciliation.

What distinguishes it is Ademoye’s performance, Egbuson’s screen presence, and their chemistry. But that same familiarity ultimately limits it.

Verdict: 7/10

World.title: 2027: Adebutu pledges LG autonomy, border community dev’t in Ogun
World.content:
Adebutu

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ogun State, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has reiterated his commitment to prioritise local government autonomy, grassroots development and strategic investment in border communities if elected in the 2027 governorship election.

Adebutu made the pledge during a PDP campaign rally in Remo, Ogun State, where he outlined key elements of his ‘Itura De’ agenda, which he said was designed to return power to the people and strengthen development at the grassroots.

The PDP candidate said local governments should be empowered to address the specific needs of their communities and determine development priorities without undue interference.

According to him, functional local government autonomy would enable grassroots administrations to respond more effectively to the concerns of residents and deliver projects that directly improve their living conditions.

He said: “Local governments must be empowered to address the needs of their people and determine the development priorities of their communities. Governance should be felt at the grassroots, where its impact matters most to ordinary citizens.”

Adebutu also highlighted the importance of developing border communities, arguing that targeted investments in infrastructure and economic activities could unlock their potential and strengthen their contribution to Ogun State’s economy.

He noted that Ogun’s proximity to Lagos presented significant opportunities for economic integration, trade and investment, adding that the state could benefit from stronger economic connections with its neighbouring commercial hub.

According to him, improved infrastructure and deliberate economic planning would help border communities attract investment, create employment opportunities and contribute more meaningfully to the state’s overall development.

Also speaking at the rally, the PDP’s Ogun East senatorial candidate, Alhaji Abdul-Hameed Femi Omotayo, called for visible and measurable development across the senatorial district.

Referring to his visit to Sagamu two days earlier, Omotayo said his observations during the visit had raised concerns about the town’s development trajectory.

He criticised what he described as inadequate progress, using a metaphor to contrast urban development with the condition he said he encountered in the town.

“The current administration has turned town to bush instead of turning bush to town,” he said.

Omotayo’s remark underscored his concerns about the pace of development in Sagamu and the need for projects that residents can see and feel in their daily lives.

He maintained that Ogun East needed tangible results in infrastructure, employment generation and the creation of opportunities for residents, particularly young people.

The senatorial candidate also stressed the importance of addressing challenges affecting economic activities across communities in the district.

Poor road infrastructure, limited employment opportunities and inadequate access to economic opportunities remain important issues in discussions about community development. Deteriorating roads can increase transportation costs and impede the movement of goods, while a shortage of jobs can restrict the options available to young people.

World.title: Gordon nets first Barca goal as Liga leaders beat Getafe
World.content:
Barcelona’s English forward #17 Anthony Gordon (R) is challenged by Getafe’s Colombian defender #22 Johan Mojica during the Spanish league football match between FC Barcelona and Getafe CF at Camp Nou Stadium in Barcelona on October 10, 2026. (Photo by Lluis GENE / AFP)

Anthony Gordon scored his first goal for Barcelona as the Spanish champions extended their perfect start in La Liga with a 3-0 win over Getafe on Saturday.

England international Gordon opened the scoring in the second minute and Gabriel Jesus added another after half an hour for the league leaders, who have won every match they have played this season.

French defender Jules Kounde tucked home the third from Lamine Yamal’s cross to cap Barca’s solid win against Jose Bordalas’s side at Camp Nou.

Barca moved five points clear of second-placed Atletico Madrid, who won 2-1 at Alaves earlier, and lead Real Madrid, fourth, by nine points before Los Blancos host Villarreal later on.

Barca were without their top scorer Raphinha, who sustained a hamstring problem during the international break with Brazil.

Flick replaced him with former Arsenal striker and Selecao compatriot Jesus and his side came roaring out of the blocks.

Gordon, who has impressed since joining this summer, grabbed his first Barca goal with a low deflected effort after bundling his way past three players.

The winger was Barca’s brightest spark in the first half, continuing his fine goalscoring form for England in the recent Nations League matches.

Barca defender Eric Garcia forced a save from Getafe goalkeeper David Soria with a drive from distance as Flick’s side controlled the game.

Getafe defender Zaid Romero gave the ball away in his own box for Barca’s second, passing it straight to Jesus, who stroked into the bottom corner.

Soria denied Olmo before Yamal teed up Kounde for the third.

The defender, making a record 194th appearance for Barca for a French player, overtaking Eric Abidal, was on hand to turn home from close range from teenage star Yamal’s cross.

Barca, who also won their Champions League opener, have nine victories from nine matches across all competitions.

World.title: Trump to decide ‘very quickly’ if to join Saudi strikes against Houthis
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump. Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP.



US President Donald Trump said Saturday he would soon decide whether to join Saudi strikes against Iran-backed Houthins after an attack on Riyadh’s international airport.

“We may. We’re going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack, so we’ll make a decision,” Trump told reporters at the White House. “We move very quickly.”

World.title: Okpebholo, Wike, Oshiomhole, others honour Orbih at funeral
World.content:
By Ozioruva Aliu

THE governor of Edo State, Senator Monday Okpebholo, Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, and Senator Adams Oshiomhole were among the prominent politicians present when the remains of former Vice Chairman South -South of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Daniel Orbih, were on Saturday laid to rest in his home town, Ogbona, Etsako Central Local Government Area.

Speaking at the funeral service held at St. John the Baptist Catholic Church, Ogbona, Governor Okpebholo tasked Nigerians, particularly those in positions of authority, to live selfless and sacrificial lives and use their positions to make society a better place for all.

The governor, in an emotional voice, said the death of Orbih had reminded him of the uncertainty of life and the need for people to make meaningful contributions to society while they are alive.

He recalled that his first visit to the church was to celebrate Orbih’s birthday and expressed sadness that he had returned to the same venue to attend his funeral.

“This is my second time coming to this Church. The first time I came here was to come celebrate with Chief Dan Osi Orbih. I said to him, we will be coming here like this in the next eight years to celebrate your birthday but today we are here for a different purpose.

“Today, it has dawned on me that there is nothing in life; here lies in the casket the remains of Chief Dan Osi Orbih and he can’t stand up or walk anymore,” he said.

Wike, in his remarks, said the funeral activities had reinforced the reality of death and the pain of losing a close friend.

“When I saw the casket, it dawned on me that truly my friend and brother is gone. There is nothing we can do but to pray to God to give the family the fortitude to bear this great loss,” he said.

In his homily, the Catholic Bishop of Auchi Diocese, Most Rev. Dr. Gabriel Dunia, urged the congregation and Nigerians to reflect on the transient nature of life and the inevitability of death.

Dunia said titles, academic qualifications, positions, social status and personal achievements could not prevent death when the time came.

He called on the faithful to follow the path of truth and light, stressing the importance of living meaningful lives and remaining conscious of their responsibilities to God and humanity.

“Death is what all must pay and one can tell God to hold on because we are busy at the moment but be prepared to answer the call at any time,” he said.

World.title: Ukraine needs new president who will agree to end war, says Trump
World.content:
US President Donald Trump speaks during a meeting with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, DC, on July 21, 2026. (Photo by SAUL LOEB / AFP)





US President Donald Trump on Saturday urged Ukraine to replace Volodomyr Zelensky with a new leader, lashing out at him for strikes on Russian oil refineries that have contributed to pre-election high diesel prices.

Trump told reporters at the White House that he had told Zelensky to “do what you want” against Russia, but “don’t hit refineries.”

“He better damn well stop,” Trump said, before adding that he thinks “it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president” who will agree to end the war.

World.title: 2027: Yari’s camp denies backing ADC candidate in Zamfara
World.content:
Yari

By Luminous Jannamike

The camp of former Zamfara State Governor, Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, has denied allegations that he is sponsoring the African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate, Bilyaminu Yusuf Shinkafi, accusing political rivals of trying to tarnish his reputation ahead of the 2027 elections.

In a statement on Saturday, Sani Abdullahi Shinkafi, a former APGA national secretary and Zamfara North senatorial aspirant, said the allegation was part of a campaign to undermine Yari following his appointment as Director-General of President Bola Tinubu’s Presidential Campaign Council.

“It is mischievous, false, handwork of mischief makers and political adversaries of the former governor,” he said.

Shinkafi explained that Bilyaminu was a cousin of Yari’s wife, arguing that their family connection did not establish political sponsorship. He added that the ADC candidate had previously sought the APC ticket for Zamfara North senatorial district but was not cleared by the party’s screening committee before defecting to the ADC.

The statement also rejected claims linking Yari to eight suspended members of the Zamfara State House of Assembly who recently resigned from the APC.

“It has become necessary to state categorically that the eight suspended members of the Zamfara State House of Assembly are not political allies of Senator Abdul’aziz Abubakar Yari,” Shinkafi said.

The lawmakers were suspended on February 26, 2024, over allegations including gross misconduct, contempt of the House and holding an unauthorised sitting. The Assembly also accused them of forceful entry into legislative offices and destruction of public property.

Shinkafi said five of the eight lawmakers were elected on the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) platform in 2023, while three won their seats on the APC platform.

The dispute continued after Governor Dauda Lawal defected from the PDP to the APC in March 2026. The suspended lawmakers had petitioned the House of Representatives Committee on Public Petitions over their prolonged suspension and the withholding of their salaries and allowances.

According to Shinkafi, Yari provided financial assistance to the affected lawmakers and continued efforts to broker peace, despite the failure to resolve the dispute.

“Those who blame Senator Abdul’aziz Yari for not intervening in the protracted Zamfara State House of Assembly issue did so out of ignorance and mischief,” he said.

Shinkafi urged Nigerians to disregard the allegations, insisting that Yari remained committed to Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.

World.title: Fitch upgrades Nigeria’s outlook to positive, affirms ‘B’ rating
World.content:
The Federal Government says Fitch Ratings’ revision of Nigeria’s economic outlook to positive reflects sustained reforms, stronger external reserves and moderating inflation.

Fitch, on Friday, revised Nigeria’s Long-Term Issuer Default Ratings outlook to positive from stable, while affirming the country’s rating at ‘B’.

The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, disclosed this in a statement in Abuja on Saturday.

He said that the positive outlook indicated the possibility of a rating upgrade if current economic trends and reform momentum were sustained.

Oyedele said that Fitch attributed the improved outlook to greater naira flexibility, disinflation and faster-than-expected accumulation of foreign exchange reserves.

The minister said that Nigeria’s gross foreign reserves rose to 54.9 billion dollars on Sept. 25, from 32 billion dollars in mid-April 2024.

He said that the increase was supported by stronger portfolio inflows, higher export receipts and remittances, alongside increased formalisation of foreign exchange transactions.

Oyedele said that the improved reserve quality had strengthened Nigeria’s capacity to withstand external shocks, projecting a current account surplus of 6.4 per cent of GDP in 2026.

He said that Fitch also forecast Nigeria’s real GDP growth at 4.3 per cent in 2026, up from four per cent in 2025.

It projected economic growth to remain above four per cent in 2027 and 2028, driven largely by non-oil activities.

The minister said that crude oil production had met Nigeria’s OPEC target of 1.5 million barrels per day since May.

Oyedele said that increased domestic refining was reducing refined petroleum product imports and demand for foreign exchange.

Average inflation was projected to moderate to 15.4 per cent in 2026, less than half its 2024 level.

The minister said that on public finances, Fitch expects tax reforms to increase non-oil revenue relative to GDP, while government debt is projected to average 32 per cent of GDP between 2026 and 2028.

The projected debt ratio is significantly below the 56 per cent median for countries rated ‘B’.

The minister said Fitch also recognised Nigeria’s liquid domestic debt market and bank recapitalisation exercise, noting that many banks had capital adequacy ratios exceeding 20 per cent.

Oyedele said that the three major international rating agencies had taken positive rating actions on Nigeria in 2026.

He recalled that S&P Global Ratings upgraded Nigeria’s rating to ‘B’ from ‘B-’ in May, while Moody’s Ratings revised its outlook to positive in August.

Separately, FTSE Russell returned Nigeria to Frontier Market status, effective Sept. 21, 2026.

According to the minister, the decisions reflect growing confidence in the country’s economic reform trajectory.

Oyedele said that the positive outlook validated reforms implemented under President Bola Tinubu, including fuel subsidy removal, exchange rate unification and tax reforms.

He said that its medium-term ambition was to place the country firmly on the path to investment-grade status.

It added that the reforms were intended to reduce borrowing costs, attract private investment and create decent jobs.

However, he said that the government acknowledged Fitch’s concerns about persistent inflation, low government revenue relative to economic output and high interest payments.

Oyedele said these challenges remained central to the administration’s reform programme.

He reiterated the government commitment to sustaining reforms and maintaining a transparent, market-reflective foreign exchange regime.

Other priorities include implementing new tax laws, improving spending efficiency, strengthening debt management and promoting non-oil growth.

The minister also pledged to translate macroeconomic stability into shared prosperity through food security, job creation, human development and support for small businesses. (NAN)

World.title: No court issued bench warrant against me – Okorocha
World.content:
By Emmanuel Iheaka

Former governor of Imo State, Senator Rochas Okorocha, has dismissed as false a report claiming that a magistrate court issued a bench warrant against him for alleged forgery.

In a statement endorsed by his Chief Press Secretary/Special Adviser on Media, Sam Onwuemeodo, the erstwhile governor challenged anybody with the said bench warrant to publish the document in 48 hours.

Okorocha noted that the said report claimed that the bench warrant was issued on October 9 following a petition dated October 8 and wondered how an investigation and other processes were concluded within 24 hours.

The former governor urged members of the public to disregard the report, adding that what the All Progressives Congress needs at the moment is peace.

“Against the backdrop of all these, we want to strongly state, and we stand to be contradicted, that no court, whether that of the Senior Magistrate or the High Court, had ordered or issued any bench warrant for the arrest of Okorocha.

“Now that we have openly made this denial, the burden now is on those behind the trending story of the court order for the arrest of Okorocha to unveil the court order or bench warrant. Let them make it public. Under normal scenarios, they should have published the arrest story, with the court order and the name of the senior magistrate in question. Perhaps they had forgotten to do that. Now, we are challenging them to make the court order or bench warrant public. We ask that they do that within 48 hours.

“We had equally observed that, in their story, they claimed that the bench warrant was issued on September 9, 2026, whereas the LMO REC’s petitions, which they claimed, had warranted the court order, were dated October 8, 2026. And the case number is CR/M/084/2026. In other words, the Court Order came before the Petitions and before the filing of the Case. This is what you get when people decide to deceive or to chase shadows.

“We also make hay to say that INEC, or the LMO Resident Electoral Commissioner, Barr. Ibejiako, never wrote any petition against Okorocha or asked that Okorocha be investigated. Nor did he indict Okorocha in his petitions. Rather, in his petitions, he asked the police and DSS to investigate a document in circulation that had portrayed Okorocha as the winner of the APC Primary in LMO for the LMO West Senatorial District. And the petition was dated Thursday, October 8, 2026. Assuming it was submitted the same day, was it possible for both the DSS and police to have concluded their investigations on Friday, October 9, 2026, when the story of the court order for arrest began to trend? The answer is “No,” the statement read.

World.title: CAS Visits Home Unit of Ill-Fated ATR, Reaffirms Support for Personnel, Families
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, has visited 107 Air Maritime Group (AMG), Nigerian Air Force (NAF) Base, Benin City, the home unit of the ill-fated NAF ATR 42 aircraft, where he met with personnel and reassured the families of those affected by the recent accident of the Service’s continued support during this difficult period.

Addressing personnel of the unit, Aneke expressed profound condolences over the loss of their colleagues, describing the deceased as dedicated patriots who served the nation with honour and commitment.

“Our thoughts and prayers remain with the families of our fallen colleagues,” he said.

According to a statement by the Director of Public Relations and Information, Nigerian Air Force, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, the CAS stressed that the personnel had made the ultimate sacrifice in the service of the nation and that the nation would not forget them or their contributions to the Nigerian Air Force.

He further assured the bereaved families that the NAF would continue to stand by them, providing the necessary emotional, administrative and institutional support.

Reaffirming the Service’s commitment to their welfare, Air Marshal Aneke also acknowledged the provision of scholarship awards for the children of the deceased personnel, noting that their well-being remained a priority.

“We will continue to do everything within our capacity to support the families and ensure that the children of our fallen comrades are not left without support. Their welfare is our responsibility, and we will remain committed to it,” he stated.

On efforts to restore and strengthen 107 AMG, the CAS assured personnel that the Service would take the necessary measures to improve their welfare, sustain training and facilitate the availability of operational platforms.

“We will support this unit to quickly regain its strength. That support will include welfare, training and the availability of the platforms required for you to continue performing your duties effectively. We expect you to remain focused, professional and resilient,” he said.

In his response, the Commander of 107 AMG, Air Commodore Onu, expressed appreciation to the CAS for visiting the unit at such a difficult time and for reassuring personnel and the families of the deceased of the Service’s continued support.

“Sir, your presence here has strengthened the morale of our personnel. We appreciate your leadership, concern and commitment to the welfare of our people. We remain resolute and committed to our responsibilities, despite the challenges we are currently facing,” he said.

Onu further assured the CAS that personnel of the unit would remain dedicated to their duties and continue to uphold the traditions and professional standards of the NAF.

The CAS also commended the personnel of 107 AMG for their professionalism, resilience and unwavering dedication in the face of adversity, urging them to remain steadfast as search, recovery and investigative efforts continued.

He expressed appreciation to the Nigerian Navy and other security agencies for their invaluable support in the search and recovery operations, noting that the collaboration underscored the importance of jointness and inter-Service cooperation in responding to national challenges.

Reaffirming the NAF’s commitment to its personnel and their families, Aneke assured all those affected that the Service would continue to provide the necessary support while pursuing a thorough and professional investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident.

World.title: Shettima: Nigeria’ll Deepen Nutrition 774 With Lessons From Ethiopia
World.content:
.Back in Abuja after three-day Nigeria–Ethiopia nutrition leadership exchange



Deji Elumoye in Abuja

Vice President Kashim Shettima has said Nigeria will deepen the implementation of the Nutrition 774 Initiative with practical lessons from Ethiopia’s experience in tackling malnutrition, strengthening food systems and coordinating nutrition interventions across different levels of government.

The Vice President said the knowledge gained from the three-day Nigeria–Ethiopia Nutrition Leadership Exchange would be adapted to Nigeria’s realities, particularly in strengthening collaboration among the federal government, states and local governments to improve nutrition outcomes at the community and household levels.

Shettima spoke as he returned to Abuja yesterday after leading Nigeria’s delegation to the leadership exchange in Addis Ababa and Oromia, Ethiopia, themed ‘Moving the Needle on Nutrition’.

During the visit, the Vice President according to a statement issued by his Media Assistant, Stanley Nkwocha, held a bilateral meeting with Ethiopia’s Deputy Prime Minister, Temesgen Tiruneh, where both leaders reviewed bilateral relations and explored opportunities for deeper cooperation in agriculture, trade, investment, food security, aviation and other areas of mutual interest.

At the opening session of the exchange, Shettima emphasised the value of African countries learning from one another, noting that Ethiopia’s Seqota Declaration and Nigeria’s Nutrition 774 Initiative provide useful platforms for sharing home-grown approaches to addressing malnutrition.

He also highlighted Nigeria’s efforts to strengthen nutrition financing, accountability and subnational implementation, stressing that improved nutrition is critical to human capital development, productivity and economic growth.

On the second day of the programme, the Vice President led governors, ministers and other stakeholders on field engagements across Oromia focused on agriculture value-chain transformation.

The delegation visited wheat, banana and papaya farms, the “Bounty of the Basket” Training Centre and households in Mojo, as well as other facilities, to study how agricultural production, food systems and value-chain development are being linked to improved nutrition and livelihoods.

Shettima also visited the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute, where the delegation received briefings on the application of technology, data and innovation to development and public-sector delivery.

The final day of the exchange focused on early childhood development, with engagements covering pre-primary education, healthcare, daycare and parental coaching, followed by a working session on translating lessons from Ethiopia into concrete commitments for the Nutrition 774 Initiative.

The programme culminated in a Nigeria Country Session and a joint closing ceremony attended by Shettima and Deputy Prime Minister Tiruneh, during which both countries reaffirmed their commitment to sustained cooperation and knowledge exchange on nutrition and development.

Shettima said the real measure of the exchange would be how effectively the lessons are translated into improved outcomes for Nigerian families, particularly women and children, through stronger implementation of Nutrition 774 across the country.

World.title: Abia Engages Community Leaders On Accommodation For New Teachers, Offers N30,000 Incentive
World.content:
Boniface Okoro in Umuahia

Abia State Government says it is engaging traditional rulers, Presidents-General and other community leaders to provide accommodation for the newly recruited 4,075 teachers posted to rural and hard-to-reach areas, while also offering a N30,000 incentive to those who accept the postings.

The Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education, Elder Goodluck Ubochi, disclosed this in Umuahia during a press briefing to sensitise the Cohort 2 teachers who have just received their letters of engagement and posting, against the backdrop of complaints by the new recruits.

Ubochi said the second batch of recruitment became necessary after the deployment of the first batch of 5,394 teachers, as vacancies still exist in remote schools, which is the essence of the second engagement.

He said the teachers were informed from the outset and even signed a commitment that they would be deployed to where their services are needed, and therefore should not expect postings to places of comfort.

The commissioner acknowledged complaints from some teachers posted to hinterlands, but insisted they must first report to their schools, register their presence with the headteacher or principal, and then report back their challenges.

According to him, government under Governor Alex Otti is passionate about teachers’ welfare and does not want a situation where a teacher spends more than his salary to get to work, hence the interface with communities and School-Based Management Committees (SBMCs) for accommodation.

He appealed to Presidents-General, traditional rulers and Abians in diaspora who own unoccupied buildings in the hinterlands to release even their boys’ quarters to accommodate the teachers.

“We have also opened a help desk in the ministry. When they go to these places, we expect them to come back and report their experiences. Because when a teacher is not comfortable, he will not be able to deliver,” Ubochi said.

On welfare, he disclosed that Governor Otti has approved an additional N30,000 incentive for teachers serving in difficult areas. “There is an additional N30,000 incentive that has been in the cooler waiting to be extended to those who take up this responsibility.
