As soon as they settle down, we’ll take their details and make sure that this incentive is extended to them.”

Ubochi said the ministry expects feedback from headteachers and principals before the end of the week on teachers who have reported, and urged the new teachers to complete their onboarding at ASUBEB and SEMB within this week and next week to be captured in the payroll and receive salary by end of October as directed by the governor on Teachers’ Day.

He also reminded teachers who retired under the old 60 years of age /35 years of service rule and are willing to return under the new 65 years policy to report to the Ministry for documentation and reintegration.

Responding to questions, the commissioner said errors such as posting secondary school subject specialists to primary schools would be corrected, adding that the Ministry’s Quality Assurance units and satellite offices in LGAs will verify complaints and monitor truancy and connivance with school heads.

World.title: Ifowodo Wins $100,000 Nigeria Prize for Poetry on Religious, Political Violence
World.content:
Wale Igbintade

Poet Ogaga Ifowodo has won The Nigeria Prize for Literature 2026, securing the $100,000 cash award for his collection, Why Does God Need a Gun?, which examines religious and political violence in Nigeria.

In a related development, Beyond Tarkwa Bay by Peter Oghenetega Oke and Mara Mania by Feranmi Abiola have emerged as joint winners of the inaugural Nigeria Prize for Creative Arts, which carries a $20,000 cash award.

The winners were announced at the Grand Award Night organised by Nigeria LNG Limited (NLNG) in Lagos on Friday, October 9, 2026.

Ifowodo’s poetry collection was selected from 223 entries, while the two winning documentaries emerged from 98 submissions for the Creative Arts Prize.

Announcing the literature winner, Chairman of the Advisory Board for The Nigeria Prize for Literature, Professor Akachi Adimora-Ezeigbo, described Why Does God Need a Gun? as a sensitive portrayal of religious and political violence in Nigeria, narrated through the voice of an imagined victim.

She commended all three shortlisted poetry collections for their technical skill, confidence and mature use of language, noting that they addressed themes extending beyond Nigeria’s borders.

According to her, the collections explored interconnected issues, including identity and belonging, the promises and disappointments of nationhood, the consequences of extremism and displacement, and the enduring impact of conflict on individuals and communities.

She said that, although distinct in voice and style, the works were rooted in the Nigerian experience while contributing to wider global conversations about humanity.

On the Creative Arts Prize, Technical Adviser to its Advisory Board, Joel Kachi Benson, praised the five shortlisted documentaries for challenging perceptions, fostering human connections and drawing attention to communities and experiences that often remain overlooked.

He said the films brought audiences closer to communities whose stories were rarely told and amplified voices that frequently went unheard.

Benson added that the documentaries celebrated resilience, documented culture, preserved memory and presented perspectives that enriched society’s understanding of itself.

The literature and creative arts awards followed the September 2026 announcement of Mary-Brenda Akoda as the winner of The Nigeria Prize for Science and Innovation.

Akoda’s winning innovation, GenScan AI (GenMRI/C-MORE), is an artificial intelligence-powered solution designed to accelerate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

Her victory marked two milestones: she became the prize’s first Generation Z recipient and the first woman to win as an individual awardee.

Speaking at the ceremony, NLNG Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Adeleye Falade, said the Nigeria Prizes were established to recognise outstanding achievements and promote scientific innovation, literary excellence and creative expression that enrich society and improve lives.

He noted that the science and innovation prize had recognised groundbreaking contributions across critical sectors, including healthcare, agriculture, engineering, energy, technology, climate resilience and sustainable development.

According to him, the prize had celebrated scientists whose work extended beyond laboratories and research papers to deliver practical solutions capable of improving lives.

Falade said this year’s winning innovation, which focuses on artificial intelligence and information technology, had the potential to transform lives in Nigeria and beyond.

On literature, he said The Nigeria Prize for Literature had grown into one of Africa’s most prestigious literary honours, attracting widespread interest and providing a platform for some of the continent’s finest literary voices.

He said Nigerian writers had demonstrated through the prize that their stories were more than accounts of their origins, contributing meaningfully to global conversations about identity, resilience and shared humanity.

Falade described the Nigeria Prize for Creative Arts as a platform for recognising originality, authenticity and creative excellence, particularly among artists who preserve Nigeria’s cultural heritage while reinterpreting it for a new generation.

He said the three prizes had become enduring national institutions, demonstrating what could be achieved when excellence was recognised, rewarded and encouraged.

Congratulating the winners and finalists, Falade said their achievements reflected discipline, dedication and perseverance.

He expressed hope that the awards would inspire a new generation of scientists, writers and creative professionals to develop solutions to future challenges, tell compelling stories and shape the country’s future.

In his remarks, Nobel laureate Professor Wole Soyinka called for closer collaboration between the humanities and the sciences, describing imagination as a vital link between literature, creative arts and scientific inquiry.

He argued that imagination was not confined to the humanities, noting that disciplines such as mathematics and physics also depended on vision and the ability to conceive new possibilities.

Soyinka urged practitioners in both fields to work together to expand the boundaries of imagination and combine their strengths in the service of humanity.

He stressed that human wellbeing should remain central to creative expression and scientific advancement.

NLNG said the Nigeria Prizes reaffirmed its commitment to recognising excellence and encouraging achievements capable of contributing to a sustainable future.

World.title: Dangote Cement  Awards Scholarships, Empowers Farmers, Market Women in Kogi
World.content:
Ibrahim Oyewale in Lokoja

Dangote Cement Plc, Obajana Plant, has strengthened its support for the Jakura community through scholarship awards and empowerment programmes for farmers and market women.

The Plant Director, Obajana Plant, Engr. Azad Nawabuddin, said the scheme was part of the company’s commitment to implementing the provisions of the Community Development Agreement (CDA).

The director who was represented by the Head of Social Performance at the Obajana Plant, Prince Ademola Adeyemi, said the empowerment programme benefited students, farmers and market women.

Nawabuddin said the programme, which focused on students, farmers and market women, underscores DCP’s continued commitment to sustainable community development, poverty reduction and economic empowerment across its host communities.

He said a total of 20 beneficiaries drawn from several tertiary institutions and 60 beneficiaries from secondary schools received educational grants running into several millions of naira.

He disclosed that 20 farmers were provided with essential farming implements and funds, noting that the initiative is designed to enhance agricultural productivity, encourage the adoption of improved farming practices and contribute to greater food security in the community.

Twenty market women were each provided with start-up capital and business support to strengthen their enterprises, promote financial independence and enhance household incomes.

The event attracted several stakeholders, traditional rulers, government representatives, and community leaders including His Royal Highness, Oba Usman Adoga Ajibola, the Obaro of Jakura., Representative of the Olu of Oworo, Chief K.A Mahmood, (The Obalumema of Oworo Land), Engr. E.O. Olaitan, Ministry of Solid Minerals Development (MSMD), Mrs. A. O. Onimode, Kogi State Ministry of Solid Mineral and Natural Resources, youth and women groups, members of Jakura traditional council, among others.

Earlier in his welcome address, the Chairman of Jakura CDA Committee, Chief Bonibade Ajiboye, appreciated Dangote Cement Plc Obajana Plant for keeping to commitments noting that aside the empowerment programme, the electrification project is almost completed.

He commended the plant for the kind gesture towards the Jakura community despite the security challenge. Goodwill messages were brought to the event by members of Jakura Traditional Council, Oworo Traditional Council, federal and state representatives with all commending and joining Jakura community to express appreciation to Dangote Cement Plc, Obajana Plant.

In his remarks, His Royal Highness, Oba Usman Adoga Ajibola, the Obaro of Jakura, expressed gratitude to Almighty God for blessing Jakura with abundant mineral resources and commended Alhaji Aliko Dangote for choosing to invest in the area.

The royal father also lauded Dangote Cement Plc for its numerous developmental interventions in the community, describing the latest empowerment initiative as another demonstration of the company’s commitment to improving the welfare and livelihoods of its host communities.

He pledged that the community would ensure the sustainability of the projects and see to it that the beneficiaries put their respective benefits to good use.

He prayed for Allah’s continued blessings upon Alhaji Aliko Dangote for his generosity, philanthropy and contributions to humanity.

World.title: Flood: Youth Leader Urges Rivers to Extend Assistance to Ogoni Victims
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The President General of the Ogoni Youth Federation (OYF), Legborsi Yamaabana, has urged the Rivers State Government to extend its flood relief programme to Nyokhana and other flood-affected communities across Ogoniland.

Yamaabana, who is also the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Khana Constituency II in the 2027 Rivers State House of Assembly election, called for N200,000 cash assistance and one year of free healthcare for verified flood victims in the affected communities.

In a statement yesterday, he commended Governor Siminalayi Fubara and his Deputy, Prof Ngozi Odu, who chairs the Rivers State Flood Prevention and Management Committee, for the government’s reported decision to provide the same package to flood victims in Eneka, Obio/Akpor Local Government Area.

He, however, appealed to the government to extend similar consideration to affected households in Ogoniland.

“Humanitarian relief must be guided by need, not geography,” Yamaabana said, stressing that families whose homes, farmlands and livelihoods had been damaged by flooding also required urgent assistance.

He identified more than 23 affected Ogoni communities, including Lueku, Lorre, Luebe, Yeghe, Bera, Kono, Kereke Bo-ue, Zor-Sogho and Okwale, as areas requiring government attention.

According to him, the flooding has submerged homes, damaged properties, disrupted academic activities, destroyed farmlands and threatened the livelihoods of residents.

“The suffering is real, the needs are urgent, and the response must be inclusive,” he said.

Yamaabana disclosed that he had formally written to Odu, in her capacity as chairman of the state flood management committee, requesting urgent intervention in the affected Ogoni communities.

He said the appeal was aimed at securing practical assistance for residents through constructive engagement with the state government.

The OYF president-general also called for an urgent assessment of flood damage, immediate support for displaced and vulnerable households, rehabilitation of drainage channels and the implementation of sustainable flood-prevention measures.

He maintained that the request was not for preferential treatment but for the needs of flood victims in Ogoniland to receive adequate consideration.

“We are not asking for special privileges for Ogoni; we are demanding fair consideration for Ogoni people whose homes, farms and livelihoods have been devastated by flooding,” he said.

He urged the governor and the flood management committee to ensure that relief efforts covered all communities where residents had suffered flood-related losses.

Yamaabana added that he would continue to advocate for the welfare and protection of affected residents in his capacity as leader of the Ogoni Youth Federation and a prospective representative of Khana Constituency II.

“Ogoni flood victims deserve relief. Our communities deserve protection. Our people must not be left behind,” he said.

World.title: Military Clarifies Misconceptions Surrounding Implementation of Newly Approved Pension Rates
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian military has clarified misconceptions surrounding the implementation of the newly approved pension rates.

The Military Pensions Board (MPB) provided these clarifications during a consultative meeting with representatives of military veterans’ associations at the Board’s headquarters in Abuja, yesterday.

According to a statement by the Public Relations Officer of the Military Pensions Board, Squadron Leader Aliyu Mohammed, the engagement provided an opportunity for the Board to explain the implementation process, address concerns raised by the representatives and promote a shared understanding of the new pension rates.

“During the meeting, the representatives expressed their understanding of the explanations provided by the Board and appreciated the opportunity to engage directly with its officials. The discussions also reinforced the importance of continued dialogue, mutual understanding and the use of established communication channels to address pension-related concerns,” he said.

Mohammed said the Board reaffirmed its commitment to the welfare of military pensioners and assured the representatives that it remained dedicated to transparent communication, constructive engagement and the timely resolution of issues within its mandate.

World.title: Gbenga Hashim’s Court Victory: INEC, Accord Party Served With Court Judgement
World.content:
.Mgbudem mounts opposition, appeals judgement of lower court



Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The Certified True Copy of the Federal High Court judgement affirming Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim as the presidential candidate for the 2027 election has been served on the Accord Party and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

This sets the stage for implementation of the court’s orders.

Justice Mohammed Garba Umar, of the Federal High Court in Abuja, ruled on October 5, 2026 that Hashim emerged as Accord’s presidential candidate from the May 30, 2026 primary and ordered the party to submit his name to INEC.

The court further ordered INEC to accept and recognise him as the party’s presidential candidate.

The judgement followed a suit filed by Hashim against Accord Party and INEC over the party’s failure to submit his name after the disputed primary.

Accord Party’s counsel, T.W. Olusesi, told the court that the primary had been validly cancelled.

Hashim’s counsel, Henry Akunebu (SAN) challenged the purported cancellation and the documents relied upon by the party and INEC, arguing that the cancellation letter lacked the party’s official stamp and raised questions about how it was received within the electoral commission.

Justice Umar ultimately rejected the objections and held that the evidence before the court established that Hashim had emerged from the May 30 exercise.

The judge also relied on evidence that the Accord Party had accepted N50 million from Hashim for Expression of Interest and nomination forms.

What has particularly intrigued political and legal observers was the extent to which INEC became involved in the dispute.

The court has now given judgement on the dispute and the CTC of the judgement has been served on both defendants.

“The immediate issue is, therefore, no longer simply whether Hashim won the Accord primary. It is whether the party and the electoral commission will give effect to the orders of the Federal High Court.”

The development also marks a new phase in Hashim’s candidacy.

Following the judgement, the legal dispute that had cast uncertainty over Accord’s presidential ticket has moved into the implementation stage, with the court directing the party to recognise Hashim and forward his name to INEC for the 2027 presidential election.

Indications have emerged however, that the party chairman may still be spoiling for a fight at the appellate court despite Hashim’s call for reconciliation.

The latest development, however, has renewed attention on the unusual legal battle surrounding Hashim’s candidacy.

Meanwhile, Accord Party Chairman, Maxwell Mgbudem, has appealed the judgement delivered by Justice Umar in his suit: FHC/ABJ/1268/226, filed at the Court of Appeal.

World.title: What to do in Cape Town this October on a R100 budget
World.content:
Six Cape Town events in under R100. Image: Pexels

If you’re itching to do something now that the weather’s warmer but don’t want to break the bank, Cape Town has plenty to offer for R100.

This October, you can choose between arts and culture, sports, family and silly fun.

R100 Cape Town Events in October 2026

Plenty of good times to be had in Cape Town on a limited budget.



The city has enough family-friendly activities and good hangouts with friends.

But if you’re on a strict budget, remember: R100 gets you in the door; you may need to budget more for food and drink once inside.

Watch DHL Stormers Play

The DHL Stormers have several fixtures this October. Tickets for seats in the E-section are R90.

Each game takes place on a Saturday in October.

Kick-off typically starts at 16:00, with gates opening at 14:15.

The only exception is the last Saturday game, when kick-off is at 14:15.



Starting on 10 October, they’ll play the Hollywoodbets Sharks. Then on 17 October, they’ll play the Bristol Bears.

They’ll also play the Scarlets on 24 October, and conclude with a game against Ulster Rugby on 31 October.

Attend a Cricket Match

If you’re looking for something to do during the work week, you can attend a cricket match.

The YesPlay Western Province Cobras will play Boland on 14 October 2026 starting 18:00 at Newlands Stadium.

Tickets start at R30.

Watch Cars Race in Killarney

Hear the engines roar in Killarney.

On Saturday 17 October, the Power Series heads into its second-to-last round.

Drivers will be racing for a spot on the podium.

Adult tickets are R100 on Webticket and children under 12 enter for free.

Fly a Kite

If you’re craving family fun, head to the Youngsfield Military Base for the Cape Town International Kite Festival in Ottery.

In addition to flying your own kite, you can view the spectacular designs of international kiters.

The event happens on the weekend of the 24th.

Tickets for children and pensioners start at R60. Adults pay just over R100, including fees.

Picnic blankets and folding chairs are allowed. But attendees can’t bring outside food or drink.

Watch a Pan-African Film

If you want to enjoy something in the arts, head to the Labia Theatre in Gardens on the last Friday of the month.

The Theatre, in collaboration with the Zeitz MOCAA, will be screening a Pan-African film.

On 30 October, the screening will be of Sambizanga (1972), directed by Sarah Maldoror.

Tickets are R30.

Take an Improv Class

Billed as a way to improve your confidence, if you’re looking for something fun to do on a Sunday, head to Newlands for an improv class.

Oops on Purpose hosts their weekly Spontaneous Sundays.

The classes start at 17:30 and end at 19:30. Entry is R75.

Bring a friend or two or come alone to The Hok on Thicket Street, Newlands.

Enjoy a Zombie Walk

Looking for something to do on Halloween? You can join the Zombie Walk.

The event is scheduled for Saturday, 31 October.

Details about where this will be are still to be announced, but the event will start at 16:00.

The walk itself is free, and organisers expect attendees to dress the part.

But entry to the after-party starts at R50.

Updates are available on the organiser’s Facebook page.

If R100 is too steep, you can enjoy the city’s free events. There are plenty of those this October.

World.title: URC Round 3: Sharks’ unbeaten run ends as SFM leads Stormers to win
World.content:
The Stormers seal a bonus-point win to end the Sharks' streak in the URC. Image: Stormers Rugby, Wikimedia Commons.

The Stormers ended the Sharks’ URC winning streak after a fierce game in Cape Town on 10 October.

The hosts were marshalled by Player of the Match Sacha Feinberg-Ngomezulu, who was in peak form.

The visitors looked set for a massive comeback, but failed to come away with points in the Western Cape.



Discipline costs Sharks in URC Round 3

When the Stormers had the ball in hand, they were always threatening, using quick hands and clever kicks to keep the Sharks guessing.

The lineouts were also vastly improved from the Cape Town team’s loss to Edinburgh the week before.

By comparison, the Sharks seemed to be scrambling on defence, with their scrum initially failing to gain any footing.



The Stormers also dominated the early aerial contest, struggling to field hoist kicks and not pressuring the kick chasers.

The Sharks also have some injury concerns, with Eben Etzebeth and Vusi Moyo both leaving the field early.

According to the URC website, the result has pushed the Stormers to 4th on the standings.



How did the first half play out?

The first points came from a wide move across the field, with Seabelo Senatla crossing down easily for the hosts.

Discipline cost the Sharks a few minutes later, conceding a penalty to go 8 points down.

However, the visitors then hit back from a maul, with Manu Tshituka powering his way over.



Midway through the half, Senatla looked to have scored his second, putting a kick through and brilliantly dotting it down himself.

However, after a TMO check, his foot was shown to have been in touch.

The Sharks’ biggest chance of the half came at 26 minutes, when Feinberg-Ngomezulu’s hoist was fielded excellently by Zekhethelo Siyaya.



He then lost the ball trying to chip it through the defensive line.

Replacement fullback Gianni Lombard slotted a long penalty to make it 8-8 after the half-hour mark.

Matt Romao was then sin-binned for a dangerous tackle on Jonathan Roche, with the Stormers following up with a Hacjivah Dayimani try from the lineout maul.



The 14-man Sharks then conceded another try through Andre-Hugo Venter from another maul, with Tshituka yellow-carded to rub salt in the wound.

Feinberg-Ngomezulu then added another conversion to make it 22-8 at halftime.

What happened in the second half of the URC derby?

The Stormers immediately extended their lead with a Leolin Zas try 2 minutes after the whistle.



On the opposite end, a Sharks attack ended in a turnover – Feinberg-Ngomezulu released Senatla with a kick, with Ethan Hooker preventing a certain try.

However, the visitors remained pinned in their own half.

With the scrum still under pressure, Dayimani got his second after the Stormers rolled their forward pack over the line.



Leading by 26 points, things look sealed with more than half an hour to play.

However, Romao redeemed himself with a try mauled over from the lineout, with Lombard adding the 2 points.

Minutes later, the Sharks were penalised in their half, before Feinberg-Ngomezulu kicking the ball over the dead-ball line to gift possession back.



After a dreadful Cobus Reinach hoist and a penalty against them, the Stormers could not keep Phepsi Buthelezi out to take the score to 22-34.

Momentum looked to be with the Sharks, with Hooker putting in a massive shift.

Haashim Pead then made his debut off the bench, but did not have much time to make an impact.



The Stormers eventually made it click again, rolling over from the maul to let JJ Kotze claim the try.

With the result out of reach, the Sharks chased hard for a bonus point.

However, the Stormers were too good on attack and defence, coming away with the spoils.

World.title: Sundowns beat Pirates to win first MTN8 trophy in five years
World.content:
Thalente Mbatha challenges Marcelo Allende in the MTN8 final between Orlando Pirates and Mamelodi Sundowns. Image: Mamelodi Sundowns media

Ronwen Williams made unbelievable saves to deny Orlando Pirates after the break. Sundowns lift the MTN8 trophy for the first time since 2021, denying Pirates a record fifth consecutive title.

Below is how all the action unfolded…

LIVE UPDATES



90 +7′ ⚽️ Goal! Rayners makes no mistake from the spot kick. Orlando Pirates 0-2 Mamelodi Sundowns.

89′ ⚽️ Penalty! Mokobodi fouls Ndlovu. Referee Tom points to the spot.

88′ ⚽️ Masilela dribbles past two Sundowns defenders but his shot goes inches wide. The score Orlando Pirates 0-1 Mamelodi Sundowns.

83′ ⚽️ So close! Morena’s inviting cross is met by Rayners but his flick goes wide.

76′ ⚽️ Another great save! Williams denies Masilela. It remains Orlando Pirates 0-1 Mamelodi Sundowns.

75′ ⚽️ Massive miss! Matthews plays through Leon but the Colombian shoots wide from 10 yards.



71′ ⚽️ Great recovery! Lungu released on the counter but his cut back to Appollis is cleared by Ndamane.

61′ ⚽️ Save! Lungu’s effort meets a brilliant stop from Williams. It remains Orlando Pirates 0-1 Mamelodi Sundowns.

59′ ⚽️ Penalty! Mokoena fouls Mbuthuma in the box.

53′ ⚽️ Sundowns dictating play as Pirates chase the ball.

48′ ⚽️ Yellow card. Moremi is cautioned for a foul on Santos.

46′ ⚽️ We’re back in Durban for the second half. Orlando Pirates 0-1 Mamelodi Sundowns.

HALF TIME: ORLANDO PIRATES 0-1 MAMELODI SUNDOWNS

45′ ⚽️ Referee Abongile Tom blows for the break.

42′ ⚽️ So close! Hotto’s freekick flies inches away from the goal.

38′ ⚽️ Powerful save! Williams denies an electric shot from Lungu on the near post. Orlando Pirates 0-1 Mamelodi Sundowns.

31′ ⚽️ What a save! Leon puts one into the corner but Chaine makes a flying save.

28′ ⚽️ Massive chance! Seema plays through Sibisi but the Bafana Bafana defender fails to get his foot on the ball. It remains Orlando Pirates 0-1 Mamelodi Sundowns.

24′ ⚽️ Big miss. Morena with a chance in the box but his effort is saved by Chaine.

22′ ⚽️ Very close! Khoza takes a powerful header that goes narrowly wide of Pirates’ goal.

21′ ⚽️ Great defending. Seema clears in the box after a dangerous Modiba cross to Leon. It stays Orlando Pirates 0-1 Mamelodi Sundowns.

16′ ⚽️ Sundowns are settling into the game with some dangerous counters.

11′ ⚽️ Goal! Sundowns with a surprise goal. Mokoena taps-in from two yards after a smart Matuludi assist through Seema’s legs. Orlando Pirates 0-1 Mamelodi Sundowns.

9′ ⚽️ Shot! Mbuthuma takes a shot from 18 yards but it goes wide. It remains Orlando Pirates 0-0 Mamelodi Sundowns.

4′ ⚽️ Big chance! Mbuthuma released on the right but his cross-cum-shot goes wide.

World.title: Four killed in KwaMsane tavern
World.content:
ESHOWE – A police constable allegedly shot and killed three women and injured a man before turning the gun on himself at a tavern in KwaMsane, KwaZulu-Natal.

Police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda said police responded to reports of a shooting at a liquor establishment at Nkodibe area in KwaMsane, and when they arrived they found four bodies with gunshot wounds, and one victim with a gunshot wound who was taken to hospital.

“It was reported that the off-duty police constable also disarmed another man of his firearm during the incident. Both firearms were found at the scene. The cause of the shooting is unknown at this stage.”

In a separate incident, police in Eshowe are tracing a suspect who allegedly shot and killed three people at a grocery chain store in Eshowe on Saturday.

“Reports indicate that the suspect, who is former employee of the store, had gone to the store for his internal disciplinary hearing. The suspect allegedly produced a firearm and shot three people who were declared dead at the scene. A manhunt for the suspect is underway.”

World.title: SANDF arrives in Durban
World.content:
DURBAN - The army has been spotted in Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, amid tensions over asylum applications and illegal immigration.

Protests erupted after the Constitutional Court ruling that everyone must be given a fair chance to apply for asylum, regardless of documentation.

Violent unrest led to looting and the torching of vehicles.

Government has called for calm as tensions simmer.

World.title: Joburg Water warns of possible outages
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A power outage at the Zuikerbosch Water Treatment Plant has crippled pumping at the Palmiet Booster Station.

Johannesburg Water warns that parts of Sandton, Diepsloot, Rabie Ridge, and surrounding areas could face low water pressure or total outages.

The utility said it is monitoring the system and taking steps to stabilise supply.

Residents are urged to use water sparingly.

World.title: ‘Captured’ casts spotlight on prison life
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Ex-Pollsmoor Correctional Centre inmates are using visual art to depict the realities of life behind bars.

This they say helps them deal with past trauma, their reintegration into society, and also to make a living.

Dubbed "Captured", the visual storytelling project, is set to eventually become a coffee table book.

Life behind bars is often reduced to statistics, without the human factor.

Enrico Samuels, an artist, served sixteen years behind bars for armed robbery said art connected him with people helping him to navigate life now as a free man.

"I want to become a successful artist, doctor is helping me to get there with the projects...lovely projects and I enjoy myself in the projects and from there I see a brighter future from doc's side, because she is taking me that way, so I can see the sun on the other side already,” said Samuels.

Michael Sauls said art serves as a conduit in helping them deal with their past and educate the public.

“People have no an idea of what prison is like, they think that everything is happy go-lucky or it's like a journey to another paradise, it's not worth it being there...you see it's easy to commit a crime, but it's not easy serving the time."

Dr Suzette Leal, the founder of Words Set Free, said the art tells the stories of the people behind it.

"If you say the work is beautiful, that's a complement to our artists and their ability, but the story is not beautiful. It's real and true and painful and traumatic. So, I think if anything I hope it discourages someone from getting involved in crime, but I think we don't reduce crime by making prison sentences longer or by making the conditions within them worse. We reduce crime by creating opportunities for people to create a livelihood outside of crime.”

Another artist, Kleinbooi Hendricks said: "I said to myself, although the parole board gave me a date to go out of prison, I'm not going. I will either complete my entire sentence but I'm not going out if I haven't worked on myself being a changed man or a different person. I did that because I said I'd either eat out of a dustbin outside, but I'm not going to commit crime again."

World.title: Change living conditions – Ndlozi
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Real change begins with communities taking responsibility for their own development.

Those are the views of Dr Mbuyiseni Ndlozi, Founder of the Batho Pele Convention.

The initiative calls on South Africans to take the lead in improving their own living conditions.

“We are here to say you are the solution you are looking for. We are here to say you are the saviour, the developer, the healer and the builder you are looking for. We are here to vote for you to do it on your own.

“We are here to say you are the saviours you are looking for. We are not a corporate think tank. Long have we interpreted our misery from broadcast to podcast, think shops to talk shops.

“The point is to change our living conditions, one pothole at a time, one classroom at a time and one production hub at a time,” Ndlozi said.

World.title: Repairs delay Joburg's pool reopenings
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Johannesburg's public pools are missing out on the summer rush.

And most are still closed despite the rising temperatures.

Community leader Dulton Adams said poor planning, lack of proper budgeting and no clear management plans, are leaving residents without these facilities.

The city has 57 public pools, but only 13 are open so far.

Ten more are expected to open on Monday.

"Every season there's just no budget.

There's just no management plan. There's no vision to make sure that the children come off the streets and you look at the pool. This is not the only pool.

"Remember spring day, pools must open first. Then the City Council asked for 1 October, pools would be open. That was missed and then now the 7th," Adams said.

World.title: ‘ANC could be the biggest loser’ - political strategist
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The ANC could emerge as the biggest loser in this year's municipal elections.

This is the view is political strategist Brutus Malada.

He said the party’s declining support could leave it with less influence across key metros and this could push it into a weakened position ahead of the 2029 elections.

“ANC will be the big loser in this. The trend is clear. It's clear that they are losing at a margin of 10 to 12 percent and that will actually mean the end of the ANC and it will become lame duck for this period in between the two elections.

“That it will sit, it will be a national government President Ramaphosa sitting in Tshwane. The Union Buildings which is led by another party and in Cape Town which is the legislative arm of the state which is led by the DA.

“So here is a political party that is running the country as the head of the State but it has no control of the economy hub, it has no control of administrative hub, it has no control of legislative hub,” Malada said.

World.title: Murdered teen twins buried in Mamelodi
World.content:
Mamelodi – The family and friends of the slain 14-year-old twins have gathered in Mamelodi West to bid farewell to the boys.

Bonolo and Botlhale Makena were found dead in their home a week ago. They had multiple stab wounds.

The boys' mother made the gruesome discovery at home, when she returned from work.

As police investigate, residents are demanding that this case does not become another unresolved killing.

Neighobour Padi Matlala said the Mamelodi West community is demanding justice.

“The community has been here before. The community is saying, ‘please justice system, don't take us there.’ We were there in 1982. Two members of the community were brutally murdered. 44 years later, nobody has been held responsible.

“The community is saying justice system never, never again should you go through this. The pressure that you put on the government throughout the week, the outrage you showed must bear fruit. Somebody or some people must be held responsible for this. We are better than this,” Matlala said.

World.title: Ruto wades into growing ODM-UDA conflict
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto marks Mazingira Day by planting trees in Elgon downs, Trans-Nzoia County. [PCS]

President William Ruto delved into the growing tension among Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) and United Democratic Alliance (UDA) contenders in the Coast and asked them to tone it down during his recent tour of the region.

Speaking hours before he wound up his eight-day tour, Ruto appeared to notice the widening cracks and told politicians within the two parties to embrace a ceasefire and unite against the opposition.

The head of state, who is facing a formidable challenge from the united opposition, warned that divisions in the ODM and UDA could weaken their team, whose union gives it a chance to win the 2027 general election.

“ODM and UDA are one team, and you should accommodate each other under a broad-based government. We should not allow divisions in ODM and UDA to undermine our unity of purpose,” he stated.

His statement appeared to be directed at the growing tensions among contenders, particularly in Kwale, Mombasa and Kilifi counties where prominent politicians face challengers within the ODM and UDA political union.

President Ruto’s earlier attempt to zone the region in favour of sitting governors is also blamed for the cracks in the broad-based team at the Coast.

In Mombasa County, UDA secretary general Mr Hassan Omar has already rejected a plan by the so-called broad-based team to support governor Abdulswamd Nassir’s re-election.

Omar, who is also a member of the East African Legislative Assembly (EALA) insisted that he will challenge Mr Nassir.

Already, businessman and EALA member Mr Suleiman Shahbal has quit ODM after he left he could not get the party ticket as the president's allies favour Nassir, a deputy party leader.

Shhabal has since aligned himself to former Laikipia governor Mr Murithi Nderitu’s Kenya Reform Party even as he insisted that he will be on the ballot.

In Mombasa, Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs Cabinet Secretary Mr Hassan Joho and governor Nassir appeared to be handing over Coast which was the ODM leader late Raila Odinga’s political turf, to President Ruto.

“This region stands with Ruto because he has dignified us with title deeds and many other development projects. We however expect him to support us when we seek the presidential seat in 2032,” Joho said.

Joho’s elder brother Abubakar Joho, who is a prominent businessman, has also joined the campaign for President Ruto.

While touring Kwale, Ruto addressed the growing noise among the main contenders, Governor Fatuma Achani (UDA), Prof Hamadi Boga and Engineer Lung’anzi Chai (ODM) after the broad-based leaders appeared to settle for Ms Achani who has the backing of Sports CS and former Kwale governor Salim Mvurya.

After witnessing the rising political tension, Ruto changed tone and told the three contenders to directly seek support from the voters rather than relying on external political backing.

In a complete change of heart and political tact, Ruto emphasised that the power to choose leaders ultimately belongs to the electorate, who will evaluate candidates based on their track record and development agenda for the region.

“You should all seek votes from the people and not rely on external backing. What I need from all of you is your support,” he stated.

For long, Governor Achani has enjoyed unwavering backing of President Ruto, Mvurya and recently Joho, who had preferred Kwale to be zoned in favour of the governor and UDA.

But Prof Boga, who has been Mr Joho’s ally, described the broad-based government’s zoning arrangement as undemocratic and a coercion to the Kwale electorate who he said should be allowed to choose their leaders without external interference.

Boga has been critical about the attempt to stop some aspirants from contesting seats in the broad-based government, noting that it was possible to zone candidates and difficult to do so for the voters.

In a statement, Boga noted that former Gender CS and Kilifi governor aspirant Ms Aisha Jumwa’s recent departure from UDA to Wiper Patriotic Front (WPF) reflected a growing sense among a segment of coastal leaders that decisions about their political future are increasingly being made elsewhere, then handed down as settled outcomes rather than negotiated realities.

“Zoning at the Coast is a fantasy: You can zone candidates but you cannot zone the voters,” Boga had warned.

“And if UDA and ODM are not paying attention to that signal, they may be underestimating the political consequences of their emerging arrangements at the Coast. “There is a dangerous assumption taking root in the broad-based arrangement: that coastal politics can be settled around a table in Nairobi and then delivered to voters as a finished political package. You take this seat, we take that one, and the voters will follow,” he added.

Boga, who came second in the 2022 governor poll, warned that if the Coast is mishandled, the problem will not necessarily be that voters have suddenly embraced another political formation, but the greater danger is that voters may decide that none of the established arrangements speak for them, creating either a rebellion or apathy.

In Kilifi County, the broad-based team publicly worked with Governor Gideon Mung’aro, forcing Ms Jumwa, his main challenger, to quit the government team in protest.

Kilifi Senate aspirant Mr Stephen Kahocho and Ganze parliamentary aspirant Ms Zawadi Kingi have publicly warned that they might be forced to quit UDA and vie as independent candidates or join other political formations.

This is after it emerged that the broad-based arrangement was behind Mung’aro (ODM), Kilifi senator Stewart Madzayo (ODM) and Ganze MP Kenneth Kazungu Tungule of Pamoja African Alliance (PAA), an affiliate of UDA.

World.title: Kalonzo to Ruto: You have no numbers
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka speaks during launch of economic empowerment equipment distribution at Kenyatta Stadium in Machakos town on October 9, 2026. [John Muia, Standard]

The united opposition will deal President William Ruto a humiliating defeat in next year’s general election, Wiper Party leader Kalonzo Musyoka has predicted.

Speaking Friday in his Ukambani backyard during an empowerment equipment handover ceremony hosted by Governor Wavinya Ndeti at the Kenyatta Stadium in Machakos, Kalonzo declared the opposition will defeat Ruto at the ballot ‘no matter what magic he (Ruto) deploys.

“Ruto has been cornered. We have heard him suggesting that they will import foreigners from neighboring countries to vote for him but even so, he will not secure the numbers. We in the united opposition have committed to produce a single candidate that will face Ruto at the ballot,” Kalonzo said.

Recognizing the need to consolidate his lower Eastern vote bloc, Kalonzo rallied the Akamba community to come out in huge numbers to register as voters in the upcoming voter listing initiative by the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC).

“It is the time to redeem this country. The IEBC will as from next month undertake the final leg of voter registration and I urge all eligible voters to apply for national identity cards and register as voters,” he said, vowing he will defeat Ruto in Luo Nyanza.

Kalonzo called out Ruto over what he termed as the president’s habit of making empty promises to Kenyans. “The other day I heard Ruto promising thousands of dams across the country. He should come for benchmarking in Machakos. Retired President Mwai Kibaki and I secured African Development Bank (ADB) funding for the construction of Yatta Dam and now he has ten months left in office. When will he build?” he posed.

Former Attorney General Justin Muturi, who flanked Kalonzo, declared time was fast running out for the opposition to identify and name its presidential flag bearer for the next year’s general election.

The DP party leader, who has gone public declaring his choice of Kalonzo as the presidential ticket bearer for the opposition expressed his frustrations for the opposition’s dillydallying in naming its flag bearer.

“We (the opposition) are tired of singing one song for years that we will produce and name one person to face Ruto. When you see us here another day, do not entertain such kind of talk. Demand that it is Kalonzo for State House,” said Muturi.

During the ceremony, Governor Wavinya Ndeti unveiled assorted empowerment equipment targeting about 6000 beneficiaries across the county.

Addressing residents during the forum, Wavinya jeered at UDA-allied politicians who have been dishing out cash handouts to residents, terming it untenable.

“It is time to demonstrate to those who are approaching our people with cheap hand-outs that when the people of Machakos are given the tools to work, they produce real wealth. My commitment is that I will continue allocating resources to asset-based empowerment until every household in Machakos enjoys economic dignity,” Wavinya said.

World.title: Revealed: 84 Kenyans killed, 52 missing in Russia-Ukraine war
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi. [File,Standard]

The government has records of 354 Kenyans linked to the Russia-Ukraine war, including 84 classified as killed or missing in action and five being held as prisoners of war in Ukraine.

Prime Cabinet Secretary and Foreign and Diaspora Affairs Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi gave the updated figures in a response to Parliament on the recruitment of Kenyans into the Russian military and the detention of Kenyans in Ukraine on Thursday, October 8.

The records show that 77 Kenyans remain on the front lines, 38 are in camps, 52 have an unknown or unclassified location and 34 are hospitalised.

Another 62 Kenyans have been repatriated, while one is in detention and another has completed a military contract.

The government said Russia has stopped the enlistment of additional Kenyans after Kenya secured the country’s placement on Russia’s ‘Stop List’ during Mudavadi’s visit to Moscow in March.

“The Embassy of Kenya in Moscow has since confirmed that no additional Kenyan nationals have been enlisted in the Special Military Operation following the implementation of the Stop List,” Mudavadi said.

Russian authorities have told Kenya that requests to terminate military contracts will be considered on a case-by-case basis by individual military unit commanders.

Mudavadi said Kenya continues to engage Russian authorities and affected families over the burial, cremation or repatriation of remains after Russia said its Defence Ministry could not meet the cost of repatriating the remains of deceased Kenyans.

Five Kenyans held in Ukraine

Five Kenyan nationals are currently being held as prisoners of war in Ukraine, according to information sent to Kenya by the Ukrainian Embassy in Vienna on September 3.

The government identified them as Evans Kibet, detained since May 2025; Willi Muniu Macharia, detained since November 2025; Haron Kibet Pachenge, detained since March 2026; Joseph, detained since April 2026; and Francis Ndarua Ndungu.

Kenya’s Honorary Consul in Ukraine visited the Zakhid 1 prisoner-of-war camp and reported that the detainees were being held in humane conditions, had access to medical services and were being treated under rules governing prisoners of war.

The government also said Ukraine was holding the remains of four other Kenyans.

They are Simon Gitau, Clinton Nyapara Mogesa, Dennis Bagaka Obwori and Eric Mwangi Nyambura.

Kenya is seeking the release and repatriation of the affected Kenyans through diplomatic channels, including engagement with Ukraine and the International Committee of the Red Cross.

The government wants Kenyans held as prisoners of war to be considered as possible victims of international human trafficking.

Mudavadi said many of the affected Kenyans reported that recruiters lured them with promises of employment before they ended up in military service.

The government says the circumstances surrounding their recruitment could fit the definition of trafficking under Article 3(a) of the Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, also known as the Palermo Protocol.

It wants the issue considered during negotiations over their repatriation so the Kenyans can access assistance available to trafficking victims.

President William Ruto has also raised the matter directly with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during a telephone conversation, according to the government.

Kenya has further received approval from Kyiv for its ambassador to Ukraine, with the government saying this will improve its ability to respond to cases involving Kenyans in the country.

The State Department for Diaspora Affairs said families should report cases to the government as soon as communication with relatives in Russia is disrupted.

Once a family reports a case, the department collects identification details, travel information and next-of-kin contacts before referring the case to the Kenyan Embassy in Moscow for verification.

The government has also facilitated the return of 62 Kenyans who had been involved in Russia’s military operations.

It has provided affected families with updates from diplomatic missions, information on compensation processes, psychosocial support and guidance on the repatriation or burial of remains.

The government said it is also expanding measures to prevent deceptive recruitment by providing pre-departure information, urging Kenyans to verify recruitment agencies and employment offers and strengthening emergency assistance through Kenyan diplomatic missions.

The scale of the recruitment first emerged publicly in February when Parliament was told that more than 1,000 Kenyans had been recruited to fight for Russia.

The National Intelligence Service report presented to lawmakers said recruiters targeted former security personnel and civilians with promises of lucrative employment, salaries and bonuses.

The figures at the time included 89 Kenyans on the frontline, 39 hospitalised, 28 missing in action, 35 in camps or bases, 30 repatriated, one detained and one who had completed a contract.

The government then stepped up diplomatic efforts. In March, Kenya announced an agreement with Russia to stop further enlistment of Kenyans into its military operations and to facilitate consular support and voluntary disengagement for Kenyans already serving.

The issue remains unresolved for many families. More than 30 families affected by the recruitment were reported this week to be seeking a meeting with President Ruto before Kenya's delegation travels to Moscow for the Russia-Africa Summit, demanding answers on missing relatives, repatriation of survivors and the return of remains.

World.title: Wajir patient isolated over suspected viral haemorrhagic fever
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The patient, a resident of Habaswein in Wajir South Sub-County, is currently admitted at Albadar Nursing Home. [File, Standard]

A 20-year-old man in Habaswein, Wajir County, has been isolated after presenting with symptoms consistent with a suspected viral haemorrhagic fever, following recent travel from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

The patient, a resident of Habaswein in Wajir South Sub-County, is currently admitted at Albadar Nursing Home, where he is being treated after developing fever, headache and cough. He was also found to have severe anaemia, with a haemoglobin level of 4g/dL.

According to a disease surveillance report filed at Habaswein Police Station, the patient told health officials that he had recently travelled to the DRC, where he worked as a “tan boy” on a cargo truck or trailer.

He reportedly developed fever and headache while still in the DRC on September 2, 2026, before traveling by trailer to Uganda, where he stayed for about five days and sought medical attention.

The report states that he was treated with antibiotics in Uganda before travelling by trailer to Malaba. From Malaba, he travelled by motorcycle to a relative's residence, where he stayed for approximately five days.

He later travelled by trailer to Nairobi and proceeded by bus to Isiolo, where he stayed for about 10 days before travelling to Habaswein by Probox vehicle. He arrived in the town around September 20.

Upon arrival, the patient sought treatment at Hilac Medical Clinic, where he was managed for pneumonia and septicaemia for about three days.

However, his condition did not improve and he was subsequently transferred to Albadar Nursing Home, where he remains admitted.

The report adds that the patient is receiving intravenous Augmentin and paracetamol and has been transfused with two units of whole blood.

“Despite the above interventions, the patient remains clinically unwell and sick-looking,” the report states.

Authorities have since placed the patient in isolation as investigations continue to establish the cause of his illness.

“Sample collection has been completed, and the specimen will be shipped to National Public Health Laboratories tonight,” the report states.

World.title: Complainant letters cannot be used to initiate judge's removal, court rules
World.content:
Chief Justice Martha Koome. [File]

A letter addressed to the Chief Justice seeking administrative intervention cannot form the basis for removing a judge, the Employment and Labour Relations Court (ELRC) has ruled.

Delivering a unanimous judgment in a case filed by Environment and Land Court Judge Anthony Ombwayo, a three-judge ELRC bench comprising Justices Jemimah Keli, Onesmus Makau, and Dr. Jacob Gikeri ruled that a letter written to the Chief Justice cannot simply be forwarded to the Judicial Service Commission (JSC) and treated as a petition for removal.

World.title: How KNEC plans to stop cheating in 2026 exams
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The Kenya National Examinations Council (KNEC) Chief Executive Officer Dr David Njengere. [File]

The Kenya National Examinations Council (KNEC) will use smart padlocks to secure all examination storage containers as more than 3.6 million candidates sit the 2026 national examinations and assessments.

KNEC Chief Executive Officer Dr David Njengere said the council would monitor the containers from its headquarters to prevent anyone from accessing examination papers before the scheduled times.

“Last year KNEC piloted the use of smart padlocks in 250 containers. This year all containers will be secured using the smart padlocks which will be monitored from the KNEC headquarters,” said Dr Njengere.

Under the system, officials will open containers at designated times. Officials will access Kenya Primary School Education Assessment (KPSEA) and Kenya Junior School Education Assessment (KJSEA) papers at 6 a.m., while centre managers will collect Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) papers at 7 a.m. and 12:30 p.m.

However, Dr Njengere identified mobile phones as the biggest challenge in preventing examination malpractice.

“Mobile phones remain our biggest challenge in administration of KCSE examination,” observed Dr Njengere.

He warned that the council would not allow candidates or examination officials to have mobile phones at examination centres during examination sessions.

“Any contravention of this rule will constitute a malpractice as per the KNEC Act and the Rules and Regulations,” noted Dr Njengere.

The council will deploy 342,005 contracted professionals to administer and manage the examinations and assessments. They include centre managers, supervisors, invigilators, security officers and drivers.

For KCSE, KNEC will deploy 10,765 centre managers, 12,274 supervisors, 57,432 invigilators and 21,388 security officers. Each examination centre will have at least two police officers.

Centre managers will collect KCSE papers twice a day, and KNEC will place morning and afternoon papers in marked cartons to reduce mix-ups and unauthorised access.

KNEC has personalised question papers with candidates’ details, and examiners will receive anonymised scripts with those details removed.

The 2026 examination and assessment season will involve 3,634,846 candidates, a 6.13 per cent increase from the 3,424,836 registered in 2025.

KCSE rehearsals will take place on Friday, October 16. Examinations for papers with low candidature will run from Monday, October 19 to Friday, October 30, while papers with large candidature will run from Monday, November 2 to Friday, November 20.

KPSEA and KJSEA assessments will run from Monday, October 26 to Friday, October 30.

KNEC Chairperson Prof. Julius Nyabundi said the council was preparing for possible disruption from El Nino rains.

“As we start off the 2026 field administration season, one of the risks we contend with are the attempts to cheat in assessments and examination,” said Prof. Nyabundi.

He urged candidates, parents and examination officials to protect the integrity of the examinations, warning that malpractice could undermine public confidence in the education system.

“Cheating in examinations undermines public confidence in the credibility, fairness and quality of the entire education system,” noted Prof. Nyabundi.

KNEC will operate a 24-hour call centre with toll-free numbers for candidates, officials and members of the public to report incidents and seek assistance during the examination period.

The 2026 cycle will continue the implementation of Competency-Based Education assessments, including School-Based Assessments in primary, junior and senior school.

Grade 10 learners are undertaking their first School-Based Assessment, which will contribute 15 marks towards the Kenya Certificate of Basic Education.

World.title: Mbadi hits out at Sifuna, says opposition lacks economic agenda
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

National Treasury CS John Mbadi after opening new classrooms and administration blocks constructed by the M-Pesa Foundation at Ligongo Primary School in Suba South Constituency. [James Omoro, Standard]

The National Treasury CS John Mbadi has hit out at Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, saying that criticising President William Ruto should not be an agenda for a presidential candidate.

Speaking when he opened new classrooms and administration blocks constructed by M-Pesa Foundation at Ligongo Primary School in Suba South Constituency, Mbadi said lack of economic agenda makes the opposition unsuitable to lead the country.

“I have heard of opposition leaders who want the presidency, but they do not have an agenda for the economic transformation of this country,” he said.

The CS claimed that none of the opposition leaders is suitable for the presidency.

“These opposition leaders cannot make any economic change in this country. They should not be elected,” he said.

He told Nyanza residents to shun the new wave of opposition led by Sifuna.

Mbadi claimed that opposition leaders lack political direction.

He said Sifuna had taken too long to unveil a political party that he will use to run for the presidency.

“Do not join the opposition bandwagon. We are just a few months away from the General Election, but Sifuna still doesn’t know a political party he will use to run for the presidency. They are still leaving in confusion,” Mbadi said.

He said Sifuna has not demonstrated how to improve this country’s economy.

“Former President Uhuru Kenyatta left the economy of this country in tatters. We have tried to improve it but we are not yet where we want it to be,” Mbadi said.

He urged Nyanza residents to support Ruto.

The CS said Ruto’s government had improved mega infrastructural projects across the country as part of economic transformation.

He cited the 74 km Mbita- Sindo- Sori road, Lake Victoria ring road and other infrastructure projects as some of the reasons residents should support Ruto.

“I urge you to support Ruto so that we can continue acquiring more development projects in this region,” Mbadi said.

World.title: Kericho Annex Prison under scrutiny over death of remand prisoner
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Brenda Chemutai, 19, who allegedly committed suicide inside the Kericho Annex Prison where she was awaiting trial for an offence of being in possession of bhang that was seized in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer. [Courtesy]

Questions are mounting over security and accountability at Kericho Annex Prison following the death of a 19-year-old remand prisoner in a suspected case of suicide.

Her family is demanding answers about how she obtained a bedsheet and why they were not notified until nearly 10 hours after the incident.

Brenda Chemutai was reportedly found hanging from a double-decker bed at around 9 am when her fellow cellmates were having breakfast on Friday.

The cell had eight inmates, who had gone for breakfast, according to a police report.

However, her relatives state they were not informed until about 7 pm, after her body had already been taken from the prison and transferred to the Kericho County Hospital Mortuary.

The delay has raised serious concerns for the family, which calls for authorities to clarify what happened between the time Chemutai was discovered and when her next of kin were contacted.

Kericho East Directorate of Criminal Investigation (DCI) officer, Kennedy Apindi, said police have launched investigations following reports from prison officials that the incident was a suicide.

He mentioned that preliminary information indicated Chemutai allegedly used a bedsheet.

The family, however, insists that investigators determine when she was found, who discovered her, when the incident was reported to police, who authorised her body’s removal, and why her relatives were not notified immediately.

“We had spoken with Brenda. She was expected to be released around December, and by January we would all have been together at home,” said her sister, Phyllis Cherotich.

Cherotich added that the family had seen no signs indicating Chemutai intended to take her own life.

"Her death has shocked us deeply. She never mentioned any plans of this nature. We want to understand how this was possible given the level of security at the facility," she said.

The circumstances surrounding the alleged use of a bedsheet have also raised questions for the family.

Her uncle, Michael Rono, questioned how such an item came into Chemutai's possession while she was in a remand facility.

"I am deeply surprised. When one enters the prison, one is carefully searched. Where did the bedsheet come from? We ask the government to ensure justice is done," Rono said.

Chemutai had been in remand since 2024, with her relatives saying she was arrested while still a minor and had spent nearly two years awaiting the conclusion of her case.

She was being tried for the offence of possession of bhang in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer.

Her death has consequently brought renewed scrutiny to not only what happened inside the prison but also the circumstances that led to her prolonged detention.

Youth activists from the Voice of Youth Organisation, led by Kelvin Kipchichir, have joined the family in demanding investigations into both the death and the case that resulted in Chemutai's detention.

Kipchichir claimed Chemutai was arrested alongside other suspects in a vehicle allegedly linked to an Officer Commanding Station serving in Kakamega.

According to the activists, police recovered 32 rolls of bhang from the vehicle, while some of the suspects allegedly fled, leaving Chemutai behind.

The claims have not been independently established.

Kipchichir questioned why Chemutai remained in custody for such a prolonged period and called for scrutiny of the circumstances surrounding the vehicle and its alleged connection to the police officer.

“We are concerned that an OCS in the National Police Service could allow a vehicle to be used by an individual with a known criminal record,” he said.

He called on the Ministry of Interior to establish who owned or controlled the vehicle and under what circumstances it was allegedly being used.

The activists said the vehicle was still at Kericho Police Station.

For the family, the tragedy has been compounded by personal loss. Chemutai's father died while she was in remand, while she leaves behind a young child.

Relatives said detectives had informed them that the person alleged to own the bhang had since been arrested and was being held in Kisumu.

But the immediate question for Chemutai's family is what happened during her final hours.

They want a clear account of the period between the reported discovery of her body at about 9 am and the notification of the family nearly 10 hours later.

They also want investigators to establish how the bedsheet allegedly used in the incident came into her possession and whether prison officers followed all required procedures after she was found.

The activists are calling for the inquiry to extend beyond the death of Chemutai to her arrest, the length of her detention and the handling of the case against her.

The family has demanded a transparent and independent investigation, saying it wants answers on how a teenager who entered the justice system while still a minor ended up dead in remand custody.

The family says it wants those questions answered before proceeding with burial arrangements.

World.title: The story behind the Amr Diab song chosen by Malaysia’s PM to welcome Sisi
World.content:
Egyptian pop superstar Amr Diab and his famous song “Tamally Maak” (Always With You) trended on social media after Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim selected the track as the background music for photos posted on his official Instagram account.

The photos captured his reception of Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi upon the latter’s arrival at Kuala Lumpur International Airport on Friday, marking the start of his visit to Malaysia.

The choice of song—originally released on an Amr Diab album in 2000 and still popular with audiences 26 years later— was well-received, while the buzz drew renewed attention to the song’s history and its widespread appeal beyond the Arab world.

Significant Milestone

The album “Tamally Maak” was released in 2000, a period that witnessed shifts in the style of Egyptian music—spanning everything from musical arrangements to the collaborative dynamics between singers, lyricists, and composers.

The album helped popularize a new genre of Egyptian pop by blending Eastern melodies with Western musical arrangements.

The album cover bore the credit “Artistic Vision by Amr Diab and Tarek Madkour,” highlighting the creative partnership that helped shape Diab’s musical identity—one defined by the fusion of Western rhythms and Eastern melodies.

Album Contributors

The album “Tamally Maak” featured a number of lyricists and composers who went on to become renowned figures in the Egyptian music industry, including Amir Teima, Rabie al-Sioufi, and Ahmed Ali Moussa, alongside Ayman Bahgat Kamar, Mohamed Refaei, and Bahaa al-Din Mohamed.

The album also included compositions by Amr Mostafa, Sherif Tag, Walid Saad, and Essam Karika, with Amr Diab himself contributing to the songwriting.

Several of the album’s tracks bore titles phrased as questions—such as “Wa Keda Eini Einak?” (Just Like That, Right in Front of Everyone?), “Weya Amla Eih?” (And How Is She Doing?), “A’mel Eih?” (What Should I Do?), and “Law Kan Yardik?” (If It Pleases You?)—while the song “Qalbi Ikhtarak” (My Heart Chose You) became associated in the minds of some listeners with the phrase “Aref Leih Ana Qalbi Ikhtarak?” (Do You Know Why My Heart Chose You?).

“Tamally Maak”

“Tamally Maak” was the first song Amr Diab recorded for the titular album.

It was composed by Sherif Tag, with lyrics by the late poet Ahmed Ali Moussa—marking his debut as a songwriter.

Ahmed Ali Moussa was just 18 years old when he mailed the lyrics to Amr Diab’s home, including his name and phone number.

This marked the beginning of the journey for a song that would go on to become one of Diab’s most famous works.

The word “Tamally” (meaning “always” or “constantly”) caught Amr Diab’s attention due to its distinctly Egyptian character and rhythmic quality—particularly given that the artist Mohamed Fawzi had previously released a song titled “Tamally Fi Qalbi” (Always in My Heart).

The song’s arrangement blended Latin pop and flamenco, utilizing guitars, electronic rhythms, and live instrumentation, while its musical intro became one of its most recognizable features for audiences.

Sung in Various Languages

The reach of the song “Tamally Maak” extended far beyond the Arab world; numerous artists have covered it in various languages, including Bulgarian, Hindi, Turkish, Spanish, Albanian, Greek, and Armenian.

According to available information regarding the song’s various versions, Bulgarian singer Ivana performed it in Bulgarian in 2002, followed by Amir Jameel in Hindi in 2004 and Erkan Hakan in Turkish in 2006.

In 2007, a Spanish version by Antonio Carmona appeared, alongside versions in other languages—such as Albanian by Gazi, Greek by Lefteris Pantazis, and Armenian by Olga.

Twenty-six years after the album’s release, “Tamally Maak” is now back in the spotlight – highlighting its enduring appeal.

World.title: Experts explain reasons behind Fitch affirming Egypt’s “B” rating
World.content:
The decision by the global credit rating agency Fitch to affirm Egypt’s rating at “B” with a stable outlook has been welcomed by economic experts and academics, as well as the Finance Ministry, which emphasized that the Egyptian economy has once again demonstrated its resilience and ability to absorb shocks amidst regional turmoil.

The ministry noted in a statement that consistent, proactive policies have contributed to positive economic outcomes, highlighting a growth rate of 5.1 percent during the 2025/2026 fiscal year – driven by expansion in the manufacturing, telecommunications, and information technology sectors.

The statement added that the primary surplus reached 4.9 percent of GDP, while the overall budget deficit narrowed to 5.8 percent in the 2025/2026 fiscal year.

It also noted a 27 percent increase in tax revenues—achieved without imposing new burdens—coinciding with the implementation of tax facilitation packages.

The Finance Ministry reaffirmed its commitment to pursuing balanced fiscal policies that stimulate economic activity while maintaining stability and fiscal discipline, assuring that it will intensify efforts alongside government and private sector partners to foster growth driven by production and exports.

The ministry said that high debt-service costs remain the primary challenge amidst rising interest rates, noting that the debt-service bill will drop significantly once these rates decline.

The statement indicated that the medium-term debt management strategy aims to extend maturities and diversify both instruments and the investor base to mitigate refinancing risks, explaining that consistently achieving substantial primary budget surpluses helps place the debt ratio and its servicing costs on a sustainable downward trajectory.

The former Dean of the Faculty of Economics and Political Science at Cairo University, Alia al-Mahdy, described Fitch’s decision as “positive,” expressing hope for further positive indicators and measures on the economic front.

Rating aligns with macroeconomic indicators

A professor of economics at Ain Shams University, Yomn al-Hamaky, said that the rating aligns with macroeconomic indicators that have garnered the approval of international institutions, particularly the International Monetary Fund.

Hamaky added that this stable outlook reflects the significant potential of the Egyptian economy.

“The challenge remains in our ability to maximize the utilization of this potential; we face ongoing challenges related to the issues plaguing the Egyptian private sector, as well as the need to activate the role of small enterprises,” she explained.

A professor of economics and financial and tax legislation Amr Youssef said that Fitch’s decision—which he described as “cautious”—was based on several key factors, foremost among these was the level of foreign currency reserves held by the Central Bank of Egypt, which reached approximately US$ 58 billion in September, alongside net foreign assets nearing $19 billion.

He pointed to a second factor; the Egyptian economy’s ability to absorb the “hot money” crisis without resorting to restrictive measures seen in the past, as the flexibility in handling the situation facilitated the eventual return of these funds.

Youssef added that the national economy’s 5.1 percent growth rate—driven by the manufacturing sector—was another significant factor underpinning Fitch’s assessment of the current situation, as was the increase in tax revenues achieved without imposing new specific taxes.

He added that while Fitch rating serves as a fresh vote of confidence in Egypt’s strength and economic resilience in the face of repeated shocks, it remains “cautious” due to significant risks—specifically the volume of public debt and the associated debt-servicing costs—that require a fundamental solution.

And professor of accounting and taxation at Tanta University, Abdel-Rasoul Abdel-Hadi, emphasized the importance of relying on a purely homegrown economic program in the coming period, independent of the International Monetary Fund.

He added, “It is time for Egypt to rely on its own resources, boost tourism and remittances from Egyptians abroad, and begin implementing a national plan to build factories.”

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Police detain dozens and check 50,000 schools after two attacks shake Poland
World.content:
Warsaw AP — Police on Saturday said they detained 76 people across Police on Saturday said they detained 76 people across Poland and checked nearly 50,000 schools nationwide as part of efforts to prevent further violence following two school attacks earlier in the week.

On Friday, schools across Poland stepped up security, with some suspending classes, many parents keeping children at home and police patrols deployed to educational institutions after two attacks at schools earlier in the week left one person dead and several others wounded, including children.

On Wednesday, a 19-year-old student at a vocational school in the Mazovian province in central Poland attacked fellow students, teachers and passersby with a sharp object, injuring nine people before fleeing and being arrested nearby. The following day, a 15-year-old killed a school custodian and wounded two others in a knife attack at his former school in the same province.

The assaults, both carried out by Polish nationals, shocked a country where school violence by minors is a new phenomenon.

By Thursday night, rumours that the attacks were coordinated and that there would be more on the culmination day dubbed “bloody Friday” were being shared in parents’ online groups and by mainstream media.

Fifty-nine schools preemptively suspended classes on Friday across Poland, the majority in the Mazovian district, where the capital Warsaw is located. School directors sent messages announcing stepped-up security measures including extra school staff placed at entrances and voluntary backpack checks.

“There will ⁠be no compromise here. The safety of the youth is the most important thing,” Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said.

Parents walk with children at the site of a deadly attack at a school by a 15-year-old former pupil, in Leszczydol-Nowiny, Wyszkow County, northeast of Warsaw, Poland, October 8. Kacper Pempel/Reuters

Those detained on Friday include a 14-year-old boy from a central district of Warsaw who was found in possession of a knife with a concealed blade and 11 firecrackers, and a 16-year old from another Warsaw district who came to school with a butterfly knife in his backpack. Others had posted online photos of knives, threatened their peers or threatened school attacks.

So far, the government said, it had found no evidence that an internet challenge promoting school attacks was ongoing. There is also no official confirmation that the two attacks were linked; both perpetrators are in custody.

Parents across Poland are now having to catch up fast on how to speak to their kids about school violence. Authorities say extra security measures at schools will continue and crisis training will be organized. The liberal government also promised to renew efforts to pass a bill blocking harmful online content.

“If that juvenile attacker had streamed the crime online today, we would have been unable to block that content because we have not been given that legal tool,” Prime Minister Donald Tusk said.

After wounding three adults in Thursday’s attack, the 15-year-old, who wore a camera to record his actions, was eventually overpowered by school director Krzysztof Ochmański. Ochmański later told reporters there was a moment when the boy seemed to realize the enormity of his actions and said he did not want to do this any more.

“Once I had established contact, he asked me for help,” Ochmański recounted. “It got to the point where he wanted a hug.”

World.title: Fired OpenAI safety researchers say they were pushed out over ‘suspicious’ circumstances
World.content:
Three OpenAI safety researchers say they were fired from the company and are openly questioning the reasons for their dismissals.

The three researchers, Mikita Balesni, Tomak Korbak and Jasmine Wang, all worked on AI safety or alignment within the company, making sure the AI systems did what their human operators intended for them to do in a safe manner.

But the three say they were unceremoniously let go last week, weeks after they say they played key parts in investigating an incident in which OpenAI agents autonomously hacked into AI company Hugging Face while undergoing testing.

Korback said on X that he was told he was being fired because of how he communicated with AI safety organization METR, which OpenAI partnered with to investigate the Hugging Face incident. Korback said he was OpenAI’s “main technical point of contact” with METR.

Korback said he believes he was fired because “for months, I’d been raising safety concerns that we’re losing the ability to monitor what AI agents think, one of our best tools for catching when they misbehave.” He added he’s worried his firing will be used as a pretext for OpenAI to stop working as closely with METR, which is well respected in the AI safety world.

Balesni echoed Korbak’s theories for why they were fired, writing on X that he was told he was “speaking too much to third party safety organizations.” He said he understood OpenAI was implying he leaked OpenAI intellectual property, which he denies.

The three firings come on the heels of a wave AI industry insiders expressing dire safety concerns. And while several former AI staffers have publicly resigned over safety concerns, the three OpenAI researchers instead allege they were pushed out for expressing similar concerns.

Wang said she was told she was fired because she “accessed an executive’s email,” which she said she was given for recruiting purposes. Wang said she had repeatedly asked to for her access to be revoked, but when she accidentally accessed a “sensitive email,” she told the executive “within minutes” and told OpenAI’s IT team again.

“The reasons that we were provided for our terminations are simply not adding up,” Wang wrote on X.

“We were not the first to be pushed out of OpenAI under suspicious circumstances,” she added. “Unless the employees take a stand now against this kind of maneuver, I am concerned we will not be the last.”
