Telangana chief minister, A Revanth Reddy on Saturday warned of a looming crisis due to El Nino and directed officials to prepare an action plan to meet the stateâs drinking water, irrigation, agricultural and electricity requirements until June next year.Chief minister Revanth Reddy held a meeting with officials to review the El Nino situation and called for preparations on the lines of those undertaken to tackle the Covid-19 crisis.He said electricity demand was expected to rise further and assured officials that the government was prepared to spend any amount to purchase power if it was unavailable in the market.According to the news agency PTI, emphasising the need for judicious electricity consumption, the chief minister called for steps to temporarily defer works that depend on power, according to an official release.He also directed officials to launch public awareness campaigns on the impact of El Nino through cinema, the media and other platforms.Stressing the need to prevent further disruptions to water supply, chief minister said not even a single drop of water should be wasted.An official release issued on October 9 said the chief minister would meet ministers on October 12 to discuss the stateâs mounting agricultural and supply challenges arising from rainfall deficits linked to El Nino.The state recorded 17 per cent below-normal rainfall during the monsoon season, leaving around 235 mandals facing drought-like conditions, the release said.

World.title: Stage set for Sunday showdown: CJP to march again tomorrow; traffic advisory issued
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has announced another march to Delhiâs Jantar Mantar on Sunday a day after an unprecedented security clampdown and mass detentions thwarted its planned demonstration demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The Delhi Traffic Police has issued an advisory warning commuters of possible disruptions across several key roads and intersections in the national capital.

In a post on X, the CJP said the government feared the consequences of people uniting against it but asserted that the organisation would not back down.

The fresh call for mobilisation comes after more than 7,000 protesters were detained across Delhi on Saturday, according to police sources, cited by news agency PTI.

Those detained included CJP leader Abhijit Dipke, former chief ministers, opposition leaders, student activists, lawyers and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee.

Despite heavy security deployment, barricades and restrictions on movement across central Delhi, some groups of protesters attempted to reach the designated protest site. Incidents of stone-pelting and clashes with security personnel were also reported at multiple locations.





The developments have triggered a sharp political confrontation, with opposition leaders accusing the government of suppressing dissent and the BJP defending the police action. With the CJP announcing another march, authorities have warned that traffic movement could be affected across several parts of the capital on Sunday.

Delhi Traffic Police issues advisory

The Delhi Traffic Police said traffic could be affected on October 11 in view of the prevailing law-and-order situation.

Diversions will be enforced from 6am, depending on the situation on the ground.

Commuters have been advised to account for possible delays while travelling through central Delhi and other affected stretches. The advisory lists 30 intersections, flyovers and road junctions where movement could be disrupted.

The affected locations include:

Jantar Mantar and central Delhi: Ashoka Road-Jantar Mantar Road roundabout, Jai Singh Road-Sansad Marg crossing, Outer Circle Connaught Place-Sansad Marg T-point, Tolstoy-Janpath crossing and Mandi House roundabout.

Connaught Place and adjoining areas: Outer Circle Connaught Place-Barakhamba Road T-point, Chemsford Road-Outer Circle Connaught Place T-point, Guru Nanak Chowk, Jhandewalan roundabout and Panchkuian roundabout.

Key road junctions and flyovers: Dhaula Kuan flyover, Lodhi Road flyover, Moti Bagh flyover, Bhikaji Cama Place underpass, Neela Gumbad roundabout and Sardar Patel Marg-Panchsheel Marg crossing.

Other affected stretches: Shankar Road-Vande Mataram T-point, Windsor Palace roundabout, Rail Bhawan roundabout, Patel Chowk roundabout, RML Hospital roundabout and Minto Road-Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Marg junction.

The police said the diversions would depend on the prevailing circumstances.

Motorists travelling through these areas should check official traffic updates and allow additional time for their journeys.

What happened in Delhi on Saturday?

Delhi witnessed an extensive security operation on Saturday as police moved to prevent the CJP's proposed demonstration. More than 30,000 police and paramilitary personnel were deployed, barricades were erected across Lutyens' Delhi and security checks were intensified at several locations.

Jantar Mantar remained largely deserted as protesters were prevented from reaching the site.

CJP leaders Abhijit Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained inside an aircraft shortly after it landed in Delhi from Mumbai. Rathee was detained from his residence in Gurugram's Sector 56. In a pre-recorded video released after his detention, Dipke said CJP organiser Ajinkya Shinde would lead the protest.

Several opposition leaders were also detained while attempting to join the demonstration.

They included AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan and former Tripura chief minister Manik Sarkar. Left leaders, student activists, lawyers and other protesters were picked up from multiple locations.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Tensions escalated in the afternoon when protesters allegedly hurled stones at security personnel near Akashwani Bhawan and Hanuman Temple in Connaught Place.

Police personnel were injured in the incidents, while officers moved to disperse the crowds and detain those involved.

Opposition leaders condemned the crackdown. Banerjee described the situation as a âSuper Emergencyâ, while Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge accused the government of turning the âmother of democracyâ into a âmuzzled democracyâ. Rahul Gandhi urged young people to continue protesting against what he alleged were attacks on democratic institutions.

World.title: Suvendu eyes Bengal sweep: Can Mamata, Congress unite to challenge BJP?
World.content:
"We are set to win 42 out of 42 in the 2029 Lok Sabha election." West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari had made this grandiose claim even before the Nandigram and Rejinagar bypoll results.

A visibly buoyant Adhikari reiterated the target after his party swept both seats. Victories in both constituencies were expected, yet the margins, particularly in Rejinagar, where roughly 70% of voters are Muslim, came as a revelation. With the all-important Kolkata and Howrah municipal polls likely to be held in late November, there is a perception that the

may win handsomely. It is up to the Opposition to put up a spirited fight.

Bypolls have usually favoured the ruling party

What may give the Opposition some solace is the fact that bypolls, at least over the last decade or so, have followed an extremely predictable pattern in Bengal. Between the 2021 and 2026 Assembly elections, Trinamool won 20 of the 21 Assembly bypolls held in the state. Its dominance was particularly striking in 2024, when it swept all 12 by-elections, including four seats previously held by BJP legislators.

In July 2024, Trinamool wrested Raiganj, Ranaghat Dakshin and Bagdah from the BJP despite the latter's electoral strength in these areas during the Lok Sabha election just weeks earlier.





In November, TMC captured Madarihat, which the BJP had held since 2016. Even in June 2025, less than a year before its Assembly rout, Trinamool retained Kaliganj by more than 50,000 votes.

Suvendu's promise

There have been exceptions to the incumbent's advantage. In 2023,

, supported by the Left, defeated the ruling TMC in Sagardighi by nearly 23,000 votes. However, the MLA concerned, Bayron Biswas, soon joined TMC.

Why BJP's victories still matter

In Nandigram, BJP's Hasi Rani Rath defeated Congress candidate Milan Pradhan, who had Mamata's support, by 1,22,753 votes.

In Rejinagar, BJP's Shankharavh Sarkar defeated Aam Janata Unnayan Party candidate Golam Nabi Azad, son of party founder Humayun Kabir, by more than 75,000 votes.

In both constituencies, BJP polled more votes than all its opponents combined. Rejinagar witnessed notable outreach from the CM, with Suvendu even saying that Muslims did not need to chant "Jai Shri Ram". He also urged them to turn over a new leaf and extend a hand of friendship to the new government.

Following the result, Adhikari attributed BJP's success partly to support from beneficiaries of the Annapurna welfare scheme, under which eligible women receive â¹3,000 per month. Whether the BJP can really secure a share of the Muslim vote in elections with bigger stakes remains to be seen. But if it does, Suvendu's dream of a clean sweep in the Lok Sabha election may well look more realistic.

Allegations of electoral excesses

The Opposition, though, has refused to grant legitimacy to the Assembly bypolls, citing alleged malpractices by the ruling machinery.

Bengal Congress president Subhankar Sarkar demanded fresh elections in both constituencies, alleging booth capturing, intimidation, bogus voting and the forcible removal of polling agents. AJUP, which had won the seat previously, alleged that its candidate received zero votes in 33 booths and just one vote in another 19 booths.

Mamata's TMC faction made similar allegations of rigging, while the rival Trinamool faction and the Left also complained about polling agents being prevented from functioning.

In Nandigram, Congress candidate Milan Pradhan alleged that party agents had been driven out of booths and voters prevented from voting. His earlier arrest in connection with an old case related to the Nandigram land movement had already prompted allegations of political harassment.

BJP supporters in Rejinagar

BJP rejected the rigging allegations, maintaining that polling was peaceful. The Election Commission described voting as largely peaceful despite receiving complaints.

One widely circulated claim that BJP had received more votes than the number of registered voters at a Rejinagar booth was subsequently rebutted by election officials, who said the original electorate figure was incorrect.

Such allegations are not new to Bengal's electoral politics, one of the reasons why the opposition have frequently asked for central forces to conduct polls. The 2018 panchayat elections witnessed widespread reports of violence and intimidation.

More than a third of the seats were won uncontested, overwhelmingly by Trinamool, amid allegations that opposition candidates had been prevented from filing nominations.

A year later, the BJP increased its Lok Sabha tally in Bengal from two seats in 2014 to 18 in 2019.

Political observers have linked that breakthrough partly to resentment over the conduct of the panchayat polls. Very recently, Abhishek Banerjeeâs Diamond Harbour model of winning by record margin of votes had also come under scrutiny.

For BJP though, barely a few months into power, the chances of pushback to any alleged excesses remain relatively modest.

What's next for the Opposition?

The INDIA bloc has upped the ante in the capital, demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged vote manipulation during the SIR process. Leaders such as Rahul Gandhi,

and even those from the Left have been sharing the stage. With a common goal, the confluence is organic. But the state-level dynamics are very different, something that has affected the INDIA alliance for a long time.

An INDIA alliance is unlikely to become a reality in Bengal, with Left and TMC cadres rarely seeing eye to eye. An alliance between Mamata's TMC and Congress remains an open question, with state leaders of the grand old party lukewarm about giving space to a leader who did not allow them much room to grow while in power.

Mamata came to power in 2011 in alliance with Congress, but the two soon parted ways. Since then, the parties have hardly worked together politically, until this by-election.

There have been several overtures from Congress in the past, but these were rebuffed by the then West Bengal CM, who wanted to maximise her political capital. Now that the script has flipped, Congress may not give in so easily.

Former state Congress president Pradip Bhattacharya disclosed in September that the state leadership had advised against a proposed bypoll arrangement under which Congress would contest Nandigram and Mamata's Trinamool would fight Rejinagar.

Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury's recent invitation to Mamata to return to Congress with her remaining MLAs and MPs came with a condition about leaving behind her political baggage, widely interpreted as a reference to Abhishek Banerjee.

Even the Nandigram understanding was not a formal seat-sharing arrangement. Mamata supported Milan Pradhan after her faction's candidate withdrew. In Rejinagar, both parties contested separately.

Many Congress leaders believe that it is time to rebuild the party in the state when opposition space is up for grabs. The BJP is still getting to grips with governance, and teething troubles in several areas, including the rollout of government schemes, have made headlines.

The organisational crisis within Trinamool adds another dimension. Following the Assembly defeat, the party split into rival factions, prompting the Election Commission to temporarily freeze its original name and symbol.

The Mamata-led faction and the Ritabrata Banerjee-led Democratic Trinamool Congress contested under different identities in the bypolls. Neither performed well. In Rejinagar, Mamata's faction received 3,847 votes, while Democratic Trinamool polled 2,044.

Mamata Banerjee's political journey before becoming CM

The Left, meanwhile, continues to face the challenge of translating political visibility into electoral support. Younger leaders such as Satarup Ghosh, Dipshita Dhar and Srijan Bhattacharya have attracted attention, particularly on social media, but the party's electoral recovery remains limited.

There were, however, modest improvements in the latest bypolls. In Nandigram, the CPI's Santi Gopal Giri increased his tally from 2,997 votes in May to 5,779. Congress also improved its vote count in both constituencies, although the Nandigram comparison is complicated by Mamata's support for its candidate.

Municipal elections: The next big battle

The immediate electoral focus now shifts to the Kolkata and Howrah municipal polls, where voting is tentatively expected in late November.

The stakes extend far beyond the two Assembly bypolls.

In the 2021 Kolkata Municipal Corporation election, Trinamool won 134 of 144 wards, securing more than 72% of the votes. BJP won just three wards and Congress two. Interestingly, the Left Front, with nearly 12% of the vote, finished ahead of BJP in vote share despite winning fewer seatst

The forthcoming election will also be fought on a substantially altered map.

Kolkata's wards have increased from 144 to 209, and Howrah's from 50 to 68. For both factions of TMC, this election will be the first major test of who enjoys greater public support. For Mamata Banerjee, south Kolkata remains her pocket borough, and following the humiliating defeat in Bhabanipur, she would be desperate to turn around her fortunes.

For Firhad Hakim and others, it will be an opportunity to prove that they can win on their own without Didi's support.

Congress and the Left have long been marginal forces in both Kolkata and Howrah, barring a few pockets. The Left appears inclined to contest independently in several areas, although the CPM has encouraged local discussions with Congress. Some Congress district leaders, meanwhile, have argued that the party should contest all 209 Kolkata wards on its own.

The decisions are yet to be finalised, leaving Congress with a difficult choice between rebuilding independently, cooperating with the Left and exploring an understanding with Mamata.

Road to 2029

Nationally, Rahul Gandhi's success in rallying different INDIA bloc parties in the campaign demanding the resignation of the CEC has done his popularity no harm. The bonhomie between Sonia Gandhi and Mamata Banerjee at the recent press conference was there for everyone to see. They have maintained cordial personal relations despite the ebbs and flows in their political exchanges. But the political calculations in Bengal remain very different.

Rahul's pointed attacks on Trinamool over corruption during the Assembly campaign had reinforced the Congress's adversarial position in the state. For local Congress workers, a sudden statewide alliance with Mamata would require a significant political adjustment. Didi however, remains in the frontlines in the protest against Election Commission and was detained on Saturday even as Rahul Gandhi skipped the protest and went to Chennai.

Former Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee detained during protest in New Delhi

At the same time, Mamata faces one of the most difficult phases of her political career, while the BJP confronts increasingly coordinated opposition protests at the national level. Hence the political equations could well change. After the municipal elections in Kolkata and Howrah, polls in more than 100 other civic bodies are expected next year, followed by panchayat polls in 2028 and the Lok Sabha election in 2029.

Those who have power in the grassroots are likely to have a headstart in the Lok Sabha election.

Suvendu has already set his sights on winning all 42 Lok Sabha seats in Bengal. Such a result would have significant implications for the BJP's national parliamentary tally. For Congress, the calculation is therefore not confined to the revival of its Bengal organisation. Its leadership must also consider the wider political ramifications of allowing the BJP a free-run in the state.

For the Opposition, national unity over electoral issues is one thing. Building an effective political arrangement in Bengal is quite another. The coming municipal elections will provide the first major opportunity to see whether those differences can be bridged.

World.title: 'Fight should be face-to-face': CM Yogi accepts Akhilesh's Ayodhya challenge
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister

on Saturday accepted

(SP) president

âs challenge to contest the upcoming assembly elections from Ayodhya. Addressing a public meeting in Balrampur, Adityanath invited Yadav to contest against him from the temple town, saying the two leaders should face each other directly.

âAkhilesh ji, Ayodhya is our sacred abode. I visit Ayodhya repeatedly to ensure that there is no lapse in its development, and the identity of Uttar Pradesh is not tarnished in any way. It is a centre of our faith and devotion. We go there not to contest elections, but for its development,â Adityanath said.

âI invite you to file your nomination from Ayodhya, and I will too, and try my luck there once. Let it be decided! The fight should be face-to-face,â he added.

The challenge comes two days after Yadav dared the chief minister to contest from Ayodhya. The SP chief had claimed that the BJP was conducting surveys after his party announced its candidate but had failed to find a suitable nominee for the seat.

Adityanath currently represents the Gorakhpur Urban assembly constituency. The Uttar Pradesh assembly elections are expected to be held early next year.

Yogi targets SP over Ayodhyaâs development

Adityanath also criticised the previous SP government over its handling of Ayodhya.





He alleged that the temple town received only three to four hours of electricity and was littered with heaps of garbage during the partyâs tenure.

He further claimed that the SP government had imposed restrictions on Ramlila performances and erected barricades in the city.

âThe same Ayodhya is today writing a new chapter of development while giving shape to a new concept of Ram Rajya,â he said.

The political exchange comes after the SP won the Faizabad Lok Sabha seat, which covers Ayodhya, in the 2024 general elections.

SP candidate Awadhesh Prasad defeated the BJPâs Lallu Singh.

Yogi accuses SP of dynastic politics

At the Balrampur event, Adityanath accused the SP of misgovernance, protecting criminals and failing to provide employment opportunities to young people.

âThe SP is the party that sold the state and left it in a decrepid condition. That is why I say the real meaning of 'PDA' is 'Pradesh Dubao Alliance' (sink-the-state alliance),â he said.

The chief minister was referring to Yadavâs political slogan, PDA, which stands for pichhde, Dalit and alpsankhyak, or backward classes, Dalits and minorities.

Adityanath also accused the SP of dynastic politics. He alleged that the party had failed to give adequate representation to Dalits and backward communities in its Rajya Sabha nominations.

He claimed that one of the two seats won by the SP had gone to party leader Ram Gopal Yadav, Akhilesh Yadavâs uncle, while the other had been given to a wealthy businessman. The SP also nominated industrialist and sports administrator Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani to the Rajya Sabha.

CM highlights jobs and development

Adityanath also accused successive governments led by the Bahujan Samaj Party and the SP of failing to complete a bridge at Mathura Ghat in Balrampur. He claimed that work progressed only after the BJP came to power.

The chief minister said his government had provided government jobs to 9.5 lakh young people over the past nine-and-a-half years. He also pledged that Balrampur would not be left behind in development.

World.title: Police constable arrested for black-flag protest over daughter’s treatment
World.content:
A head constable attached to the Avadi Tank Factory police station was arrested on Saturday, after he staged a black-flag protest near his residence in Muthapudupet, ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Chennai on Sunday.

The constable, Kothandapani, was detained by Muthapudupet police for questioning. He allegedly staged the protest to draw attention to alleged medical negligence in the treatment of his 10-year-old daughter at the Institute of Child Health and Hospital for Children in Egmore.

Kothandapani, who resides within the Muthapudupet police station limits, had earlier served in the Prohibition Enforcement Wing. He had previously raised allegations of medical negligence against the government hospital over the treatment provided to his daughter.

World.title: Dept. of Posts celebrates National Postal Week  in Chennai
World.content:
The Department of Posts organised a public outreach programme at Nexus Vijaya Mall in Vadapalani on Saturday as part of the National Postal Week celebrations.

A press release said various activities such as ‘Memories with India Post’, drawing and writing contests and photoshoots were held, offering visitors an opportunity to participate in creative and interactive experiences while familiarising themselves with the services and initiatives of the Postal Department.

G. Babu, Additional Director, Chennai City Region, highlighted the initiatives and services of the Postal Department. Lekshmanan Pillai, Senior Superintendent of Post Offices, Chennai City South Division, also participated.

World.title: Goondas Act slapped on couple in Odisha woman murder case
World.content:
The Tambaram City Police have invoked the Goondas Act against Manik Uddin Laskar, 22, a native of Assam, and his wife, Bhagawati Majhi, 21, who were arrested for allegedly murdering and dismembering a 38-year-old woman in Guduvancheri.

The murder of the woman came to light on August 5, when a headless body was found inside an unclaimed suitcase found aboard the Tamil Nadu Express after it reached Agra from Chennai.

After scrutinising CCTV camera footage, the police searched a house on Mosque Street in Guduvancheri, and found human remains inside a large vessel used for preparing biryani.

The victim was identified as Hayathun Nisha, 38, a native of Odisha.

Following the investigation, the police arrested Laskar and Majhi on charges of murdering and dismembering the body of the victim.

Both were subsequently remanded in Central Prison, Puzhal.

World.title: Rahul Gandhi visits Chennai for ‘Voice of Students’ event, meets CM Vijay
World.content:
Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi arrived in Chennai on Saturday to participate in ‘Voice of Students – Chhatron ki Goonj’, a student interaction event that was held at Island Grounds near Marina Beach.

After his arrival, Mr. Gandhi met Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay at his residence on Casuarina Drive, Neelankarai. The Chief Minister hosted Mr. Gandhi for lunch, following which the two leaders visited a café in Palavakkam.

The Voice of Students event was held to provide a platform for young people to voice their concerns on education, employment, and issues affecting their future.

Congress MP Manickam Tagore, in a post on X, said Mr. Gandhi would hear students’ concerns, particularly over unemployment, educational opportunities and what he described as an unfair examination system. He also criticised the BJP and the RSS over their education policies.

Mr. Gandhi’s visit to Chennai comes amid protests by Opposition parties against the SIR exercise.

Demonstrations were held in Delhi on Saturday demanding accountability from the Election Commission over alleged irregularities in the voter-list revision process. The issue has also prompted protests in Chennai.

World.title: Protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls | Full Coverage
World.content:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke on October 3 called for a Jantar Mantar protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls and the Election Commission of India’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.

The CJP has called for criminal action against Mr. Kumar and also demanded his resignation.

Ahead of the large protest, authorities have imposed strict security measures and traffic restrictions across New Delhi, with police personnel and Border Security Force (BSF) jawans deployed at key points.

More than 55 Delhi metro stations have been closed, several rail services reduced and cancelled, citing the likelihood of “unruly crowd movement towards sensitive locations”. Several groups, including the CJP, alleged that protesters were being picked up from across the country.

The Ministry of Home Affairs has approved a temporary Internet suspension and also provided the Delhi Police with additional Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel to strengthen security arrangements.

Security forces started blocking more roads along key routes in New Delhi, such as Janpath and Ashoka Road, on October 10. Police personnel and security forces held debriefing sessions with large numbers of officials who were seen carrying tear gas munitions.

World.title: Udyog Utsav 2026 gets under way
World.content:
The 20th edition of Udyog Utsav 2026, organised by the Avtar Human Capital Trust (AHCT) under its initiative Project Puthri, was held on Saturday.

According to a press release, Project Puthri aims at equipping girls from underserved communities with the skills and exposure needed to pursue higher education and careers. The conference brought together leaders from the education and industry sectors to guide help schoolgirls on career possibilities.

Saundarya Rajesh, Managing Director of Avtar Career Creators Limited and Managing Trustee of Avtar Human Capital Trust, said, “A girl can’t choose a future she has never had the chance to see. For our Puthri scholars, Udyog Utsav is that first glimpse of what could be possible. When they meet professionals and hear about careers, they start to see themselves differently; they begin to believe that the world of work has a place for them too.”

The conference, held at Guru Nanak Educational Society, featured addresses by Remadevi Thotathil, CHRO, Latentview Analytics and K.R. Sriram, vice-president – Head of Automation Corporate IT, Worldline, among others.

The scholars got to visit corporate and institutional stalls, which allowed them to engage directly with organisations and institutions, and learn more about different educational and career pathways.

World.title: Right-wing group members assault protesters amid heavy police presence
World.content:
NEW DELHI

Amid mass detentions ahead of a planned youth-led demonstration on Saturday, a group of right-wing men gathered at Indira Chowk in Connaught Place, chasing and allegedly assaulting protesters demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Security personnel remained deployed in the area to manage the protest against the suspension of the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls as the men shouted slogans and targeted demonstrators.

The gathering took place despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) being in force in the area. Several men, who identified themselves as members of the Hanuman Sena Delhi, were seen heckling, abusing, and slapping demonstrators.

The confrontations unfolded barely 50 metres from where police personnel stood at the entrance to Baba Kharak Singh Marg. Members of the group engaged protesters in physical and verbal altercations, chased them along the inner circle of Connaught Place, and issued threats.

When asked about the lack of intervention, one on-duty officer replied, “We are seeing what can be done.” Another officer declined to comment.

The crowd of about 200 men raised slogans backing the police action — “Delhi Police lath bajao, hum tumhare saath hain” (Delhi Police, use your batons; we are with you) — with some calling for violence against the protesters and Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi.

Videos shared

The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) shared a video showing a young woman being assaulted and knocked to the ground, tagging Union Home Minister Amit Shah to ask who gave the men the right to attack young protesters. “Amit Shah ji, who gave these thugs the right to lay hands on Gen Z? Your these thugs will become the final nail in the coffin of the Modi government’s end, remember that,” the party posted on its official X handle.

In another social media video, a protester was chased and assaulted by a man apparently holding a metal knuckle, sustaining multiple wounds to his back while police personnel stood by. Protesters alleged that, in some instances, police personnel and right-wing members pursued demonstrators together, raising serious questions about the law enforcement response.

Meanwhile, LoP Rahul Gandhi slammed Home Minister Amit Shah and Delhi police. “Amit Shah’s Delhi Police has itself descended into thuggery—and it’s openly giving license and encouragement to the real goons of RSS-BJP to unleash violence on women and youth. As I had said, the more Mogambo Modi and his government suppress, the more the anger of Gen Z and students will swell,” he posted on X.

“On Monday, October 12, Congress, the entire INDIA alliance, and the country’s youth will once again take to the streets in massive numbers. And this time too, the voice will echo across the entire nation—louder than ever before... We are not the ones to get scared. We are not the ones to back down. This fight is not going to stop now!,” Mr. Gandhi added.

World.title: Meeting held to review special bus arrangements for festivals
World.content:
A meeting was held on Saturday to review the arrangements for operating special buses by the Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation for the upcoming holidays on account of Aayudha Puja and Deepavali.

Since many will leave for their home towns to celebrate the festivals, additional special buses will be operated. In the meeting held at the Kalaignar Centenary Bus Terminus in Kilambakkam, discussions were held regarding the operation of special buses, omni buses, basic amenities for passengers, and measures to be taken to prevent traffic congestion. Discussions were also held to create temporary bus stands and identify locations for the parking of additional buses.

A.R. Rahul Nadh, member secretary of the Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority, and Chengalpattu Collector M. Veerappan chaired the meeting.

World.title: Riyadh airport suspends operations after attack leaves several wounded
World.content:
Saudi authorities suspended operations at Riyadh’s international airport on Saturday after a fresh attack there left multiple people wounded.

The Saudi civil aviation authority confirmed an attack had injured several people at the sprawling King Khalid International Airport, with a diplomatic source attributing it to a missile fired by Yemen’s Houthi rebels.

The situation prompted health officials to activate a rare mass call-up of doctors to deal with the “serious emergency”, a medical source said, while foreign embassies warned their citizens to avoid the facility.

Houthis have repeatedly targeted the facility, claiming a series of strikes on Thursday that killed three people and damaged a plane, though they did not announce any new attacks on Saturday.

A witness at the airport reported hearing an explosion while waiting to board a flight, and another said they saw a strike that left people wounded and fleeing in panic.

“I was on gate 403” at the domestic terminal, the witness told AFP. “I saw 401 hit, I saw injured [people] in front of my eyes. Everyone was running.”

A medical source told AFP that the health ministry had ordered ER doctors to report to hospitals around the capital to treat the wounded on Saturday.

“We were told we are dealing with a ‘serious emergency situation’. Injured are being moved to hospitals across Riyadh”, with many in critical condition, the source said.

The aviation authority said the number of injured from the attack was still being assessed, adding that airport “operations had been temporarily suspended pending the completion of an assessment of the damage and verification of the safety of the facilities”.

The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s coalition government unravelled in July.

A source at a local hospital said five people were in intensive care there after being wounded at the airport, with “dozens of people injured” in all.

A relative of one wounded person said they had been hit in the shoulders and arms by shattered glass. Three witnesses confirmed people being evacuated from the airport.

Two doctors told AFP that several pilgrims headed to Makkah had been injured while waiting to board their flight.

A diplomatic source briefed on the matter told AFP the airport was hit by “a missile around 3:00pm” (5pm PKT).

“Houthis are attacking civilian targets. Riyadh airport is a civilian target,” the source said.

Embassy warnings

The Yemen conflict flared back to life after a four-year, UN-brokered truce collapsed, months into a wider Middle Eastern war that has rocked the region and roiled energy supplies and markets.

The scale and frequency of the recent strikes targeting Riyadh are unprecedented in the eight months of war in the region.

Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that supports Yemen’s government militarily, and has found itself drawn deeper into its impoverished neighbour’s civil war.

Both Riyadh and the Houthis have signalled a willingness to keep fighting rather than pursue diplomacy.

The US embassy in Saudi Arabia said it was “aware of attacks” on Riyadh airport on Saturday and called on American citizens to avoid the area.

The Canadian, German and Spanish embassies also warned their citizens to avoid the facility. Spain’s embassy, in a message on X, alerted nationals to a “new attack… by the Houthis”.

A senior Western diplomat told AFP that several embassies “indicated that they had decided to prohibit their staff’s travel to/from Riyadh Airport over the next week as a prudential step”.

Near the airport, passengers carrying luggage could be seen standing on the pavement at a metro station.

Yemen fighting

Meanwhile, in Yemen, Saudi-led government forces were advancing against the Houthis in areas they captured last month around the Bab al-Mandab strait, military sources told AFP.

The Yemeni government last week announced a counter-offensive aimed at retaking all areas held by the Houthis, after the group seized the country’s entire western coastline in a lightning offensive.

The Houthis confirmed that government forces had attacked in the Bab al-Mandab area — a key chokepoint for Red Sea oil and cargo shipping — but they claimed to have repelled the assault.

Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.

World.title: PM Shehbaz meets President Zardari as Centre mulls imposition of emergency in KP
World.content:
Key developments

PM Shehbaz, President Zardari discuss country’s security and political situation

NA, Senate sessions summoned on Tuesday

KP Governor Kundi, Interior Minister Naqvi meet President Zardari

PM and JUI-F chief speak on reducing tensions between Centre, KP govt; two also hold meeting at PM House

Minister calls possible imposition of emergency a “last resort” but says things headed towards “last option”

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday met with President Asif Ali Zardari, with the country’s overall security and political situation coming under discussion as the federal government mulls imposing an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

A statement issued by the President House said the premier was accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Adviser to the PM on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Usman Awan and Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar.

It said that PPP’s Sherry Rehman and Syed Naveed Qamar were also present.

“It was agreed during the meeting to convene separate sessions of the National Assembly and the Senate on Tuesday (Oct 13),” the statement said.

Later, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and Naqvi called on President Zardari in a separate meeting, the President House said.

The president was briefed on the country’s “overall security situation, particularly the worsening law and order situation” in KP. He was also informed about KP’s “security and matters relating to law and order in the country”.

Sharing a video on X, Kundi wrote, “KP has sacrificed enough. Protecting lives and defeating terrorism must take precedence over political interests.”

Earlier in the day, Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam had also met Kundi at Governor House in Peshawar.

The flurry of meetings followed heightened tensions between the PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by the PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre. They have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks.

The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied . It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticises the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

In recent days, federal ministers have assailed the PTI for staging a protest long march , which it has been warned against, at a time when KP faces security challenges. They have also linked differences over the counterterrorism policy with the possibility of an emergency or governor’s rule in KP.

Earlier on Saturday, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar assailed the KP government over a “lack of governance” in the province, alleging that the provincial administration was given Rs700 billion under the National Finance Commission for development projects.

“You did not upgrade the Counter Terrorism Department, did not establish forensic labs, did not install safe city cameras, which should be installed in the merged districts and all the entry-exit points of KP’s districts,” he alleged.

The information minister claimed that the PTI was instead spending this money on organising protests.

Minister says things headed toward ‘last option’

Speaking to Geo News on Saturday, Minister of State for Interior Affairs Tallal Chaudhry said that consultations were ongoing when asked about the imposition of an emergency in KP.

“This is something that requires comprehensive consultations,” he said. “This is not something we are in favour of as we are a democratic government, and this is a last resort.”

Chaudhry added that multiple options were being examined at different levels but questioned what other avenues were available, with the PTI failing to fulfil the federal government’s requests to cooperate in the fight against terrorism, and inciting people and speaking against national policy during the ongoing long march.

“Again, I say consultations are ongoing, and this is a last resort. The options before this, such as talks and backdoor discussions … we tried everything. We will try to make sure we think through this last step if there is no other option, but it looks like things are headed towards the last option,” he stressed.

The state minister added that ties with the PTI remained in place, as they are the opposition in parliament and currently govern KP.

“I previously said that during the second round of talks, the interior minister met the prime minister and told him that the KP government is ready to cooperate in fighting terrorism,” Chaudhry recounted.

“The prime minister told him to give KP whatever they need to fight terrorism on a political level, but they had to gather with us to fight terrorism and stand with our security forces.”

Chaudhry added that the federal government gave the PTI relevance and space, even at the expense of the ruling PML-N’s political goals, and that the government was not focused on politics but on the state and maintaining peace.

“We are ready to give everything and we have no ego. Whether we are in the government or opposition, our ego is Pakistan and it is not bigger than Pakistan,” he emphasised.

“We hoped that we could do this together and on a single platform, but how many martyrs are the prime minister and chief of army staff going to carry on their shoulders? These people [the PTI] are not ready to carry the burden with us or stand with us, so what other option is left?”

PM speaks to Fazl on reducing tensions between Centre, KP govt

Separately, Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam—Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman met PM Shehbaz in Islamabad after the two discussed reducing tensions between the Centre and the KP government during a phone call.

According to a statement from the Prime Minister Office (PMO), the two held consultations on “important national and political matters”.

An earlier statement by the JUI-F confirmed that Fazl had departed for the talks on the “country’s political situation”.

JUI-F spokesperson Aslam Ghauri, in the statement, said Fazl also took the “PTI leadership into confidence” before heading for the meeting with the prime minister.

An earlier statement from the PMO said PM Shehbaz had called the JUI-F chief and congratulated him on performing Umrah and extended an invitation for talks at the Prime Minister House.

The two also discussed reducing tensions between the Centre and the KP government during the phone call, the statement said.

The phone call follows recent contacts between Fazl, known for his engagement with politicians from across the board, and the opposition.

On Tuesday, TTAP leaders called on Fazl at his residence, following which the veteran politician advised the federal government not to obstruct the PTI long march heading towards Islamabad, as protests were a democratic right enjoyed by all political parties.

The next day, PM’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry and National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq met the JUI-F chief.

On Thursday, PTI MNA Junaid Akbar confirmed that Fazl had offered to play a role in ending the deadlock between the government and opposition, adding that the PTI’s “doors are open” to it.

Speaking on Geo News, Akbar had said no framework had been put forward by Fazl regarding his role in the negotiations, although he noted that the JUI-F chief had been in touch with PTI leadership while he was away for Umrah.

The same day, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif also hinted at efforts to restart negotiations between the Centre and the opposition, saying, “I wish a positive result comes out of the efforts of those involved in the talks. But, I have little hope.”

Speaking to Dawn, JUI-F spokesman Aslam Ghauri said his party chief was playing the role of a “facilitator, not a mediator”.

He distinguished the two roles by saying that a mediator would have the authority from opposition parties to make their own decision in light of their demands.

“It is our (JUI-F’s) priority to bring both sides on table for resumption of talks,” he added, pointing out that they had urged the government to call a multi-party conference in Parliament House, where political and security issues should be discussed.

The JUI-F leader said sitting at the table would benefit both sides, though the resumption of dialogue would mostly benefit the PTI because the KP government is “virtually being run by someone else and not by Chief Minister Sohail Afridi”.

World.title: CM Afridi says will not accept 'illegal move' of governor's rule or emergency in KP
World.content:
CHARSADDA/MARDAN: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Saturday said he will not accept any “illegal move”, including the imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency.

The KP CM made the remarks while addressing his supporters in Mardan, where the PTI long march led by him arrived on its seventh day. The federal government, citing differences over the counterterrorism policy, is mulling the option of imposing an emergency or governor’s rule in KP.

Afridi said that if governor’s rule was imposed or any “wrong decision” was taken, the long march would head to Peshawar instead of Swabi, and then move towards D-Chowk in Islamabad.

He urged the public to come out for the release of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, adding that Pakhtuns would not be intimidated by threats, guns or bullets.

The KP CM asserted that arrests and other measures could not demoralise PTI workers. He said that his party would continue its struggle to end the injustices being committed against Imran and secure his release.

Speaking on the occasion, MNA Muhammad Atif Khan contended that Afridi had placed the federal government in a difficult position through his strategy.

The PTI launched the march despite warnings from the Centre after Oct 3 talks with the federal government failed to bridge their differences for multiple reasons , particularly over counterterrorism measures.

The route plan for the march has undergone multiple changes since its launch on Oct 4. While the party initially vowed to march towards Islamabad, its final destination seemingly remains tentative as the KP CM has yet to announce the plan for the trek after Oct 11, beyond Swabi.

So far, the march — being carried out to demand Imran’s release — has remained within KP, where the PTI is in power.

Swabi authorities prepare for PTI march

Meanwhile, containers have been transported to Swabi Interchange and the Indus River bridge on the M-1 Motorway to block the party’s march, but the motorway and the Grand Trunk Road remain open to traffic.

The bridge is particularly significant because it links Punjab and KP, which lie on opposite banks of the river.

Afridi earlier called on PTI supporters across Pakistan to reach the Swabi Interchange on Oct 11 to join his long march.

However, PTI district president Sohail Yousafzai said the convoy would reach Swabi on Oct 12 (Monday), adding that Afridi had directed party workers, lawmakers and office-bearers from across the country to reach Swabi by then.

Echoing a plan announced by Afridi earlier, Yousafzai said that convoys from the Peshawar, Malakand and Kohat regions would reach Swabi Interchange on Oct 13, while those from Hazara, Bannu and Dera Ismail Khan would arrive the next day, when the CM Afridi would announce the next course of action.

The KP chief executive is expected to address party workers at Shewa Adda in Razaar tehsil at 1pm, at the district headquarters at 3pm and at Topi tehsil at 5pm, which shares a boundary with Ghazi in Haripur district.

In a post on X earlier in the day, KP Information Minister Shafi Jan said the convoy will stay overnight in Mardan. He also said the future course of action will be announced on Oct 13 and they will move beyond Swabi.

Refused pressure, Afridi claims

Earlier in the day, the KP CM addressed a large gathering at Farooq-i-Azam Chowk in Charsadda, where he reiterated his opposition to any military operations in the province.

Afridi said he stood firmly with the people and would not accept decisions imposed through pressure or threats.

“I was asked to sign, but I refused,” he said, adding that he would neither retreat from his position under pressure nor compromise on his principles.

Afridi said his position on national security and the Kashmir issue was clear and unequivocal. He noted that important national matters should be addressed on the basis of principles rather than political pressure.

Referring to what he alleged were preparations for a possible military operation, the KP CM reiterated that he would not sign any document under pressure. He claimed attempts had been made to persuade him to agree to certain decisions, but he had declined.

Afridi has repeatedly voiced his opposition to the federal government’s policies on counterterrorism and Afghanistan since he was elected as the KP chief minister in October 2025.

Speaking in Charsadda, the PTI leader stressed the need to protect public rights, democratic values and the people’s mandate, saying public aspirations and ground realities should not be ignored in decision-making. He urged party workers to remain united and maintain discipline in their political struggle.

He referred to the “threats” of the imposition of governor’s rule or emergency, adding that the matter “had gone beyond seats and power” and he was ready to “sacrifice” his seat for Imran and Pakhtuns.

The chief minister highlighted that KP had suffered immense losses in the fight against terrorism, adding that the sacrifices made by its residents should not be forgotten and that their concerns regarding peace, stability and fundamental rights deserved serious attention.

Afridi reiterated he would announce the next plan of action on Oct 13 at the Swabi interchange.

He called on PTI workers to remain united in their struggle for their rights, adding that political differences should be resolved through democratic means and that the voice of the people should be respected.

The KP CM urged party supporters to remain steadfast and vigilant amid the prevailing political situation.

The gathering drew hundreds of PTI supporters to the roundabout, many wearing red caps and chanting slogans in support of Imran. The chief minister addressed the crowd from a container alongside party leaders.

Guidelines issued for police to deal with protests

While the PTI seemed determined to continue with its long march, KP Inspector General Zulfiqar Hameed issued operational guidelines to the police to deal with protests.

The document issued by the police chief, available with Dawn, noted that in “all cases of public protests there is a possibility that miscreants and anti-state elements may use an opportunity to [incite] violence and carry out sabotage activities”.

To prevent such acts, the guidelines were issued in continuation of Operational Guidelines-9/2013 and in light of Sections 83 to 88 of the KP Police Act 2017, for “strict compliance”.

The KP IG directed personnel to exercise “maximum restraint” and avoid the use of force for peaceful protests. “The protesters shall be engaged in negotiations through the senior-most police officer available.”

However, it provided guidelines for a phased use of force to disperse violent protesters. “When it is required to use force as per law, its application shall be of minimum essential standard,” it stated.

The guidelines allowed the use of force to be graduated from the minimum to the “optimum level required” in the following manner:

In the first phase, the violent protesters may clearly be warned against violence before starting use of force. If the need arises after warning them, tear gas shells/grenades shall be used at a safe distance to disperse them

Rubber bullet guns and paper ball guns can be used against violent protesters from a safe distance to disperse them

In the second phase, if the situation requires, violent protesters may be “stopped with baton charge by using the anti-riot gear”. The special unarmed squad will be activated to apprehend violent protesters and take appropriate legal action.

In case of extreme violence and imminent threat to life and property, and when the violent protesters resist dispersal, aerial firing can be conducted by the special armed personnel/squad only with the direction of the senior-most officer present at the occasion.

The guidelines directed personnel to exercise “extreme caution” while using force against protesters to avert damage to life and property.

“Anti-riot squad or the personnel entrusted with use of force shall be properly equipped with anti-riot to avoid damage/casualties to life of all concerned.”

Station house officers (SHOs) were also told to“arrange video-recording, preferably through professional cameramen, of the entire protest/procession”.

The police were directed to seize firearm weapons or any article referred to in Section 86, Sub-Section (1) of the KP Police Act from any person possessing them and take legal action against the individual.

The guidelines issued by the IG said district police officers (DPOs), sub-divisional police officers (SDPOs) and SHOs were to personally attend to all protests in their areas of jurisdiction.

To prevent “unlawful assemblies”, any police officer could temporarily close or regulate any street or public place to prohibit persons or vehicles from entering the area for security reasons under Section 88 of the KP Police Act, 2017.

To prevent “serious disorder, breach of the law or imminent danger to life and property, appropriate use of force will be ordered” by the sub-divisional police officers (SDPOs), SHOs, or the senior-most officer present at the site.

The police strength shall include the following formations:

Anti-riot squad, fully equipped with anti-riot gear and sufficient amount of gas guns and gas shells, properly checked and verified for use by the reserve inspectors/moharrars

Special squads of unarmed men for the purpose of identifying and apprehending miscreants and violent protesters

Plain clothes personnel spread widely to identify and point out violent protesters, miscreants and saboteurs

Armed personnel shall only be deployed at important/suitable points in extremely urgent situations, only for public safety and security under the direct command of DPOs.

SHOs were to specifically ensure deployment of sufficient police strength at vulnerable places, including police stations, government buildings, petrol stations, banks, shopping centres, and major highways and roads.

Police officers were also allowed to stop any procession which violates the conditions of a licence granted under section 84 of the KP Police Act and order it to disperse.

Shortly after the guidelines were issued, the KP information minister alleged that provincial police had withdrawn the security assigned to him and all parliamentarians.

“If any harm comes to me or any parliamentarian, the KP IG will be responsible,” he said.

World.title: Section 144 imposed in Rawalpindi district for a month over 'threat to law and order'
World.content:
The Rawalpindi deputy commissioner on Saturday announced that Section 144 had been imposed in the district for a period of 30 days, over threats to sensitive installations and other critical infrastructure.

Section 144 is a provision in the Code of Criminal Procedure which empowers local authorities to ban public gatherings such as rallies, processions and sit-ins, as well as the open display of weapons.

It has been imposed amid the PTI’s long march, which has so far remained within Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, but had initially announced to move towards the federal capital. The KP chief minister reiterated today that he would lead the convoy towards Islamabad.

According to a notification seen by Dawn, the District Intelligence Committee (DIC) in a meeting today warned the DC of an “imminent threat” within the district to sensitive installations, major roads and other infrastructure “which may pose a serious risk to human life, public property, and the overall peace and order of the district”.

“The DIC has reported specific intelligence suggesting that certain groups and elements are actively mobilising with intentions to disturb the law and order situation through large gatherings, protests, and disruptive assemblies,” the notification read.

Moreover, the committee indicated that these elements may mobilise “individuals with the potential to engage in violent actions” against soft targets and near key installations and other sensitive sites.

Imposing Section 144, DC retired Captain Nadeem Nasir prohibited public gatherings of more than five people, as well as the open display of weapons, improvised explosives, spikes, laden batons, gulails, ball bearings, petrol bombs, or other instruments that could cause physical harm.

It also banned the use of drones and any attempts to “remove any restriction” imposed by the police to regulate assemblies and traffic.

The order is set to expire on Nov 8.

Section 144 has already been imposed in several parts of the country, with Islamabad imposing the provision for two months in a notification dated September 18.

The order prohibited gatherings of five or more people, as well as processions, rallies and demonstrations, at any public place within the revenue limits of the district, including the Red Zone.

Similarly, Section 144 is in force in Lahore until Oct 15, with the order citing serious threats to public peace, tranquillity and the safety of life and property.

According to a notification issued by the Punjab Home Department, a complete ban was imposed on assemblies, processions and gatherings of five or more persons at public places, roads and open spaces.

However, the ban would not apply to wedding ceremonies, funeral prayers, burials, mosques and other places of worship, courts or government institutions.

World.title: Finance minister heads to Bangkok for IMF, World Bank meetings
World.content:
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on Saturday departed for Bangkok for the annual International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group meetings.

In a statement, the finance ministry said Aurangzeb would lead Pakistan’s delegation to the World Bank Group–IMF annual meetings, scheduled to be held from Oct 12 to 18.

Thailand is preparing to host the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, bringing together more than 15,000 participants from 191 countries, including central bank governors, economic policymakers and business leaders, for discussions on the world economy.

“During the visit, the finance minister will represent Pakistan at key events of the IMF and the World Bank Group and undertake an extensive programme of over 60 high-level engagements with international financial institutions, finance ministers and policymakers, development partners, global investors, banks, credit rating agencies, think tanks and international media,” the statement said.

The ministry said the visit came as Pakistan continued its transition from “macroeconomic stabilisation towards sustainable, investment and export-led growth, while advancing structural reforms and strengthening engagement with international capital markets and development partners”.

The statement said Aurangzeb will hold a series of high-level engagements with the leadership of the IMF and World Bank Group, including the International Finance Corporation and the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, focusing on Pakistan’s macroeconomic outlook, reform progress, private sector development and future cooperation.

He will also attend the IMF managing director’s meeting with finance ministers, central bank governors and heads of regional financial institutions of the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan region.

He will also engage with the leadership of major multilateral and development finance institutions, including the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, the Opec Fund for International Development, the Saudi Fund for Development, the International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation, the Japan International Cooperation Agency, the ECO Trade and Development Bank, the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific, and the International Organisation for Migration.

“On the bilateral front, Aurangzeb will hold high-level meetings with counterparts from Saudi Arabia, China, Turkiye, Iran, the United Kingdom and host country Thailand, aimed at strengthening economic, investment, trade and development cooperation. He will also engage with the US Department of the Treasury to further strengthen bilateral economic cooperation and discuss Pakistan’s reform and investment agenda,” the statement said.

The ministry said Aurangzeb will also meet and participate in investment seminars, sovereign investor forums and roundtable discussions with leading international financial institutions.

“These engagements will provide an opportunity to highlight Pakistan’s improving macroeconomic fundamentals, structural reform agenda, international market access and investment potential,” it said.

The minister will engage with Alibaba International Digital Commerce as part of discussions on Pakistan’s digital economy, e-commerce and investment opportunities.

In addition, he will participate in key multilateral forums and will also contribute to high-level policy discussions.

“As part of Pakistan’s international market outreach, the finance minister will hold engagements with all three major global sovereign credit rating agencies, Fitch Ratings, Moody’s and S&P Global, and present Pakistan’s economic and reform trajectory to international investors,” the statement said, adding that he would also engage with leading international media organisations.

“Across these engagements, the finance minister will highlight Pakistan’s progress in restoring macroeconomic stability, strengthening fiscal and external buffers, advancing structural reforms and returning to international capital markets, while setting out the government’s priorities for investment, exports, private sector-led growth, job creation and greater financial inclusion,” it said.

Additional input from Reuters

World.title: PM Shehbaz orders installation of smart scanners at airports
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday ordered the installation of “smart scanners” at all international airports to facilitate travellers, according to a statement from his office.

The premier issued these instructions during a meeting reviewing the customs enforcement in Islamabad, attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Muhammad Ishaq Dar, as well as Federal Ministers Azam Nazeer Tarar, Dr Musadik Malik, Ahad Khan Cheema and Attaullah Tarar.

PM Shehbaz ordered that the scanners be immediately imported and that, once installed, baggage should be screened with the new technology as opposed to being searched manually by customs officials.

According to the statement, he also issued directives for customs officials, saying that passengers must not be harassed through unnecessary questioning at airports.

“The prime minister further stated that outdated procedures for screening passengers’ baggage at airports must be abandoned. Passenger convenience and comfort are the top priority, and no one will be allowed to harass passengers,” the statement read.

The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) added that an “internationally established automated system will be introduced for baggage screening” and that staff providing other services at airports would be trained in line with international standards.

“Courtesy and respect for human dignity in service delivery must be key components of the training,” the statement added.

Commending a new enforcement system introduced by the Customs department, the premier said the initiative deserved appreciation, crediting Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) Chairman Rashid Mahmood Langrial and his team.

He stressed that every possible step must be taken to curb revenue leakage, reiterating a policy of zero tolerance against tax evasion.

“Tax-paying businesses are respectable, while tax evaders will face strict action. We are custodians of the poor man’s money and will protect it at all costs,” he remarked.

Reviewing the customs system, the premier was briefed on the movement of goods and monitoring at various locations nationwide, and the performance of the Customs Enforcement Force and measures to prevent the smuggling of petroleum products.

“The meeting was informed that significant progress had been made in establishing and operationalising Digital Enforcement Stations under Customs Enforcement,” the PMO said, adding that the Indus Collectorate, in its first three weeks of operation, executed 80 operations and seized goods worth approximately Rs205 million.

“A total of 865 personnel had been deployed, covering 26 major transit routes,” it added.

With operations ongoing against smuggled textiles, vehicles, cigarettes and other goods, 280 goods valuers had been recruited and would be trained this month and in November, the statement read.

“The meeting was also informed that, as a result of the FBR’s reforms to prevent smuggling, the customs enforcement system had been consolidated into a single, coordinated organisation operating nationwide,” it added.

World.title: Cristiano Ronaldo provisionally suspended after Portugal walkout
World.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended after the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) announced on Saturday that it had opened disciplinary proceedings against the 41-year-old over his decision to walk out on the national team.

Ronaldo apologised to supporters earlier this week while criticising Portugal coach Jorge Jesus and said he would accept any punishment that was imposed.

“Disciplinary proceedings have been initiated against Cristiano Ronaldo,” said the FPF in a statement, classifying the case as “urgent” and confirming Ronaldo is currently suspended pending a decision on the final punishment.

Ronaldo left Portugal’s Nations League squad after first being made to warm up as a substitute against Norway on September 27 and not brought on, and then finding out he would not start against Denmark in the match on October 1.

The former Real Madrid and Manchester United attacker is the all-time top goalscorer and record appearance-maker in men’s international football.

According to Portuguese media, under the federation’s regulations, a player who misses a training session, a match, or a national team activity faces a suspension ranging from one to six months.

On Tuesday, Ronaldo accused Portugal coach Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time in Nations League matches but said he was not retiring from international duty and would be available to play once any potential punishment was served.

“I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team,” Ronaldo said, while accepting his actions must be “punished” by the federation.

Pele or Maradona

Ronaldo said Jesus had gone back on his word about bringing him on against Norway, and then in a press conference before the Denmark match had not said a series of points they had agreed upon during a conversation beforehand.

One of Ronaldo’s pre-approved talking points was that Jesus had “made a mistake in asking someone of the stature of Pele or Maradona to warm up and then not sending him on in the match.”

Jesus chose not to respond to Ronaldo’s statement when asked about it.

“I read the statement, and now, like I do every day, I’m going to the federation headquarters to work, to think about the Portuguese national team,” said the 72-year-old coach.

Jesus said on last Sunday he would select Ronaldo for international duty if the forward was playing for his club and was interested in being called up.

Portugal won all four of their Nations League matches and qualified for the quarter-finals with two games to spare.

Portugal host Denmark on November 14 and then travel to face Wales on November 17 in their final two Nations League Group A4 matches.

Ronaldo returned to club action on Friday with Saudi Arabian side Al-Nassr and scored as they won 3-0 against Diriyah in a Saudi Pro League match. It was the striker’s 980th career goal.

World.title: Govt assails PTI over 'lack of governance' in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
World.content:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Saturday assailed the PTI-led Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government over a “lack of governance” in the province.

Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, he alleged that the provincial government was given Rs700 billion under the National Finance Commission for development projects.

“You did not upgrade the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD), did not establish forensic labs, did not install safe city cameras, which should be installed in the merged districts and all the entry-exit points of KP’s districts,” he alleged.

On the other hand, the information minister claimed that the PTI was spending this money on organising protests.

“You don’t even give half an hour to discuss terrorism in the province, but you organise six-hour meetings to spread turmoil and vandalism,” he criticised.

Tarar further said that the PTI had “trapped” millions of people in the province to get its leader, former prime minister Imran Khan, released from jail.

“You trapped them in poverty, in disease by not providing the adequate health facilities, in ignorance by not providing educational opportunities, and in non-development by not improving infrastructure,” he said.

Tarar also alleged that the KP government had held the people of the province “captive to terrorists”.

“From the very first day, this is my opinion that they [PTI] are the B-team of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan,” Tarar said.

The information minister said that the PTI facilitated terrorists in settling in the country.

“For how long will it go on? That the security forces will clear the area of terrorists and establish peace, but you will bring the terrorists back?” he asked.

During his address, Tarar said that the PTI government in KP had dragged the province into the “stone age” during the last 13 and a half years.

Citing various federal government projects, Tarar maintained that there was no comparison of the hours spent working by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to address governance issues and take relief and reform measures.

He said that the chief ministers of all the provinces were working hard, questioning how many hours Afridi spent on governance.

“Tell us if you have ever given a big hospital, a university, a highway to your people, an information technology project to the youth of KP or given them laptops or gadgets,” he said.

“How long can such a system, where there is chaos and extremist politics, continue?” he asked.

He claimed that the KP government wanted to hand over the province to terrorists as it prioritised “personal interests over the national interests”.

“This province needs peace, not politics,” Tarar stated.

Asked about imposing an emergency or governor’s rule in KP, Tarar said that responding to this question would be premature.

“Everyone is asking how long KP and its people will remain at the mercy of its government,” he said.

“In my opinion, the conditions in KP have never been worse. They could not be worse than this. What’s worse than terrorists roaming in the streets? You have designated no-go areas in most of your districts because you collect ransom in collusion with terrorists,” he claimed.

He said that the people of KP go to Punjab or other provinces for medical treatment.

“Will there ever come a time when people from across Pakistan go to KP for treatment?” he asked. The information minister asserted that the PTI would not be allowed to destroy the province.

Addressing the same press conference, Coordinator to the Prime Minister on Information for KP Affairs Ikhtiar Wali Khan also questioned the lack of development in the province.

“Universities are shutting down because there are no vice chancellors there. Eighteen out of 34 universities in KP are on the verge of bankruptcy,” he said.

Wali said that people complained about the lack of good roads in Karachi. “But when people of KP go to Karachi, they say that Karachi’s roads are much better than KP.”

Calling on the people and journalists in KP, Wali urged them to talk about the “ground realities”, claiming that the people were crying over the existing health facilities in the province.

He referred to the KP police as the shuhada force, alleging that the provincial government had left them unarmed. He alleged that the PTI government had seized the money allocated to fund the CTD to combat terrorism.

Wali also accused KP ministers of corruption and bad governance in the province.

“The people of KP need peace, health facilities and a political culture based on tolerance, acceptance and respect,” he said.

The PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre — have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy. This was also a key reason behind the breakdown of the Oct 3 talks between them.

The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied. It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticises the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

Kundi, Muqam discuss KP’s security and political situation

In Peshawar, Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit Baltistan Amir Muqam met KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi at Governor House, where they discussed the overall law and order situation in the province.

According to a joint statement issued after the meeting, the two leaders also discussed the PTI’s long march and exchanged views on issues of mutual interest, particularly the political environment in the province.

Kundi and Muqam thanked the people of KP, saying they had rejected the politics of unrest and confrontation.

They reiterated that the federal government would continue taking all possible measures to restore lasting peace, strengthen security and accelerate public welfare and development in the province.

The two leaders also observed that the people of KP had grown frustrated with terrorism and what they described as political elements promoting instability, reaffirming the federal government’s commitment to ensuring peace and stability in the province.

In a post on X, Kundi said, “Our people have paid an unbearable price in the war against terrorism. They cannot be held hostage to the politics of anarchy and agitation.”

He affirmed that the federal government “will continue to take all possible measures to strengthen security, protect our people and support the province’s development”.

“The future of KP cannot be sacrificed at the altar of political ambition,” the governor declared.

“This province does not need any more political stunts that undermine security and endanger lives. I commend the people of KP for standing with peace,” he wrote.

In recent days, federal ministers have assailed the PTI for staging a protest long march, which it has been warned against, at a time when KP faces security challenges. They have also linked differences over the counterterrorism policy with the possibility of an emergency or governor’s rule in KP.

On Friday, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the government had finished deliberating on the imposition of an emergency and warned that it would avail the option if the KP government did not cooperate on counterterrorism.

Gohar meets CM Afridi

On the other hand, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said on X that he met CM Afridi in Peshawar to discuss the country’s political situation, the party’s long march and “other important matters”.

PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, MNA Junaid Akbar, Parliamentary Leader Shahid Kattak and KP Information Minister Shafi Jani were also present during the meeting.

Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Gohar said the imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency was not the right solution to the province’s issues, considering the “circumstances”.

The PTI chairman said there were no conflicting views on eradicating terrorism, but rather on the method of doing so, which could be resolved.

“Those who have taken up swords against the state [and[ those who are enemies of the state are our enemies; if they can be eradicated by imposing governor’s rule or an emergency, we would welcome it, but this would further deteriorate the situation,” Gohar said.

He called on the country’s political leadership to “demonstrate political wisdom” and said a meeting of either the federal or provincial apex committee should be called if any situation required the imposition of governor’s rule.

PTI rejects allegations linking it to terrorists

In a statement issued later in the day, PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram responded to the “outbursts of the so-called ministers and political orphans”.

He rejected allegations linking PTI to armed groups, declaring that the party neither supported armed struggle nor believed in the politics of violence and sabotage.

He said that “daily press conferences by liar-brigade, attacking PTI, were diverting attention from Pakistan’s economic, social and security challenges, lamenting that such useless and harmful pressers consumed valuable media airtime that could otherwise be used for public education, awareness programmes and substantive discussions on issues affecting ordinary citizens”.
